LT 将 Perp DEX 里的永续合约仓位封装成 ERC-20/4626 代币，并由此发展出很多衍生玩法，比如将股票代币的 LT 纳入 Launchpad 的底池 (e.g. @altdotfun @longdotxyz)，成为配对资产

杠杆和仓位由协议机制自动调整，用户无需自己去盯保证金、爆仓价和杠杆倍数；代价则是 管理费 + 赎回费 + rebalance 产生的磨损

@ensembleio 基于 LT 的探索是创新性的。它能将 LT 从简单的 2x 3x 杠杆代币，升级成「观点封装代币」，将结构化策略打包成 token。而这些 token 由于可转移，可交易，又可以被集成到投资组合和更广阔的生态中

Product market fit 主要来自几个方向：
> 使用门槛低。用户只需选择自己的观点，如 多/空/波动率，而无需进行复杂操作（有点像预测市场，只为最终判断负责，而无需对产生该结果的复杂过程过分关注）
> 对 Perp DEX 的天然集成。基于愈发重要的 Perp DEX 构建上层金融应用，为 Perp DEX 增加应用场景
> 可以自由构建，将某个 板块/生态/叙事 纳入到观点交易之中，直接获得强关联的敞口
> 用于对冲。比如长期看多某个标的，但短期由于大盘风险而需要获取下行保护

这类产品真正的价值在于，在用户无感的情况下，将越来越复杂的交易观点和执行过程，封装成一个可以流通的代币。随着 Hyperliquid 影响力的增强，以及 Perp DEX 赛道重要性的持续提升，LT 将会迎来更大的用户群体

text:
Passkeys are the evolution of passwords. When you register in some website, a pair of keys is created (private and public). The private key is stored in the secure enclave of your device, the public key is stored by the platform where you registered. When you want to login, your device decrypts your private key using local biometrics (faceID, fingerprint, etc) and sends a signed message identifying you, the platform verifies it and you are logged in. The advantage with passwords, among others is that passkeys are phishing resistant and that they can not (?) be leaked.
The problem is how passkeys are being used: most people save them in Apple passwords or a password manager, so you have it in the cloud and they can be hacked. Only safe way to use passkeys is storing them inside yubikeys (FIDO2).

text:
今天大家都在讨论 @star_okx 在 OKX NOW 峰会上披露的细节：OKX 上个月支付给大模型公司的 AI 账单，已经飙升到了 1000 万美元。

但单纯看钱是没有意义的，很容易理解成加密大厂在秀肌肉。

看看 AI 到底具体用在哪里了更关键。因为这不仅可能会改变我们未来使用加密产品时的交互，更关乎行业内人的饭碗与钱包。

结合现场演讲全文，可以看到 AI 在头部交易所内部的落地，主要砸在四个具体业务上：

1. 研发流程重构： 内部约 95% 的工程代码合并请求主要走 AI 工作流，开发过程彻底改变，工程师退守至审查、测试和最终批准的环节。

2. 客服具备“状态感知”： 抛弃死板的问答 Bot，AI 能够直接读取用户的账户快照、交易记录、持仓与政策上下文，提供更精准的诊断。

3. 持续的风控信号与合规： 风控从“人工抽检”升级为对数百万个并发信号做 7x24 小时持续分析；同时将全球不同司法管辖区的复杂法规结构化，让跨国合规团队在不同地区执行政策时保持一致。 

4. 私人银行平权： 传统金融里只有高净值客户才配拥有的私人投顾团队，正被做成懂用户资产、现金流与风险偏好的 AI 智能体，让普通散户也能享受到专属财富管理。

基于这些方向，对行业里的普通人与从业者有什么实质影响呢？

小编感受最深的，要数初级职位的大洗牌。

如果真的 95% 的代码提交走 AI，当生产代码变得廉价，机构里最稀缺的，必然是那个能快速看穿 AI 漏洞、敢按下“Approve”并对巨额资金安全兜底的风险审查员。

所以可能的趋势是，初级码农 / 复读机类岗位贬值，有识别能力的“背锅侠”吃香。

此外，利用 AI 顾问去套利成了一种标配。

之前几个版本的加密市场里，在链上找收益，要在数个不同的协议里切来切去，人肉盯盘的手搓感会更重一些。

现在我们总能看到更多的 KOL、P小将甚至是机构都在做自己的数据面板、策展/信号引擎和收益聚合器等等，做出来一个 Vibe 产品的门槛降低了，也成为了一种标配。
但如何用好、用对和拿到结果才是区分水平的关键。

最后，从投资/投机角度看，AI + Crypto ，还是要找那些能为“自动化金融基建”买单的项目。

能帮大资金解决链上合规审查、能帮交易所处理海量并发信号、能跑通智能体自主支付（比如 OKX 此前提出的 Agent 支付协议）的项目，才是未来能真正捕获头部交易所收购或采购需求 + 获得传统金融青睐 + 有叙事/收入流的标的。

交易所是 OKX 的起点，但绝不是终点。

从极客、密码学和早期信仰者，到交易所、ICO、DeFi、稳定币、合规建设，再到今天与传统金融、支付和资产代币化加速融合——Crypto 正在从一场社会实验，成长为全球金融基础设施。

7️⃣ 创新越快，信任与合规越重要

“Trust matters.”

金融最终建立在信任之上。过去十多年，OKX 持续建设合规、审计、治理、风控和机构级基础设施。只有创新与信任并行，Crypto 才能真正进入主流世界。

金融最终建立在信任之上。过去十多年，OKX 持续建设合规、审计、治理、风控和机构级基础设施。只有创新与信任并行，Crypto 才能真正进入主流世界。

quoted_text:
就在今天对于以太坊重要程度仅次于The Merge的Glamsterdam升级将正式完成测试网激活，以太坊也正式将一只脚迈入并行区块链时代。以太坊历史上经历了20次升级，其中最重要的是在2022年的The Merge让以太坊从POW彻底转向了POS，改变了以太坊的经济模型，当然大家对于2024年通过L2扩容的Dencun升级更熟悉，但是随着L2群魔乱舞九子夺嫡以及Vitalik亲自推翻了这一路线，终结了周天子分封天下诸侯的历史，要打造秦王大一统帝国，以太坊主网自己的扩容成了重中之重，而这次Glamsterdam则相当于是给以太坊重新换了一套发动机。

在前些年并行区块链概念被誉为以太坊杀手的核心原因，是包括以太坊在内绝大多数区块链只能A→B→C→D的依次执行交易，所以为了提高性能，只能以牺牲去中心化为代价减少节点数量。

之所以ABCD不能同时跑的原因是因为以太坊的交易之间可能本身就存在一部分依赖关系，节点并不知道几个交易之间是不是可以同时执行，于是只能非常笨重原始的一个个执行。

这次升级引入了EIP-7928名为Block Level Access Lists，简称BAL，它把每一个区块都提前记录到底访问了哪些账户，哪些存储空间，最后变成了什么状态，然后客户端节点就可以提前获知到每一笔交易之间是否存在依赖关系，于是就可以把那些不存在依赖的交易同时执行，而根据历史数据回测，以太坊大约70%的交易都不存在依赖关系。

但是BAL也有一个副作用就是会产生额外的数据传播和存储的成本，所以这次的Glamsterdam是打了一套组合拳，除了BAL外还叠加了ePBS。

EIP-7732名为Enshrined Proposer Builder Separation，简称ePBS，解决了谁负责提出区块、谁又负责构建区块的历史遗留问题，其中Proposer提议者负责决定今天轮到哪个验证者出块，Builder构建者负责从成千上万笔交易里选出来最赚钱的一组放进区块中。

但是这个过程中并没有规定构建者怎么给提议者报价，于是行业自己又搞出来了一大堆角色，包括MEV、中转器等等这些“小商小贩”们来做协调，导致现在一个区块的诞生要经过验证者→MEV→中转器→构建者→执行验证，这里面大量的关系并不属于以太坊共识层本身，以太坊最核心的出块过程中间居然插进来了一大堆协议之外的东西，导致提议者在收到一个区块后必须要在非常短的时间窗口内完成传播、执行和验证。

如果能把这些都塞进以太坊的共识层，就可以延长这个时间窗口不用那么紧张。

ePBS让构建者先提前承诺准备好了出块的资源，然后再给到提议者确认好，这两方达成协议确保这次出块该准备的东西都提前准备好了，那剩下对区块的的传播、执行和验证过程就不需要再手忙脚乱的进行。

所以ePBS可以扩大区块，从而一定程度解决刚才说到的BAL导致数据增长的问题。

总之这次以太坊的Glamsterdam升级，进一步加强了主网的速度和性能，L2们的扩容历史使命也将彻底终结。

$darwin 500m dyor

5VnbrKp28Qs9CAH6PyZdxBNvLxZcbeX3YBsozgWnpump 

okx wallet:https://t.co/G2ACNnZlcS

AI agent compute infrastructure project.

The core is to provide AI agents with intelligent model routing + proprietary GPU fallback + parallel batch processing.

It mainly solves several pain points agents face when actually running tasks: top-tier models can easily hit rate limits or run out of credits, causing tasks to get stuck; simple tasks still being handled by expensive models wastes money; batch workloads can only be processed sequentially, leaving the agent waiting; and without backup compute, the task simply fails.

Darwin is essentially an API placed in front of all the models a user has. It accepts requests in OpenAI or Anthropic format, uses rules to determine the difficulty of the task, and then routes it to the cheapest model in the user’s list that is capable of handling it.

When the budget is running low or a model hits its rate limit, simple requests automatically fall back to cheaper models. When all models are unavailable, the request falls back to Darwin’s own GPU models instead of simply returning an error. It also supports an MCP server, allowing agents to directly call Darwin as a tool.

It does not store users’ prompts or responses. It only records the model, token count, cost, and latency.

It’s basically like an intelligent load balancer + CDN + backup generator in the real world. You connect the agent’s “power meter” to it, and it automatically sends heavy workloads to large models, light workloads to smaller models, switches routes when a model is under capacity constraints, and uses its own generators when everything else is unavailable. The Swarm feature is like handing a pile of individual packages to a parallel processing center: submit them all at once, process them simultaneously, then aggregate and return the results.

The DARWIN token is used through a burn-to-credit mechanism: burning 1 million DARWIN gives you 5 credits. These credits are used to pay for calls to Darwin’s own GPUs and upgrades.

There are no subscriptions or card payments—everything is accounted for purely through on-chain burns.

The official team previously stated that around 52 million tokens had been burned, and that the developer allocation had also been burned. The price went up because Kyle Samani tweeted about the project, while the subsequent decline also happened because Kyle Samani deleted the tweet mentioning Darwin.

主网启动迎来第一段TVL 暴涨，调整了近半年（2023.09-2024.03）才迎来第二段；

第三段到第四段又调整了大半年，2025.10 Base TVL 开始突破 $5B；第四段到第五段调整了近10个月……

再回来看Robinhood Chain，主网上线至今也就3个月，第一段TVL 暴力拉升后才调整了不到1个月的时间。

Today we are open-sourcing Matilda Jev, Australia's first decision model, conditioned for Australian deployment and post-trained with our own specialised recipe. Decision models do not generate text. They answer a typed question and respond with a calibrated probability for each option in a single forward pass, reducing hallucination and making intelligent decisions faster and more efficient.

This release proves that highly capable AI models can be built, post-trained, evaluated, and served entirely within Australia. Post-trained end-to-end on our local infrastructure, the model achieved a median decision latency of 56.8ms on a single @AMD MI355X across 150,317 evaluation requests.

text:
The bridge data changes the interpretation of Ethereum’s $1.09B USDC decline.

If users were simply moving USDC to other chains, CCTP should have been net negative on Ethereum.

Instead, it was +$208M.

The actual gap came from issuer-side activity, where burns exceeded mints by $1.36B.

That makes the latest supply drop much more about redemptions than migration.
author: Covalent_HQ
quoted_text:
$1.09B of USDC left Ethereum this week. The first guess would be that it was bridged elsewhere.

That would make sense. USDC can move between chains through Circle’s CCTP, which burns USDC on one chain and mints it on another.

But the flow data tells a different story.

CCTP actually brought $208M more USDC into Ethereum than it took out this week.

The real outflow came from the issuer side. Authorized minters burned $1.36B more USDC than they minted, with one address accounting for 79% of the burns.

So Ethereum’s biggest USDC decline in 13 weeks wasn’t a cross-chain migration story.

It was a redemption story.

author: JeffLia12309881
quoted_text:
不需要Delta Hedge，用卖期权配合接货、抛货实现比特币本位增长的简便策略：
 
这是一个带 30 日均线过滤的 BTC 7 天 Wheel（轮转）回测，区间为 2023-10-06 至 2026-10-05，本金 1 BTC，不做 Delta 对冲、不计费用。三年下来赚了约 0.33 BTC，年化复利约 10%，主要来自卖 Put 权利金，代价是收益分布极左偏、回撤集中。
 
做法
 
只在现货高于 30 日均线时开仓。规则是卖出 7 天、25 delta 的 Put，名义等于当时全部权益（N = 100% Equity）。
 
Put 到期未被行权：继续下一轮卖 Put。
 
Put 被行权接货：在该指数上持有等量永续多头（相当于按 Put 行权价接货，U=K_put x Size_put），同时备兑卖出 7 天、25 delta 的 Call，张数按 U / K_call 计算，且 Call 行权价不低于 Put 行权价。
 
价格跌破均线触发退出：平掉永续并买回期权，暂停开新轮；价格重新站上均线后再从卖 Put 开始。

Sharp angular jaw, long straight nose, narrow half-lidded eyes, relaxed and unreadable expression. An unlit white cigarette angles down from his lips toward the flame. He wears a loose black tank top and a dark beaded necklace, bare shoulder and collarbone showing. His raised forearm is covered in a fine-line tattoo sleeve, fist resting on the wall, a silver ring on one finger.

On the far left edge, a weathered wall with a worn poster showing cropped bold numerals and fragments of small x86 assembly code text, lit gold where the light hits it. Background is near-black with a few soft out-of-focus city lights in orange and pale white.

Lighting comes almost entirely from the lighter flame. Warm amber and burnt orange glow blooms across her face, his jaw and lips, and the inside of his arm, with strong golden rim light tracing her hair and his profile. Deep crushed black shadows, heavy chiaroscuro, high contrast, limited palette of gold, amber, ochre, rust and black.

我长期高度信任 Binance。这次投入 Solv 的近 50 BTC，本身就是我在 Binance 买入后直接从 Binance 提出，随后进入 SolvBTC/BTC+；我也是通过 Binance Wallet 推送的信息接触到 @SolvProtocol。 整条资金路径都有 Binance 记录和链上记录可以验证。

、$TRUMP 的流动性更是达到 1 亿美元级别。

• 筛选标准：下一个具备这种潜力的标的，初始池子规模至少要是当时主流一级代币平均水平的 10 倍以上。

2. 突发上线与头部做市商深度绑定

• 盘口表现：开局不给大幅度回撤机会，5 分钟 K 线往往呈持续上推的极强走势。

• 运作逻辑：多与顶级做市商（如 Wintermute、Jump Trading、Jane Street 等）完成早期对接。散户往往只有极短的时间窗口获取早期筹码，后续阶段通常转变为博弈上所预期的流动性溢价。

3. 一级虹吸效应驱动主流所被动跟进

• 上所逻辑：交易所本质是“流量与手续费”驱动的商业模式。当代币吸纳了一级市场超过 70% 的资金与注意力时，主流交易所出于手续费竞争考虑，必然加速推进上线流程。 • 落地速度：$BOME 仅用 3 天登陆币安现货，$TRUMP 在第二天即推进衍生品与上线流程。

• 背书效应：Dev（发起方）必须在自身领域拥有顶层声誉与认知度，且必须是其首次发币。

text:
You have Hanuman Ansh inside you.

Hanuman is what? Your prana is Hanuman.

The Upanishads give prana an extraordinary position:

“Prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca.”
- Chandogya Upanishad 5.1.1

Prana is indeed the eldest and the greatest.

Where your prana is flowing is very important. As long as prana is flowing through all organs - and we do have a biological clock for it according to TCM, where you can actually track which organ Hanuman is flying to at a particular time - our Hanuman is facing opposite forces.

Those forces are simply kingdoms of bacteria. Some of them are from the opposite side; you can call them Lanka warriors. And Hanuman needs to guide the monkey army here - you can call them the army of good bacteria - to protect the gut lining and secure the gut-brain axis, so your prana keeps flowing without disruption.

The scriptures obviously don’t call bacteria the Vanara Sena or the gut Lanka. That is our modern metaphor. But the deeper symbolism fits beautifully.

In the Hanuman Chalisa, Hanuman is described as:

“Rāma dūta atulita bala dhāmā.”

The messenger of Rama, the abode of incomparable strength.

That is exactly how I see prana. Hanuman is not the destination. He is the force carrying out Rama’s work.

And who is Rama here?

Your Self.

The Katha Upanishad says:

“Aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmā.”
- Katha Upanishad 1.2.20

The Self is subtler than the subtle and greater than the great.

So when your Hanuman - your prana - is powerful, disciplined, and moving in the right direction, the entire inner army starts working differently.

Your Lanka warriors are challenged. Your Vanara Sena becomes stronger. Your inner communication becomes clearer. Your body becomes the battlefield. Prana becomes Hanuman. And Rama becomes the Self for whom all this work is being done.

And when you are on high prana energy, you just rock anything and everything in life because you get immense clarity, amazing vitality, and the power to take actions that make your life worth living.

That is Hanuman doing the work of Rama.

Prana serving the Self.

text:
早期加密行业一直急于寻找现实应用场景，Travala 就是一个很直观的例子。2020 年以前，手里的币除了交易，还能拿来订酒店和机票。那时候，“支持加密支付”本身，就足以成为一个平台的特色。

其实，BitPay 这类通用加密支付服务早在 2011 年就已经出现。但支付渠道存在，和用户能方便地在日常生活中使用，还是两回事。

几年过去，支付基础设施逐渐追上来了。U 卡让用户能在原本接受银行卡的商户消费，NOWPayments、Heleket 等第三方网关让普通网站也能接入加密收款，Binance Pay 则进一步连接了加密用户与商户。

Stripe 在2024年重启稳定币支付，2025年又与 Shopify、Coinbase 合作，把 USDC 接入传统电商的结账流程。加密支付开始融入已有的商业网络，用户可以继续在熟悉的平台购物，商户也可以照常收取法币。

这些变化，也逐渐体现在真实的消费数据里。根据引用 PaymentScan 数据的报道，2026年7月，其追踪的加密支付卡月消费金额已超过10亿美元，8月约为10.76亿美元。

回头看，Travala 像是这段发展历程中的一个见证。过去，我们需要寻找一个“支持用币付款的平台”；现在，越来越多的支付工具，让我们可以用加密资产购买原本就想买的东西。

区块链一直在往前发展。早期项目曾经引以为特色的功能，随着基础设施成熟，逐渐变成更多商户都能接入的日常服务。曾经急于寻找的现实应用场景，就这样一点点融入了生活。

历史车轮滚滚，Travala 不再引以为傲，进监控列表待下架，Binance Pay 红红火火。

text:
何一姐 @heyibinance，很冒昧向您求助。我现在确实已经没有太多办法了。

我长期高度信任 Binance。这次投入 Solv 的近 50 BTC，本身就是我在 Binance 买入后直接从 Binance 提出，随后进入 SolvBTC/BTC+；我也是通过 Binance Wallet 推送的信息接触到 @SolvProtocol。 整条资金路径都有 Binance 记录和链上记录可以验证。

但这近 50 BTC 对应的资产后来被限制赎回，至今两个多月仍没有明确处理结果。

事件曝光后，Binance 工作人员 Kim 主动联系我了解情况，并通过官方渠道与 Solv 沟通，但换来的仍是一份避重就轻的公开回复。为什么限制、依据什么规则、谁在决定、审核什么时候结束、什么时候能拿回资产，这些最核心的问题至今没有答案。

我尝试了很多渠道，对 Solv 几乎没有实际影响。Binance 是行业领头平台，您也是整个加密行业最有影响力的领头人之一。可能只有您这样的行业影响力出面，才能真正推动他们正视这个问题。 Binance 官方目前也将何一列为联合创始人兼 Co-CEO。

我一直相信去中心化，可现在我连自己资产的自主权都没有。

一个用户能不能知道自己的资产为什么被限制、谁在做决定、依据什么规则、什么时候能够拿回来——这已经不只是我个人的问题，也是整个 Web3 行业需要面对的问题。

希望一姐能够关注此事，推动相关团队要求 Solv 给出一个公开、明确、可验证的处理结果。

万分感谢。

何一姐 @heyibinance，很冒昧向您求助。我现在确实已经没有太多办法了。

我长期高度信任 Binance。这次投入 Solv 的近 50 BTC，本身就是我在 Binance 买入后直接从 Binance 提出，随后进入 SolvBTC/BTC+；我也是通过 Binance Wallet 推送的信息接触到 @SolvProtocol。 整条资金路径都有 Binance 记录和链上记录可以验证。

但这近 50 BTC 对应的资产后来被限制赎回，至今两个多月仍没有明确处理结果。

事件曝光后，Binance 工作人员 Kim 主动联系我了解情况，并通过官方渠道与 Solv 沟通，但换来的仍是一份避重就轻的公开回复。为什么限制、依据什么规则、谁在决定、审核什么时候结束、什么时候能拿回资产，这些最核心的问题至今没有答案。

我尝试了很多渠道，对 Solv 几乎没有实际影响。Binance 是行业领头平台，您也是整个加密行业最有影响力的领头人之一。可能只有您这样的行业影响力出面，才能真正推动他们正视这个问题。 Binance 官方目前也将何一列为联合创始人兼 Co-CEO。

text:
沉默与退让的背后暗藏地缘危机，《麦加共同防御协议》进入实质性执行阶段！

本周前两天在美伊局势上是难得的沉默，在伊朗议长提高海峡恢复要求后美国并没有太多实质性的外交回应

甚至在伊朗高调威胁报复之后美国撤走了英国军事基地的轰炸机，出现少见的退让举动。

但是我认为这种短期的退让与沉默并不是什么好事，甚至可以说暗藏更高的地缘风险！

美国财政部提高了对伊朗经济金融制裁的手段，将原本的金融二级制裁升级为“可随时、无需预先通知”的阶段，这意味着外国银行如果涉及到伊朗资金，将会被美国在没有提前通知的前提下进行制裁，大大的威胁到伊朗的海外资金流动性能力

另一方面， Kpler 数据显示，9月份伊朗石油出口已经降低至零，与此同时沙特、阿联酋、伊拉克方面通过关闭AIS定位大量输出原油

结合目前整体的情况来看，美国外交与军事上不作出回应，但是在金融与经济制裁上继续施加压力，彻底断掉伊朗对外能源输出以及资金回流的能力，以经济战拖垮伊朗

而特朗普显然也不是会对伊朗退让，此时的沉默更像是叙事待发，距离中期选举还有不到1个月的时间，这个期间伊朗继续承受美国的经济与金融制裁，内部矛盾摩擦越来越大，同时特朗普目前的表现很有可能在中期选举后对伊朗实施新一轮军事打击。

所以，此时美国的沉默与军事调动上的轻微退让反而是未来地缘风险进一步扩大的迹象之一

至于Brent 价格走势，目前虽然处于下跌阶段，但是跌幅较慢，核心是能源供给侧出现缓和，同时美伊方面并未出现新的外交摩擦，导致原油价格回落，但是市场对于地缘风险的定价还并未结束，这就导致Brent 出现震荡下跌的走势

如果后续事态真的按照我的预期来走，起码未来1个月Brent 会走一个缓慢的震荡下跌过程，而且Brent 不跌破95对风险市场的压制还是会很明显，作为投资者的我们则需要继续承受这种折磨，直到11月3日中期大选结束，特朗普一旦对伊朗发动大规模打击，油价会进一步反弹！

PS：沙特、巴基斯坦与土耳其的《麦加共同防御协议》进入执行阶段，土耳其与巴基斯坦表示将会尽快向沙特部署军事力量，以对抗胡塞武装对沙特的袭击，中东地缘风险明显外溢，一旦特朗普恢复对伊朗的打击，中东战局会更乱！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
中东原油出口水平已经超过战前水平？那么Brent 市场为何定价还是居高不下？美伊沉默之下市场已经做出悲观定价！

根据路透社援引油轮检测机构 Kpler的数据，9月最后一周中有4天的原有输出已经超过战前水平，恢复至1950-2259万桶/日，但是为何Brent定价还是这么高？

正如我前文宏观指引中提到的一样，原有定价有三层因素，即市场基本供应+资本市场定价+地缘局势

那么很容易就得出结论，当原油供应无法改善Brent价格时候，就是资本对目前的地缘局势感到悲观从而导致定价如此之高，目前Brent 报价102.5美元

市场悲观的因素有哪些？

this is actually a big deal for the L2 thesis

today cross-chain usually means:

L1 -> bridge -> wait -> L2 -> another transaction

different steps, different states, different failure points

what EEZ just demonstrated is atomic synchronous composability

L1 + L2 acting as one logical transaction

either everything executes or nothing does

if this scales, L2s stop feeling like isolated islands and start behaving more like one connected execution environment around Ethereum

that matters a lot for the next phase of L2 adoption

and it fits very well with what Linea and Lineth are trying to build around public and institutional Ethereum infrastructure

not a $LINEA announcement by itself

but definitely the kind of tech that makes the bigger thesis more interesting

text:
Imagine a price comparison site that makes money only when it finds you a cheaper deal than you could find yourself. It just added NEAR, and called it one of the best routes it has.

The site is called RIFT. It is backed by Paradigm, one of the biggest crypto funds. You tell it what you want to swap, it asks 20+ exchanges and bridges for a price, and sends your order to whoever is cheapest at that second. Zero added fee. If it cannot beat what you would get on your own, it earns nothing.

That business model has one consequence. RIFT has no reason to like any venue. It only cares which one wins the price check, order after order. Uniswap is in the pool. Across, Relay, LI. FI are in the pool. Now NEAR Intents is in the pool, and RIFT said why: it is consistently one of the best cross chain routes.

There is no sponsorship deal that gets you onto a price comparison site. You get there by being cheap enough, often enough, that leaving you out costs them money.

Second Ethereum DeFi team to route through NEAR this week, after Infinex. The pattern is not that near:native is signing partners. It is that the people whose job is to find the best price keep landing on the same answer.

有一个最近越来越多被提到的指标是“市场广度”。

市场广度——一个经济周期中非常值得关注的指标。指数涨而绝大多数成分股不涨，被视为“广度变窄”；反之，大部分股票一起上涨就是“广度宽”。

而9月的反弹行情中，广度在变差。
标普500站上50日均线比例约为25%，也就是说这一轮上涨，并非多数股票都参与到了。如果以行业来说的话，只有科技行业上涨。

10月初有初步反弹迹象，但不足以说广度反转。

author: nft_hu
quoted_text:
在过去一段时间里，市场的波动都高度集中在一小撮股票里。不知道大家有没有经历过，指数上涨与你的持仓脱节的时期。

过去半年，市场行情越来越“窄”：
指数创新高，主力资金却几乎只挤在同一条车道——AI、半导体、少数巨头权重。
其他板块，要么横盘、要么阴跌，偶尔跟涨一两天又很快掉队。表面上是繁荣，底层却是参与度不断收缩。

这就是所谓的 breadth narrowing：“市场的涨跌高度集中在少数股票里”，任何对这些核心资产的冲击，都可能瞬间演变成对整个“牛市”的冲击。

什么是breadth narrowing（市场广度缩小）？
指的是：上涨主要由少数权重或主题股驱动，而多数股票并没有跟涨，甚至在走弱。他描述的是行情参与度在收缩。

市场广度（Market Breadth），一个经济周期中非常值得关注的指标。指数涨而绝大多数成分股不涨，被视为“广度变窄”；反之，大部分股票一起上涨就是“广度宽”。

breadth narrowing 效应：说明指数从“广泛参与”演变为“集中于一个主题或少数风格”，例如当下经常被提到的“只靠少数 AI 半导体巨头抬指数”。
这种收窄既可能是健康的资金集中（机构挤在最强赛道），也可能是周期末端的疲态信号（其他板块普遍见顶、筹码出清）。

如果用这个视角打开最近的行情，市场其实变得更加健康了：资金从存储板块流出，流入医药、消费、软件、mag7，市场广度增加。行情从“窄而强”转向“宽而强”，牛市进入中后段的轮动期。

text:
Claude Code tip: stop letting agent teammates mark tasks done that Opus 5.5 has to redo, while Fable 5.1 sits idle

load quality gates for the whole team with --settings

claude --model opus --settings .claude/team-gates.json

Opus 5.5 acts as the lead, writing the shared task list and only reading work that passed the gates

Sonnet 5.5 teammates claim tasks from the list and can't close one until the gate lets them

Fable 5.1 sits on the team as a dedicated adversary, and three hooks decide when work gets pushed back:

→ TaskCreated: does this task name the test that proves it? exit 2 sends it back
→ TaskCompleted: does that test pass right now? exit 2 keeps the task open
→ TeammateIdle: is unblocked work still waiting? exit 2 puts the teammate back to work

Sonnet 5.5 builds. Fable 5.1 challenges. Opus 5.5 merges and ships

Jev engineering runs the identical pattern one layer down: mechanical decisions that need no reasoning (which file to open, which tool to invoke, retry or abort) execute in 16ms, so the frontier models only wake up when execution paths actually diverge

Lead on Opus. Gate every task. Keep the adversary on call.

- the full team setup
> Opus 5.5 on high leads and writes the shared task list
> ux, backend and tests teammates on Sonnet 5.5 claim tasks, file locking stops double claims
> TaskCreated rejects any task without a test command
> TaskCompleted runs that command and blocks "done" on a failure
> TeammateIdle hands idle teammates the next unblocked task
> adversary on Fable 5.1 reviews each task before the lead synthesizes

paste the setup and this prompt into Claude Code below:

"Configure my Claude Code workspace for a gated agent team:

1. Create .claude/team-gates.json:
> env CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1
> a TaskCreated hook that exits 2 when a task description has no test command
> a TaskCompleted hook that runs that test command and exits 2 with the failure output
> a TeammateIdle hook that exits 2 while unblocked tasks remain

2. Write each hook script in .claude/hooks/, then dry-run every one against a fake event payload and show me the output

3. Create .claude/agents/adversary.md with model: fable and tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash

4. Add a team rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: every task description names its test command, and the adversary reviews each task before the lead synthesizes

Show every configuration diff first. Do not apply edits until confirmed"

It's been a hard month for privacy and your right to use crypto. There's a bright spot. 

Two rules at Treasury that Coin Center has vehemently opposed over the last several years have been officially withdrawn. 

The "unhosted wallet rule" that would have made Coinbase and others collect information on people who are holding their own crypto is dead.

This is good news and I'm happy that our work for several years to characterize these rules as bad policy and probably unconstistitutional has born fruit. 

That said, the underlying statutory authority to create new, similar bad rules remains. Our work is not done and won't be until we truly protect self-custody and legitimate privacy tools in law via Congress or the Courts.

text:
on airdrops and why they are less frequent:

first, airdrops are *the* single best community building tool crypto has ever created

you tease an airdrop to acquire users, then turn a percentage of them into actual supporters because they become financially + emotionally tied to the success of the product and most importantly, you put the asset directly in their hands

best growth hack, no debate on this

but the pre token phase is also basically easy mode for teams

users are willing to pay (high) fees, deposit capital, generate volume and juice every metric imaginable for the possibility of an allocation

you are basically getting paid to bootstrap your product

the problem is that this model has been abused to death

there are well over 20 teams still farming airdrop farmers after extracting $100m+ from them, while knowing perfectly well they will never launch a token because launching a token now comes with expectations they cant meet

people want revenue
people want buybacks
people want a fair distribution
people want the token to actually capture value

how many pre token products in crypto can deliver all of that today? 10? maybe less?

so you end up with a weird equilibrium

(i) the pre token phase is extremely profitable and low risk
(ii) the post token phase forces you to prove that your product is actually viable and that there is enough value creation to sustain a token

this is why you are getting fewer airdrops and fewer TGEs

tldr: airdrops are disappearing because they worked too well while the bar for launching a good token became much higher

less TGEs is the natural outcome

今天 OKX 全球大会上 @star_okx 的开场演讲，释放了一个非常明确且信号量极大的趋势：交易所只是起点，而不是终局。

加密与 TradFi 的界限正在加速消失，下一代金融科技平台正在形成。

整理了几个核心 Takeaways，值得所有 Web3 与 FinTech 从业者深思：

1️⃣ 行业周期与 OKX 的定位蜕变

从 2008 极客实验到 DeFi 爆发，再到 2022-2024 的全球合规构建，2025 年往后加密货币正加速迈入“主流化阶段”。简单将 OKX 定义为加密交易所已经不够了，它的终局是全球金融科技平台。

2️⃣ 下一代金融服务的四大支柱（Hold, Pay, Invest, Grow） 未来的年轻人可能不会再走入传统银行网点开户。OKX 给出的长期愿景非常清晰：

• Hold（存储）：自主选择受监管交易所、自托管钱包或数字银行。
• Pay（支付）：像发消息一样跨国即时转账，极低成本。
• Invest（投资）：Crypto、美股、大宗商品融入统一体验。
• Grow（增值）：AI 赋能，让普通人拥有专属的“私人银行顾问”。

3️⃣ Crypto vs TradFi？不，是“合二为一”

现在早已不是加密对抗传统金融的时代，ICE（NYSE 母公司）、渣打银行、Circle 等主流机构入局，证明两者正走向融合。Crypto 提供 7x24 不间断基础设施与可编程货币，TradFi 提供庞大流动性与机构信任。

4️⃣ AI 不再是 PPT 概念，而是核心基础设施

最令人震撼的是 OKX 内部对 AI 的应用深度：

• 内部构建了 AI 平台“Oli”。
•工程团队 95% 的代码 PRs 由 AI 工作流完成。
•单月 API / 模型账单高达 1,000 万美元！ AI 正在深度重塑其工程、风控、智能客服与全球合规体系。

总结： 互联网实现了信息的全球化，加密技术实现了价值的全球化，而 AI 正在实现智能的全球化与个性化。三者的融合，就是下一代金融体系的模样。

Timo Keller and I have posted our resolution of questions of Venkatesh, Bost–Charles, Frey–Kani–Völklein, and going all the way back to Ihara: https://t.co/LVe2JFcueD. We construct Golod–Shafarevich towers in dimension 2, i.e. infinite (geometric) unramified towers of arithmetic surfaces.

The general vibe was that such surfaces should not exist. Timo and I laid out our program to construct them back in 2022: that is more or less the first half of the proof. This summer, helped by a little army of AI agents, we managed to finish the climb: we used GPT 5.6 Sol, Fable and Aletheia internally at Google DeepMind. The experience is described in some detail in Section 1.4 on page 5: it has been by far the most exciting human-AI collaboration that I have personally taken part to, so far.

Simultaneously and independently, Pablo Chenal has also settled the questions of Bost–Charles, and consequently Frey–Kani–Völklein: https://t.co/4OryNqvufz. Pablo gives a much shorter and more elegant existence proof, while our approach is heavier but makes the surfaces explicit. Pablo, Timo and I are currently working towards a unified perspective and merging the two works into one.

I have been dreaming of finding such a surface since 2022, and it is truly exciting to be able to finally share it!

Grok Imagine: 

1990s cel-animated anime film still, extreme low-angle shot from the ground in front of a drum kit, looking up at a furious pink-haired magical girl drummer mid-performance, an enormous burning red sun filling the entire sky behind her. Wide-angle lens distortion makes the drums loom huge in the foreground.

The drummer sits dead center behind the kit, leaning forward into the strike. Pastel pink hair styled in two round buns on top of her head with long thin twin tails whipping outward to both sides in violent wind, loose strands flying. Straight blunt bangs with a small gold crescent moon mark on her forehead. Her eyes are solid glowing rectangles of hot pink-red light with no pupils, brows slammed down in rage, mouth wide open in a full scream showing teeth and tongue. Skin tinted warm tan by the red light. She wears a white short-sleeved sailor uniform top with a wide sailor collar trimmed in pink stripes, a large pink bow on the chest pinned with a round gold crescent brooch, a pink pleated skirt, and a worn brown leather belt with heavy metal buckles. Thick rusted iron chains are wrapped tight around both wrists and forearms, broken links swinging loose in the air. Her right arm is thrown straight up overhead gripping a wooden drumstick, her left arm is cocked across her body with the second stick about to crash down.

The drum kit is battered and massive. Two large bass drums sit side by side at the bottom of the frame, each with a cracked off-white drumhead painted with a dark red crescent emblem. Two rack toms tilt toward the camera above them, a snare drum sits in the center. All shells are scuffed black with scratches, rust streaks and dented finish, wrapped in tarnished chrome hoops, lugs, tension rods and clamps drawn in obsessive mechanical detail. Dark bronze cymbals hang at steep angles on both sides of the frame on heavy stands with wing nuts and boom arms, plus a hi-hat on the right. Chunks of broken pale concrete and stone rubble are piled in the immediate foreground around the base of the kit.

Behind her, a colossal crimson sun dominates the frame, its surface mottled and boiling in deep red and salmon tones, ringed by a thick blazing corona of orange and yellow fire that licks outward into a dull ash-grey sky. Sparks and specks of ember drift through the air.

Lighting is harsh backlight from the sun, casting the drummer and kit in red-tinted shadow with glowing orange rim light along her hair, arms, cymbal edges and drum hoops. The only front light is the glow from her eyes. Limited palette of crimson, salmon, burnt orange, bone white, dusty pink, rust brown and black.

Hand-drawn cel animation look, dense gritty ink linework, heavy hatching and texture on metal and stone, flat cel shading with hard shadow shapes, retro 90s OVA aesthetic, dark fantasy and heavy metal album cover energy, post-apocalyptic mood, subtle film grain, slight analog softness, dynamic action composition, hyper-detailed.

quoted_text:
TLDR of @papertrade_xyz: 

nothing like this exists in a crypto; it is truly a brand new primitive

it is modeled after "bucket shops" that were popular in the early 1900s. They were gambling dens were you could wager on stock price movements without actually buying or selling the underlying. The house would always take the exact other side of your bet

This is exactly how papertrade operates. When you place a trade, the house (aka papertrade LP) takes the otherside of your trade. There is no orderbook; the trade is exactly executed at the HL oracle mid price

Now where does the LP funds from?
Incredibly, the LP starts at 0 - no one prefunds it. The LP counts on the skill of the average trader being poor and thus in aggregate a losing position. A fee is skimmed off the top of winning trades (none from losing) to also skew the LP positive

What if the LP doesn't have sufficient funds?
Then traders owed $ are placed into a queue where they're paid out in FIFO order. Traders have to lose to payout traders who won.

$Paper Tokenomics 🧻:
Here is the very cool part - you can only earn their token by losing trades. And the emissions increase when the LP has < $2M, to encourage people to lose to backstop a dwindling LP

And then staking paper earns you the fees and profits that the papertrade LP earns.

Incredibly interesting experiment built by @izebel_eth. Best of luck on the launch! A ton of eyes on this and a lot of people who want to farm $PAPER

text:
Sixth question on AI.
Does AI need to be a zero-sum race between the US and China?
Many influential voices in tech as well as the current administration argue that it does. (See, for example, https://t.co/63jNKZIGON, https://t.co/82WRjDEklx, https://t.co/3isNlCWI2U and this from the White House, https://t.co/roDrwiWjIj).

There are many aspects of these arguments, but I would like to focus on three that have received less attention than they deserve.

The first aspect is that this framing typically assumes that there is a single direction of progress for AI, and the US and China are racing along this dimension toward superintelligence or at the very least some sort of powerful AI that will confer huge military and strategic advantages to the winner. If, on the other hand, the US and China are developing these technologies in different directions, there is much more room for coordination and even for each country learning from the other’s best practices.

My reading of the evidence is that there are huge differences in the American and Chinese approaches. The US is focused on foundation models, such as frontier large language models. China is also investing – and arguably catching up – in these models, but there is much greater emphasis in China on applications of AI (with the government setting targets for the spread of AI across industries, https://t.co/1yimDjGmzK).

This reflects several factors, in my assessment. First, Chinese AI investments started with government demands for surveillance technologies and government-supplied data to AI companies (e.g., https://t.co/GXWDWukQty). Second, China is facing a huge demographic transformation, which will create scarcity of labor in the near future. This encourages companies to integrate robotics and AI much more actively into the production process (and China accounts for 59% of all robot installations in the world, https://t.co/YQjXLWZwrs). Third, applications and integration of these technologies into the production process requires a lot of engineering. China has a large and very well-trained supply of engineers (whereas the US has far fewer engineers and a lot of engineering talent is currently going to Silicon Valley, which hasn’t focused on applications). Fourth, China was relatively late in catching the “artificial general intelligence,” AGI, bug, although now there is more emphasis on this in China as well.

Whatever the exact causes, this difference in approach implies that there is plenty for the US to learn from China as well as the other way around.

The second aspect is that the zero-sum framing ignores or downplays the crucial need for global coordination. This framing claims that the strategic and military advantage that powerful AI will create is all that matters. But the race to AGI also poses huge risks (and this is true regardless of whether this race is truly advancing toward superintelligence or just producing distorted intelligence, as I argued in my first post in this series). And these risks are global. If the US and China are racing toward AGI with no guardrails and coordination, even the follower (probably China) will have models capable of creating havoc. In this case, racing without any global coordination is a recipe for disaster.
The third aspect of the problem is that this framing narrows the scope for any kind of coordination on other global issues between the US and China – including climate change, pandemics, nuclear nonproliferation and world peace. Tellingly, climate cooperation between the US and China has now largely stalled).

Let me add that I’m saying all of this not as an admirer of the Chinese system. On the contrary, I have been a vocal critic of both the Chinese Communist Party and the Chinese development strategy since Why Nations Fail (https://t.co/NMlp4VprG7) and I have argued that the Chinese success has some of its roots in severe labor repression (https://t.co/14SDaw2Y8H).

Indeed, this argument does not ignore the fact that China has an authoritarian, repressive regime, and it is using AI for surveillance and to stamp out dissent. Global coordination and efforts to set up reasonable rules that apply to all parties do not require the counterparty to be fully democratic or ruled by angels. In fact, sometimes it is more important to set up such a global framework when dealing with dangerous adversaries (as the arms-control treaties that the US and the Soviets signed demonstrate).

In sum, my assessment is that it is a colossal mistake to frame the AI race as a zero-sum one between the US and China. It poisons the much-needed dialogue and coordination between the US and China on broader issues; it makes the AI race more reckless; and it discourages the building of reasonable guardrails and regulations.

The last point is particularly relevant, and makes me sometimes say: if China did not exist, Silicon Valley would have to invent it.

text: The rumor I referenced earlier.
author: AndrewCurran_
quoted_text:
So, it seems OpenAI is about to release something like 400 AI-generated proofs on a public server.

To the best of my understanding, people are still trying to figure out how the forced Navier–Stokes example actually works. I know of several experts who are studying it, and it is definitely not an easy task.

Until mathematicians digest that example, however, its impact on mathematics as a living subject seems necessarily limited. What questions does it open? What new ideas does it suggest? What does it teach us about fluids, beyond the yes/no information contained in the theorem itself?

Mathematics does not grow simply by accumulating correct statements. Results have to be understood, connected, explained, challenged, reused. Until that happens, they risk remaining lettera morta.

Now imagine adding 400 more AI-generated proofs. For each of them, until some human mathematician picks it up, studies it, and connects it to the existing mathematical culture, isn't it in essentially the same position?

So my question is genuinely: what is the intended mathematical value of releasing hundreds of proofs at once? What happens if there simply aren't enough people willing or able to read them?

To be clear, I think mathematicians should discover mathematics by any means necessary, including scavenging through artificial, alien-looking mathematical material, since there may be extraordinary things to find there.

But humans are not machines, as attention, understanding, taste, and mathematical culture are scarce resources.

What happens if the rate at which mathematics is generated becomes much greater than the rate at which mathematicians can absorb it?

text:
Sepolia testnet validators: update your nodes.

Today at ~4pm, we’ll see Glamsterdam (Gloas + Amsterdam) go live on Sepolia.

This marks a major milestone for Glamsterdam and for Ethereum more broadly.

Glamsterdam’s main focus has been scaling, but at the same time the fork also reduces trust requirements, improves sync, and harmonizes resource pricing to improve DoS resistance as the chain scales.

It will likely be the largest Ethereum fork since the Merge, and it has been ambitious from the beginning.

ePBS and BALs were selected as headliners early on, and the fork’s theme - scaling - evolved quite naturally from there. When core devs later decided to reprice the EVM as well, the fork’s surface area increased quite a lot and Glamsterdam became a much broader upgrade than initially expected.

That also meant more work across specs, clients, tooling, and testing. Almost a year of benchmarking, implementation work, refining specs, testing and devnets followed, and over time Glamsterdam has really started to harden.

It has also been the first fork where AI played a major role across basically the whole pipeline: research, benchmarking, testing, client implementations, and security audits, which is interesting to witness. 
One can clearly feel the accelerated pace at the frontlines: while Sepolia is forking to Glamsterdam, core devs are already busy shipping the first Hegota devnets.

Ethereum is not yet where it needs to be, but we’re getting there. Fork after fork, the chain becomes more scalable, more robust, and more capable.

And with post-quantum security likely becoming one of the main focus areas over the next few years, there is still a lot ahead.

text:
Lets be honest everyone is now using Claude and ChatGPT.

But if you code, you should use Claude Code or Codex.

Here are 10 GitHub repos that will turn you into a 100x developer for free:

1. https://t.co/PqiVq9ZLbd

GitHub's own toolkit for spec-driven development, with 140K+ stars. Instead of letting the agent guess, you write a clear spec, it plans, breaks the work into tasks, then builds. It's the difference between an agent that wanders and one that ships what you actually asked for.

2. https://t.co/sCPtoQIuyQ

A full marketplace of 112 specialist agents and 146 skills that install in one go. A dedicated expert for debugging, security, code review, and docs, each ready to take a task. You stop making one generalist do everything and start running a department.

3. https://t.co/UCtkeppeCr

OpenAI's official plugin that lets you run Codex from inside Claude Code. Type /codex:review and you get a second frontier model auditing the first one's work. Two of the best coding models checking each other, in one terminal, free.

4. https://t.co/htbfPPXvTW

The canonical list of MCP servers, the plugins that give your agent real-world powers. Over 500 of them: databases, browsers, GitHub, Slack, filesystems. This is the shopping catalog for turning your coding agent from a chatbot into something that actually touches your systems.

5. https://t.co/Juf95Mx3p9

Automation your agent can actually drive, with 400+ integrations and native MCP support. Connect your apps, wire up a workflow, and let Claude or Codex trigger it. The thing Zapier charges you per task for, self-hosted and free, with an AI agent at the wheel.

6. https://t.co/U8UtmaiLyl

Lets Claude Code build and run n8n automations for you. Describe the workflow in plain English, "watch this inbox, summarize new emails, post them to Slack," and the agent wires up the whole pipeline. Automating your own life without touching the automation tool yourself.

7. https://t.co/xYpNfckkN6

A library of 100+ production-ready subagents you can drop into Claude Code, covering backend, frontend, DevOps, security, and more. When you need a specialist for a specific stack, it's already written. Copy, paste, and your agent just got an expert teammate.

8. https://t.co/3ol9btEpNS

An automated spec workflow that walks any task from requirements to design to tasks to implementation, with a dashboard to watch it happen. The guardrails that stop a big build from quietly drifting off course three hours in. Structure for the stuff that matters.

9. https://t.co/yJ6nJcvR2Q

The official skills library straight from Anthropic. Document handling, web app testing, and the core patterns everything else is built on. If you install nothing else from this list, start here, it's the reference set the whole ecosystem is measured against.

10. https://t.co/aDHWVaDSAo

The everything box: 135 agents, 42 commands, 176+ plugins, 20 hooks, and 14 MCP configs in one place. When you don't know what you need yet, this is where you go to see what's possible. The map of the entire Claude Code ecosystem.

Most people are still copy-pasting from a chat window.

The ones who set these up are writing software at a completely different speed.

quoted_text:
不需要Delta Hedge，用卖期权配合接货、抛货实现比特币本位增长的简便策略：
 
这是一个带 30 日均线过滤的 BTC 7 天 Wheel（轮转）回测，区间为 2023-10-06 至 2026-10-05，本金 1 BTC，不做 Delta 对冲、不计费用。三年下来赚了约 0.33 BTC，年化复利约 10%，主要来自卖 Put 权利金，代价是收益分布极左偏、回撤集中。
 
做法
 
只在现货高于 30 日均线时开仓。规则是卖出 7 天、25 delta 的 Put，名义等于当时全部权益（N = 100% Equity）。
 
Put 到期未被行权：继续下一轮卖 Put。
 
Put 被行权接货：在该指数上持有等量永续多头（相当于按 Put 行权价接货，U=K_put x Size_put），同时备兑卖出 7 天、25 delta 的 Call，张数按 U / K_call 计算，且 Call 行权价不低于 Put 行权价。
 
价格跌破均线触发退出：平掉永续并买回期权，暂停开新轮；价格重新站上均线后再从卖 Put 开始。

quoted_text: 加密一级市场为什么快死了，我们曾作为最活跃的投资机构之一，这十年感受最明显问题，第一个是叙事破灭了，从白皮书到机构背书到TVL刷量，基本市场不再买单。第二个是供给失衡，现在出现数以万计项目，优秀项目跑出来难度极大。第三个是1➕3解锁机制，基本是定向杀死VC，让项目，MM和交易所先跑，第四是上币成本，现在一级项目为什么需要高估值和大融资，主要是几个龙头交易所上线，平均成本需要千万美金。虽然VC问题也很多，但没有大量VC支持一级市场，市场只剩下专业发币集团和MEME币活跃。一级市场是加密创新的重要来源，需要行业龙头真正的去buliding方向，比如币安上币筛选方式改进，按照现在模式，当年V神的ETH来了也上不了币安。其次是彻底废除1➕3解锁机制，VC承担了最大风险，应该不背负最差的解锁条款，项目成功或失败根本不是VC决定的。最后是加密项目需要回到真正的营收和回购，美股那么多年持续繁荣，最重要的是业绩增长和督促回馈股东利益，这才是行业龙头们应该做的事情，让市场二级投资者真正找到优质项目。

text:
It’s hard to point to exactly where things went wrong but there used to be a lot more mission focus in this space. You rarely hear about decentralization and why it’s important anymore.

Probably the focus on getting a BTC ETF / “institutions” involved. This made it clear people cared about number go up over BTC being anti-establishment, a tool for freedom, savings, etc. While institutions are absolutely important for improving and modernizing financial infrastructure (Ethereum/Solana/DeFi), they’re really not for BTC. But they were needed to make price go up.

The natural response of new people coming into the space is to see it as a way to strike it rich. The vast majority of new entrants are coming in with 2-5 figs. They realize they can’t get rich from buying 15,000 sats so naturally they turn to speculation, leverage and memecoins. The vast majority of onchain activity is related to these things. Launchpads and perps platforms succeed because this is what most users want. There’s nothing inherently wrong with this and for most it goes in the same bucket as dudes ripping 8 leg parlays.

In the earlier days it was easy to just ignore when DOGE was the only coin but now it’s everywhere you look. Sharp traders naturally seek out the least informed counterparties and the rest, as they say, is history. There’s probably nothing anyone could have done to make it any other way. All the blame goes towards exchanges, launchpads, “extractors” but in retrospect, it is obvious this was always the inevitable path of a permissionless sandbox.

It’s a bit surreal to see this and the “real stuff” all happening at the same time. In the original DeFi telegram the first topic of conversation was whether to call it DeFi or OpFi (Open Finance). DeFi won out back then but as we see more tokenized RWA, centralized stablecoins, CFTC/SEC involvement, and big TradFi players planting their roots in every corner of the market, it’s clear that OpFi was more appropriate. 

Anyway since that ethos is dead hopefully the institutions can at least adopt our perps ways and manifest the pump on our bags before someone tries to shut down the blockchains in 2029 🚀

text:
Launchpads are the new NFTs.

Think back to what NFTs actually were at their peak. The art mattered less than what holding it meant: a profile picture was a membership card, a signal that you belonged to something and were early to it. The collections that survived were the ones that turned holders into a tribe.

But belonging to an NFT collection was mostly passive. You bought in, you held, and you waited. The team shipped the roadmap, a few big accounts drove the narrative, and everyone else watched the floor price. If the collection succeeded, you benefited from it, but you didn't build it. And if you missed the mint or got priced out, you were on the outside looking in.

Launchpads follow the same playbook with one crucial difference: anyone can take part in the success. Every participant can launch a token, shill it, and bring their own audience with them. A launch that takes off is a win for the person who created it, the people who traded it, and the platform itself. Nobody needs permission, a whitelist spot, or a five-figure entry ticket to contribute. You are helping write the story, where NFT holders could only own a piece of it.

That is why the strongest launchpads have one thing in common: a social moat. Cultural relevance. Community support. Anyone can fork the contracts, copy the bonding curve, and undercut the fees. What they can't copy is the crowd that shows up every day, trades together, and feels that the platform's success is their own.

Innovation brings attention, but attention fades the moment something newer ships. If you look at everything in this space that has reached billions in value, it has always been about bringing people together.

And since everyone is here to trade and make money, it's only natural that people rally around launchpads. An NFT collection gave you one asset and one outcome: the floor went up or it didn't. A launchpad gives you a new shot every day, with the same community rallying around each one. That is a much bigger upside than a 10K-piece JPEG collection could ever offer, and it keeps people engaged long after a mint would have sold out and gone quiet.

The tribes haven't gone anywhere. They've just moved from holding the same JPEG to building on the same platform.

Grid is now on 42.

Grid turns the live price chart into a board. Tap the one you believe in. When the chart reaches that column, the cell holding the price wins.

Leverage trading puts professional market makers on the other side of your trade. One wick and you’re liquidated, even when you called the price right.
Grid has no MM. Every column is a pool. No liquidation, no margin. The most you can lose is your stake, and you know it before you tap.

Two ways to play:
- Tap. Pick the exact price. Crowded cells pay less; contrarian choices pay more.
- Up / Down. Don’t want to be so precise? Pick a line and call the price above or below it.

text:
If I had to pick the single most important thing in trading, it would be risk management.

I mostly focus on day trading.

I usually set my risk-to-reward ratio at around 1:1 or 1:2, and when I identify a setup where I believe my win rate is above 50%, I repeat the same process consistently.

Risk-to-reward simply means how much you're willing to lose compared to how much you're aiming to make.

Even with just a 51% win rate and a 1:1 risk-to-reward ratio, you can have a positive expectancy over a large enough number of trades.

Trading isn't about relying on luck.

It's about building an edge, managing risk, and repeating that edge enough times to minimize the impact of luck.

More trades with a proven edge = less luck, more skill.

Think of it as turning a private solar project into an onchain market, giving investors exposure to its value and yield without owning the asset itself.

That could change who gets access to these investments, since projects like this usually:

→ Sit in private markets
→ Come with high barriers to entry
→ Offer limited liquidity

Loaf’s idea is to make that exposure easier to access and much easier to trade.

But the upside goes beyond the investor. The money is ultimately tied to infrastructure that produces electricity for homes and businesses.

text:
Time for a quick debunking of these claims..

> "THORChain is more decentralized than Bitcoin and Ethereum, by the definition that you're granting to me in this moment."

> "If you look at, like, halting, meaning the ability to stop the production of blocks, you would need 1/3 plus 1."  

Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are dynamically available, meaning block production does NOT halt should 1/3 plus 1 of their operators go offline. Block finalisation does halt, but the chain keeps going. This is fundamental to Ethereum's 100% uptime and its censorship-resistance.

It's also worth pausing on who are the largest entities in Ethereum's validator set. The largest, Lido (~21% of total stake) is not a monolith, it is a decentralised pool of operators operating delegated stake. In particular, there is a level of independence between operators within Lido, that complicates any statement regarding their coordinated behaviour.

Next, we have Binance (~7.5-8%), Kraken (~3.5-7%), Coinbase (~3.5-5%) and Etherfi (~3.8%). Numbers are approximative, as identification is not perfect, I'm looking at three different sources including Rated network @ratedw3b (which lists SSV as an independent entity, but it is in fact a collection of operators staking for other entities including Etherfi and Lido), https://t.co/sQxGpY2ETH @beaconcha_in and
@hildobby's Dune dashboard https://t.co/uvt2tOBBHV

We can certainly discuss whether these numbers are decentralised enough, what could be done if not etc. We just can't go around and claim that Ethereum would go down from the collusion of 1 or 2 parties. The chain keeps going, and the inactivity leak ensures finalisation resumes promptly.
author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
THORChain cofounder Chad Barraford admits 4 operators could halt THORChain, but argues Bitcoin and Ethereum can be stopped by even fewer

Laura: You said, quote, 'A chain may claim to have hundreds of validators, but that number means very little if most of them are operated by the same entities, hosted in the same data centers, or selected through a closed process.'"

"But THORChain itself has less than hundreds. And as we mentioned earlier, there are just 4 operator addresses that control 39 nodes. So do you think that THORChain passes your own litmus test?"

Chad: "Yeah. I think when it comes to evaluating how decentralized a protocol is, number of validators, not a good way to do it. And I'm not citing THORChain as decentralized because there's 115-ish validators. I'm saying it's decentralized because it has 50, 60, whatever the number is, individual operators across the world, which is better than Bitcoin, right?"

"Bitcoin's got 3, like, mining pools together would be 51% of the computing. Same thing for Ethereum. They've got, like, what, 3 or 4 operators with the major validators of Ethereum, and you would have the same situation. And most of those are, by the way, corporate entities, like Coinbase and Binance and these kinds of things."

"THORChain is more decentralized than Bitcoin and Ethereum, by the definition that you're granting to me in this moment."

"If you look at, like, halting, meaning the ability to stop the production of blocks, you would need 1/3 plus 1. It's something different if you categorize it as, like, a 2/3 majority to control the blockchain rather than stopping it."

"Even if you take the lesser of the two and you do, like, 1/3 plus 1, you can get 4 operators to, you know, stop the entire protocol. I don't know why they would do that, because you'd be burning your own RUNE to zero, which is not really in their financial interest to do so. But theoretically, on paper, they could do that."

"There's only, like, 3 entities you would need for Bitcoin, and, like, 1 or 2, or whatever the number is, for Ethereum. That's just, like, that is the world, right?"

text:
An AI agent can borrow money, spend it on tools and promise to repay. But if its work doesn’t earn enough, who absorbs the loss?

That question matters for @kudo_archi. Its updated positioning also makes the scope clearer: Kudo is building infrastructure for programmable promises between agents. Lending is one application of that infrastructure.

Agents need to pay for data, computing, APIs and other services. Credit could let them purchase resources before earning revenue. Other agreements involve delivering work after receiving payment, or paying someone after a job is completed.

All of these require a commitment that counterparties can inspect and evaluate.

Kudo turns that commitment into a transferable Covenant NFT, or cNFT.

The NFT records what an agent asks for and what it promises in return, including the amount, deadline or deliverable.

For a loan, the ask is funding upfront. The promise specifies repayment terms. Once the funding condition is fulfilled and verified, the cNFT transfers to the lender.

After the promise is fulfilled, Kudo’s Evaluator checks the outcome, closes the covenant and burns the NFT.

Transferability creates another possibility: a holder could sell the claim before settlement. An agent holding an invoice cNFT could eventually sell it at a discount to receive payment early, similar to invoice factoring.

However, Kudo’s secondary marketplace remains planned. Transferable claims still need buyers, reliable pricing and enough information to assess risk.

The updated design separates three functions.

The promise layer records commitments and monitors fulfillment.

Modules define the agreement, such as lending, work invoicing or advance payments. They’re intended to set limits, price risk and determine what covers a failure.

Hooks connect the system to evidence outside the NFT. Kudo says its current hooks check on-chain transfers and posts on X. Hooks for x402 receipts and general APIs are planned.

This distinction matters. Recording a promise is one task. Determining whether a particular service was delivered properly is another.

Kudo also explicitly separates willingness from ability.

It uses trusted execution environments, or TEEs, through @PhalaNetwork to attest that an agent runs the expected code. That code is designed to prioritize its open promises.

This gives counterparties evidence about the agent’s execution environment and repayment behavior. It doesn’t ensure the agent will earn enough, remain online or deliver satisfactory work.

An agent can follow its instructions and still fail financially.

Under Kudo’s proposed reputation design, broken promises become part of the agent’s public record. Counterparties could respond with stricter limits, higher prices or refusal to transact.

That may encourage responsible behavior, but reputation penalties don’t reimburse a lender who has already lost money. The module’s failure protections remain essential.

The credit-scoring story has changed too.

The older 0–10 “ability score,” based on mindshare, market capitalization and social engagement, has been superseded.

Kudo now plans a Kudos score based on promise history. That moves the emphasis toward observed fulfillment, although its predictive usefulness still needs evidence. ERC-8004 identity integration and the Kudos score remain roadmap items.

According to Kudo’s October 5 partner brief, the current system runs on Robinhood Chain testnet, with cNFTs, Phala attestation and an Evaluator checking loan repayments and X posts.

Mainnet deployment, work invoicing, advance-payment modules, additional hooks and decentralized Evaluators are planned.

The token numbers also need a correction.

Kudo reports 281.6 million $KUDO burned, equivalent to 28.16% of the stated one-billion supply.

That comprises 200 million from the team wallet and 81.6 million from Pons LaunchLocker. The team burn represents 20% of total supply, or two-thirds of its original allocation, taking that allocation from 30% to 10%.

Future Evaluator staking and slashing would give KUDO a role in securing verification. That remains planned, and burns alone don’t establish sustainable demand.

Personally, Kudo offers an interesting framework for agent agreements. Its updated design makes the responsibilities clearer.

The thesis gets stronger with audited execution, reliable evaluation, explicit loss allocation and repeated fulfillment funded by real customer revenue. The remaining challenge is proving both that agents honor commitments and that counterparties are adequately protected when they can’t.

NFA. DYOR.

众所周知，Ethena 是做稳定币的，USDe 是生息稳定币

但 9 月 25 日之后，它的生息来源发生了一次重要变化 ⬇️

从前只能靠「买币、同时做空币的合约」给 USDe 赚钱，现在则开始用同一套方法从「股票」中赚钱

更深层地解释一下，USDe 不是靠把美元存银行生息，它的老办法是「基差交易」 ⬇️

- 一边买入现货，比如 BTC

- 一边在永续合约里做空同样数量的 BTC

- 价格涨跌两边大致抵消，所以叫 Delta 中性，不赌涨跌
剩下能赚的，主要是永续的资金费：很多人杠杆做多时，会付钱给空头

其实并不复杂，就是很多人都这样做的「资金费率套利」只不过体量要大得多得多

这次 Ethena 创新性地使用 bStocks 和对应的股票合约来完成这件事

比如持有代币化英伟达，同时做空英伟达合约

币安是第一家配合它这么做的交易所

Ethena 创始人 Guy Young 称，这是 USDe 上线以来，资金机制最重要的一次扩展

总之利好不断，上涨不停，作为 $ENA holder 继续 bullish！

People don't get what the most exciting part of this deal is here.

In simple terms:

Solar energy has an obvious problem - most of the energy is produced during the day, while demand peaks in the evening.

Project Amber combines 200+ MW of solar with multi-hour battery storage, with new funding expected to help expand that storage capacity.

That means more excess solar power can be stored during the day and released when the sun goes down, instead of being wasted or forcing the grid to lean as heavily on fossil-fuel generation during peak hours.

@Loafmarkets is building an exchange for investments tied to individual physical assets, and this agreement could bring Australian solar + battery projects onto it.

So if you're familiar with RWAs, this could let you get exposure to a specific energy project's value and income, while the money raised could help fund its development and expand battery storage.

Still early with the MOU, but I'll keep an eye on whether you and I can invest and which projects get added.

text: .@MahoneDeFi breaks down @serotonin_hq's take on Pareto
author: paretocredit
quoted_text:
Serotonin’s article is one of the better deep dives into how @paretocredit is building an onchain credit marketplace for institutions.

Here are a few insights from the piece that still hold up today:

1. Pareto is filling a gap that Aave and Morpho don’t really address

Most major money markets are built around over-collateralized lending.

Institutions like prime brokers, prop trading firms, and crypto funds often need under-collateralized credit lines with customized terms.

Pareto’s Credit Vaults are designed for exactly that.

The smart contract acts more like a credit facility, with predefined lending cycles, interest rates, and redemption windows.

It is closer to "real credit" than a typical DeFi lending pool.

2. The hybrid onchain + offchain model is actually practical

Onchain: vaults, lending cycles, redemption windows, and callbacks for early exits when the borrower agrees.

Offchain: due diligence, loan structuring, monitoring, and reporting.

For example, the @FalconXGlobal vault has M11 Credit handling much of the credit underwriting and operational side.

That structure makes it possible to onboard names like FalconX, @RockawayX, and @FasanaraDigital instead of limiting the market to retail DeFi borrowers.

3. DeFi composability is an important part of the thesis

The FalconX vault receipt token, AA_FalconXUSDC, is already being used as collateral in Morpho markets curated by Gauntlet to build leveraged credit strategies.

The same exposure is now being risk-tranched through @roycoprotocol and also serves as a core underlying asset for nALPHA on @NestCredit x Plume.

If this thesis keeps expanding, Pareto’s moat may come from becoming the infrastructure layer that connects institutional credit with the rest of DeFi.

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
(1/2): I have met this person at nearly every crypto conference I have ever attended, and by now I can usually identify him before he even reaches the registration desk, because he arrives wearing the unmistakable expression of a man who has crossed three time zones, answered forty-seven Telegram messages from people he does not like, and paid twelve euros for airport water in order to be physically present at a gathering devoted to the future, only to discover, almost immediately, that the future appears to consist largely of men standing beneath purple lighting and discussing distribution.

He checks into the hotel, opens the conference app, scrolls through a schedule containing panels called things like “Reimagining Coordination at Scale” and “The New Institutional Frontier,” and feels, for one brief and embarrassing moment, the stirring of hope, because perhaps this will be the one, perhaps this will be the conference where somebody says something real, where a conversation escapes the gravitational pull of fundraising announcements, ecosystem grants, and whatever the phrase “go-to-market motion” is currently being asked to conceal.

By ten in the morning he has received a tote bag made from allegedly regenerative fabric, a metal water bottle that leaks from the lid, a lanyard large enough to function as a municipal permit, and three invitations to side events taking place simultaneously in different parts of the city, each one described as “intimate,” despite having eight hundred RSVPs and a DJ flown in from Berlin.

He goes to the first panel.

A founder says we are still early and venture capitalist says the next billion users are coming. Eventually a moderator, with the glazed composure of somebody who has already moderated this exact conversation in Singapore, Dubai, Paris, Denver, and a yacht off Mykonos, asks what needs to happen for mass adoption.

Everyone agrees that UX must improve and the audience nods with the solemnity of a parliamentary vote.

Nothing has technically been said, but the applause is loud.

By lunch he has participated in six conversations, all of which begin with “What are you working on?” and end with “We should definitely find a way to collaborate,” which in conference language means that both parties will add one another on Telegram, exchange a fire emoji beneath a future announcement post, and never again occupy the same emotional universe.

He meets a man building infrastructure for autonomous agents, although the infrastructure is not yet built and the agents are not yet autonomous. He meets another man launching a protocol for decentralized reputation, who spends most of the conversation explaining which well-known investors already trust him. He meets a founder who says he is obsessed with user sovereignty, then glances every twenty seconds toward the entrance in case someone more important has arrived.

By the evening he is standing in a cavernous venue once used to manufacture turbines, now filled with dry ice, ornamental lasers, and several thousand people discussing credible neutrality while trying to get past a velvet rope.

There is free food, technically, although it consists of two miniature tacos placed on a slate tile by a person wearing black gloves, and there is free alcohol, abundantly, which may explain why the revolution against extractive intermediaries has temporarily organized itself around a sponsored bar requiring three wristbands and a QR code.

text:
我们正站在稳定币超级周期的起点。
但坏消息是，美元稳定币早已是一片红海。

Tether 与 Circle 构成的双寡头格局，让所有后来者望而却步。
供应量上，USDT 与 USDC 合计占稳定币总市值约 83%；
使用量上，仅 USDT 就占据 CEX 交易量的 73.6%；
盈利能力上，Tether 年净利润已超过百亿美元，其美债持仓规模位列全球第 17，超过多数主权国家。
今天想在美元稳定币市场挑战这两大巨头，难度不亚于在 2010 年重新打造一个 Facebook。

然而，这个看似固化的市场中，还隐藏着一个被绝大多数人忽视的机会。
目前，约 99.5% 的稳定币都以美元为支撑。
换句话说，所有非美元货币在链上的份额加起来还不到 0.5%。这是一整片尚未被开垦的大陆。
真正的问题只有两个：
▌哪种非美元货币值得被搬上链？
▌应该用什么机制将它搬上链？

作为目前规模最大的瑞士法郎稳定币，@frankencoinzchf 给出了自己的答案。
Frankencoin 于 2023 年上线，从未脱锚，目前已部署在 8 条链上，TVL 超过 6300 万美元。
10 月 8 日，稳定币 ZCHF 上线 Kraken。目前支持的交易对为 ZCHF/USD、ZCHF/CHF, 对于 Frankencoin 来说，这是一个里程碑式的时刻。

1/ 为什么是瑞士法郎？
稳定币锚定哪种法币，本质上是在替持有者选择一条长期购买力曲线。
过去 50 多年里，美元对瑞士法郎累计贬值约 80%。瑞郎能够长期保持强势，背后有几个重要原因：
瑞士央行长期奉行克制的货币政策；
瑞士拥有长期低通胀的传统；
政治中立、财政稳健、法治健全，使瑞郎具备天然的避险货币属性。
因此，持有 USDT 十年和持有 ZCHF 十年，最终的购买力差距可能相当可观。

2/ 为什么是 Frankencoin？
大多数美元稳定币，本质上是美元资产的代币化包装。
Circle、Tether 等中心化发行商持有美国国债等储备资产，再在链上发行对应的稳定币。用户真正信任的，依然是背后的发行机构。

Frankencoin 选择了完全不同的路径。
没有中心化发行方；
由链上资产超额抵押；
抵押品包括 BTC、ETH、代币化黄金和代币化股票；
整个系统去中心化运行，储备与规则均可链上验证。
它更接近 DAI 的模式，只不过锚定的不是美元，而是瑞士法郎。

对于加密原生用户来说，无需信任中心化机构并非附加功能，而是产品最核心的价值之一。
在机制设计上，Frankencoin 由两个核心代币组成。
▌ZCHF 是稳定币本身，可用于支付、储蓄和借贷。
▌FCS 代表储备池的所有权份额。协议收入归 FCS 沉淀在储备池，同时 FCS 持有者也拥有协议治理权。
一个负责提供稳定价值，另一个负责承接协议收益与治理权，两者共同构成 Frankencoin 的经济系统。

3/ Frankencoin 真正瞄准的市场
必须承认，Frankencoin 不会与 USDT、USDC 正面争夺交易流动性。
属于它的战场在别处。
它瞄准的，是美元稳定币双寡头在结构上难以覆盖的三类需求。
长期购买力保值；
去中心化与抗审查；
真实的瑞士法郎支付需求。
如果用一句话概括，美元稳定币是链上的现金流货币，瑞郎稳定币则更像链上的避险储蓄账户。
二者并不是非此即彼的替代关系，而是服务于不同场景的互补关系。

当稳定币超级周期真正展开，市场终将意识到，稳定币的多元化，不仅意味着发行方的多元化，更意味着底层计价货币的多元化。

What makes $HIGGS truly worth paying attention to is that it is trying to turn AI influencers, tokens, and content production into a closed loop.

DoVAVzViX8Bjy3r15nwikSaSbzE6dV4ovd28aWpJpump 

The concept is very simple: create an AI influencer, define its image and name, and then directly generate a corresponding token. The character, content, and token are bound together from the very beginning.

What’s really interesting is the economic model. 30% of the trading fees generated by each AI influencer is used to buy back and burn HIGGS, while the rest goes into the content-creation-related economy. In other words, token trading activity can in turn provide an AI influencer with the budget to continuously produce content.

In theory, this creates a cycle:Token Trading → Fees → Content Production → Attention → More Trading → Fees

This is the biggest difference from traditional AI Memes: AI is not just narrative packaging, but is actually built into the token’s economic cycle.

If an AI influencer can continuously produce content, gain attention, and then convert that attention into trading volume, it effectively has its own content engine.

Of course, the biggest variable in this model is also very clear.

Creating an AI character is no longer difficult. The real challenge is: can that character continuously capture attention?

If it ultimately just becomes Launch → Produce Content → Nobody Watches → No Trading, then HIGGS is still just a more AI-native Launchpad.

But if it can eventually produce a group of AI influencers with sustained growth, stable content, UGC, followers, and trading volume, then HIGGS’s positioning will change.

It may no longer just be an AI token launchpad, but instead be trying to become the infrastructure for an AI-native Creator Economy.

So simply looking at how many tokens HIGGS has launched is basically meaningless.

The three things that actually need to be watched are:

- Whether content can remain sustainable as the number of AI influencers grows;

- Whether content can convert into real attention and trading volume;

- Whether trading activity across the ecosystem can continuously translate into HIGGS buybacks and burns.

If these three metrics start forming a positive feedback loop, HIGGS’s valuation logic may truly shift from AI Launchpad to AI Influencer Economy.

Higgspad’s core idea is to let users quickly create AI influencers with a single sentence, automatically launch a dedicated token for each character on pumpfun, and use its Studio tool to generate short videos featuring that character.

It primarily aims to solve two problems: creating virtual influencers or AI content accounts has a high barrier to entry, while pure Meme coins lack the ongoing content needed to sustain attention.

The platform bundles “character creation + video generation + one-click token launch” into a single workflow, allowing trading fees to support AI generation and the platform token in return.

The process takes three steps: describe the character, choose a template, or upload a photo to generate a profile picture and full-body image → name the character → launch its token with one click from your own wallet.

Each AI character comes with its own token, while the platform token captures value through burns funded by trading fees from these sub-tokens. It essentially works like an “AI character factory + fee flywheel.”

HIGGS is the platform token. Under the mechanism, 30% of the creator fees from every AI token launched through Higgspad is used to buy back and burn HIGGS. The remaining 70% can be allocated by the creator between the “AI Treasury” and their own wallet.

What makes this interesting is how it directly connects the currently popular AI video generation trend with Solana Meme launches, creating a simple loop of “content creation → token trading → partial fee-funded platform token burns.” Its advantages include an extremely low barrier to entry, fast launches, a clear fee-revenue mechanism, and built-in spending controls and freeze switches.

SymRegFlow just redefines how video world models handle camera control.

Instead of needing dense, expensive pose–video pairs, it fine-tunes existing models using only noisy geometry-based proxies—no real novel-view footage required. The trick: dual “anchors” warped to each target pose, with a cross-anchor consistency objective that, both in theory and in practice, recovers clean results. On nuScenes, SymRegFlow achieves state-of-the-art FVD (158.6, down 31% vs. FreeVS) and FVMD (2519), with best-in-class FID (19.2) and 99.4 instance preservation for source-conditioned inference.

Directed Cross-View Attention keeps compute low (1.5× less than full attention) and protects original-view quality.

This is a lightweight, architecture-agnostic upgrade for scalable, viewpoint-controllable video generation—no extra data collection, and grounded in theory.

quoted_text:
The rest of Asia has moved. Korea is still deciding.

Hong Kong licensed its first stablecoin issuers in April. Japan's yen stablecoin has been live since October 2025. Singapore is writing its framework into law. Korea passed its tokenized-securities law in January and reopened its exchanges to corporations, but the Digital Asset Basic Act, the statute that would license a won stablecoin, remains in committee over a single question: who gets to issue it.

While that question sits unanswered, net stablecoin outflows from Korean exchanges have run for eighteen consecutive months, about $10.4 billion in total, almost all of it in dollars. The demand for onchain assets is there. It is being served offshore.

Today we are publishing The Seoul Standard, a joint research report with @redstone_defi written for the allocators, funds and institutions weighing Korea. It covers:

- A decade of Korean digital asset legislation, from the 2017 ICO ban to VAUPA, and why each crisis produced the next statute
- What DABA and the enacted STO framework require of institutions, and the bank-versus-fintech dispute stalling one of them
- How a won stablecoin, tokenized deposits and tokenized securities could put inert KRW balances to work onchain
- Bear, base and bull scenarios with dated triggers, plus a sourced risk register

Read and download the full report (KR/EN): https://t.co/sP7lEzjHbF

text:
我们正站在稳定币超级周期的起点。
但坏消息是，美元稳定币早已是一片红海。

Tether 与 Circle 构成的双寡头格局，让所有后来者望而却步。
供应量上，USDT 与 USDC 合计占稳定币总市值约 83%；
使用量上，仅 USDT 就占据 CEX 交易量的 73.6%；
盈利能力上，Tether 年净利润已超过百亿美元，其美债持仓规模位列全球第 17，超过多数主权国家。
今天想在美元稳定币市场挑战这两大巨头，难度不亚于在 2010 年重新打造一个 Facebook。

然而，这个看似固化的市场中，还隐藏着一个被绝大多数人忽视的机会。
目前，约 99.5% 的稳定币都以美元为支撑。
换句话说，所有非美元货币在链上的份额加起来还不到 0.5%。这是一整片尚未被开垦的大陆。
真正的问题只有两个：
▌哪种非美元货币值得被搬上链？
▌应该用什么机制将它搬上链？

作为目前规模最大的瑞士法郎稳定币，@frankencoinzchf 给出了自己的答案。
Frankencoin 于 2023 年上线，从未脱锚，目前已部署在 8 条链上，TVL 超过 6300 万美元。
10 月 8 日，稳定币 ZCHF 上线 Kraken。目前支持的交易对为 ZCHF/USD、ZCHF/CHF, 对于 Frankencoin 来说，这是一个里程碑式的时刻。

1/ 为什么是瑞士法郎？
稳定币锚定哪种法币，本质上是在替持有者选择一条长期购买力曲线。
过去 50 多年里，美元对瑞士法郎累计贬值约 80%。瑞郎能够长期保持强势，背后有几个重要原因：
瑞士央行长期奉行克制的货币政策；
瑞士拥有长期低通胀的传统；
政治中立、财政稳健、法治健全，使瑞郎具备天然的避险货币属性。
因此，持有 USDT 十年和持有 ZCHF 十年，最终的购买力差距可能相当可观。

2/ 为什么是 Frankencoin？
大多数美元稳定币，本质上是美元资产的代币化包装。
Circle、Tether 等中心化发行商持有美国国债等储备资产，再在链上发行对应的稳定币。用户真正信任的，依然是背后的发行机构。

Frankencoin 选择了完全不同的路径。
没有中心化发行方；
由链上资产超额抵押；
抵押品包括 BTC、ETH、代币化黄金和代币化股票；
整个系统去中心化运行，储备与规则均可链上验证。
它更接近 DAI 的模式，只不过锚定的不是美元，而是瑞士法郎。

对于加密原生用户来说，无需信任中心化机构并非附加功能，而是产品最核心的价值之一。
在机制设计上，Frankencoin 由两个核心代币组成。
▌ZCHF 是稳定币本身，可用于支付、储蓄和借贷。
▌FCS 代表储备池的所有权份额。协议收入归 FCS 沉淀在储备池，同时 FCS 持有者也拥有协议治理权。
一个负责提供稳定价值，另一个负责承接协议收益与治理权，两者共同构成 Frankencoin 的经济系统。

3/ Frankencoin 真正瞄准的市场
必须承认，Frankencoin 不会与 USDT、USDC 正面争夺交易流动性。
属于它的战场在别处。
它瞄准的，是美元稳定币双寡头在结构上难以覆盖的三类需求。
长期购买力保值；
去中心化与抗审查；
真实的瑞士法郎支付需求。
如果用一句话概括，美元稳定币是链上的现金流货币，瑞郎稳定币则更像链上的避险储蓄账户。
二者并不是非此即彼的替代关系，而是服务于不同场景的互补关系。

当稳定币超级周期真正展开，市场终将意识到，稳定币的多元化，不仅意味着发行方的多元化，更意味着底层计价货币的多元化。

text:
@chainalysis  最新发布的《东亚加密采用报告》显示，

在全面禁止加密交易的背景下，中国大陆链上稳定币 P2P 交易的独立钱包数量，在2024年-2026年的两年内暴涨了 43 倍。

在大多数人眼里，大陆的 P2P 交易无非是去交易所买卖 U、微信支付宝转账出入金的日常操作。

但这份报告揭开的是稳定币在链上的一套庞大“影子结算网络”，一些有意思的细节和洞察如下：

1.U 不再是资产，是高频周转的营运资金

报告统计，在全面禁止交易所的背景下，大陆年间仍跑出了至少 1760 亿美元的加密经济规模;

其中 59.1% 完全由个人独立钱包之间的点对点流转驱动，这个份额在过去一年里翻了 3.5 倍。

大陆自托管的稳定币,年化资金周转率高达 33.2 次，是全球平均水平（9.3 次）的 3.5 倍，远超香港（6.1 次）和日本（9.9 次）。

换算成直观的体量，意味着大陆用户手里平均只沉淀了约 31 亿美元的稳定币底仓，却在一年里倒手刷出了 1041 亿美元的总流转额与 1810 万次转账数据。

此外，造成交易数据激增的主力并非大户搬砖，而是 100 美元以下的微额转账（暴涨 996%），以及 1000 到 10000 美元的中小额商户款项（暴涨 1321%）。

2. 爆发拐点：传统支付风控外溢，催生替代通道

报告把这一波爆发的转折点，精确锁定在 2025 年 3 月。 
当时国内社会信用与金融互联网风控体系进一步扩容，银行端针对异常资金流的监控和“断卡”常态化，部分个人和跨境小微商户在传统银行通道里遭遇了限额、冻结或风控壁垒。 

这种强摩擦催生了强需求：抗审查、免许可的稳定币成了天然的替代支付工具。

典型的场景正是“国内电商平台沟通商品细节，转头切到 Telegram 甩出钱包地址直接结付 USDT”。

既然没有合规交易所，这些数据到底怎么算出来的？

Chainalysis 作为数据分析机构，并不依赖官方申报或问卷，而是先通过庞大的地址标签库，剥离掉全球合规交易所的内部撮合，专门将个人独立钱包（Unhosted Wallets）之间以及“个人与场外承兑商（OTC）”的链上真实转账单独提炼出来；

再结合亚洲时区的网络流量特征、客户端语言，以及服务于华人圈的知名 OTC 承兑资金簇进行关联归因。 

Chainalysis 自己也承认，目前统计的大陆1760 亿美元的加密规模，只是基于链上确凿痕迹倒推出来的保守保底值，水面下的真实体量只多不少。

从数据来看，国内现实环境的监管摩擦与防冻卡需求，反而自下而上地催熟了一套极其务实、换手率极高的地下清算体系。

稳定币在大陆早已超越了单纯的投机工具，被用成了流通性极强的影子化、数字化美元现金。

quoted_text:
AI Trading 或许还很遥远，但 AI Strategy 已经近在眼前。

关于 AI 交易，我一直持审慎态度。
原因在于，LLM 是足够好的工程师，却不是好的预言家。交易本质上是在和市场的随机性对赌，把这件事交给一个黑盒，风险不可控、亏损无法追溯。
可换个角度看，理解 DeFi 原语、编写 Python、生成一份清晰的策略 PRD，恰恰是 LLM 的强项。
让 AI 去造工具，而不是替你下注，这才是更务实、也更安全的用法。
这正是我看好 @almanak 的原因。

1/ 我用 Almanak 搭了一个真实的池子
我用 Almanak 创建了一个 LP 策略，用来管理 Uniswap V3（BSC）上 USDT-BTCB 资金池中的流动性仓位。参数如下：
▌最多投入 80% 双边余额
▌价格区间为现价 ±10%
▌每日最多 3 次再平衡
整个过程没有写一行代码，也没有把决策权交给任何黑盒，参数完全由我掌控。

2/ Almanak 是什么
它是一个代理式、非托管的链上策略平台。
三类意图：支持 Swap / LP / Borrow，覆盖大多数 DeFi 操作场景
七条链：多链部署
两种范式：既支持规则明确的确定性策略，也支持 LLM 驱动的 agentic 策略
非托管：资金始终在你自己的 Safe 钱包里，

3/ 上手其实很简单
前置准备：
一个 Web3 钱包

然后，两条路任选其一 👇
▌路径 A - 从信号出发
在 Edge 里挑一个信号 → 发给 Almanak Code → 自动生成 PRD + 代码 → 对话迭代 → 一键部署

▌路径 B - 完全自定义
打开 Almanak Code，用自然语言描述你想要的策略 → 对话迭代生成代码 → 进入部署向导
无论哪条路，最终你拿到的都是份可审查、你自己拥有的代码。用户可以自行选择是否将策略代码导出到 GitHub 。

Almanak 传送 - https://t.co/mO9SebyFVq

4/ 也要清楚它的边界
任何工具都有它的射程，Almanak 也不例外。
它擅长的是分钟级及以上的策略，比如收益轮动、LP 管理、费率套利、自动再平衡等。
它不擅长的是高频交易、MEV 抢跑、清算机器人的速度竞赛。

换句话说，它卖的是策略能力。这也恰好呼应了它对自己的定位——一个人的链上对冲基金。

text:
Time for a quick debunking of these claims..

> "THORChain is more decentralized than Bitcoin and Ethereum, by the definition that you're granting to me in this moment."

> "If you look at, like, halting, meaning the ability to stop the production of blocks, you would need 1/3 plus 1."  

Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are dynamically available, meaning block production does NOT halt should 1/3 plus 1 of their operators go offline. Block finalisation does halt, but the chain keeps going. This is fundamental to Ethereum's 100% uptime and its censorship-resistance.

It's also worth pausing on who are the largest entities in Ethereum's validator set. The largest, Lido (~21% of total stake) is not a monolith, it is a decentralised pool of operators operating delegated stake. In particular, there is a level of independence between operators within Lido, that complicates any statement regarding their coordinated behaviour.

Next, we have Binance (~7.5-8%), Kraken (~3.5-7%), Coinbase (~3.5-5%) and Etherfi (~3.8%). Numbers are approximative, as identification is not perfect, I'm looking at three different sources including Rated network @ratedw3b (which lists SSV as an independent entity, but it is in fact a collection of operators staking for other entities including Etherfi and Lido), https://t.co/sQxGpY2ETH @beaconcha_in and
@hildobby's Dune dashboard https://t.co/uvt2tOBBHV

We can certainly discuss whether these numbers are decentralised enough, what could be done if not etc. We just can't go around and claim that Ethereum would go down from the collusion of 1 or 2 parties. The chain keeps going, and the inactivity leak ensures finalisation resumes promptly.

THORChain cofounder Chad Barraford admits 4 operators could halt THORChain, but argues Bitcoin and Ethereum can be stopped by even fewer

"But THORChain itself has less than hundreds. And as we mentioned earlier, there are just 4 operator addresses that control 39 nodes. So do you think that THORChain passes your own litmus test?"

Chad: "Yeah. I think when it comes to evaluating how decentralized a protocol is, number of validators, not a good way to do it. And I'm not citing THORChain as decentralized because there's 115-ish validators. I'm saying it's decentralized because it has 50, 60, whatever the number is, individual operators across the world, which is better than Bitcoin, right?"

"Bitcoin's got 3, like, mining pools together would be 51% of the computing. Same thing for Ethereum. They've got, like, what, 3 or 4 operators with the major validators of Ethereum, and you would have the same situation. And most of those are, by the way, corporate entities, like Coinbase and Binance and these kinds of things."

"THORChain is more decentralized than Bitcoin and Ethereum, by the definition that you're granting to me in this moment."

"If you look at, like, halting, meaning the ability to stop the production of blocks, you would need 1/3 plus 1. It's something different if you categorize it as, like, a 2/3 majority to control the blockchain rather than stopping it."

"Even if you take the lesser of the two and you do, like, 1/3 plus 1, you can get 4 operators to, you know, stop the entire protocol. I don't know why they would do that, because you'd be burning your own RUNE to zero, which is not really in their financial interest to do so. But theoretically, on paper, they could do that."

"There's only, like, 3 entities you would need for Bitcoin, and, like, 1 or 2, or whatever the number is, for Ethereum. That's just, like, that is the world, right?"
