quoted_text:
AI Trading 或许还很遥远，但 AI Strategy 已经近在眼前。

关于 AI 交易，我一直持审慎态度。
原因在于，LLM 是足够好的工程师，却不是好的预言家。交易本质上是在和市场的随机性对赌，把这件事交给一个黑盒，风险不可控、亏损无法追溯。
可换个角度看，理解 DeFi 原语、编写 Python、生成一份清晰的策略 PRD，恰恰是 LLM 的强项。
让 AI 去造工具，而不是替你下注，这才是更务实、也更安全的用法。
这正是我看好 @almanak 的原因。

1/ 我用 Almanak 搭了一个真实的池子
我用 Almanak 创建了一个 LP 策略，用来管理 Uniswap V3（BSC）上 USDT-BTCB 资金池中的流动性仓位。参数如下：
▌最多投入 80% 双边余额
▌价格区间为现价 ±10%
▌每日最多 3 次再平衡
整个过程没有写一行代码，也没有把决策权交给任何黑盒，参数完全由我掌控。

2/ Almanak 是什么
它是一个代理式、非托管的链上策略平台。
三类意图：支持 Swap / LP / Borrow，覆盖大多数 DeFi 操作场景
七条链：多链部署
两种范式：既支持规则明确的确定性策略，也支持 LLM 驱动的 agentic 策略
非托管：资金始终在你自己的 Safe 钱包里，

3/ 上手其实很简单
前置准备：
一个 Web3 钱包

然后，两条路任选其一 👇
▌路径 A - 从信号出发
在 Edge 里挑一个信号 → 发给 Almanak Code → 自动生成 PRD + 代码 → 对话迭代 → 一键部署

▌路径 B - 完全自定义
打开 Almanak Code，用自然语言描述你想要的策略 → 对话迭代生成代码 → 进入部署向导
无论哪条路，最终你拿到的都是份可审查、你自己拥有的代码。用户可以自行选择是否将策略代码导出到 GitHub 。

Almanak 传送 - https://t.co/mO9SebyFVq

4/ 也要清楚它的边界
任何工具都有它的射程，Almanak 也不例外。
它擅长的是分钟级及以上的策略，比如收益轮动、LP 管理、费率套利、自动再平衡等。
它不擅长的是高频交易、MEV 抢跑、清算机器人的速度竞赛。

换句话说，它卖的是策略能力。这也恰好呼应了它对自己的定位——一个人的链上对冲基金。

text:
Compound V2 never writes to your debt balance. You still owe more every block.

The whole trick is two numbers.

borrowIndex: one global value that grows every time interest accrues.
Your snapshot: what borrowIndex was the moment you borrowed.

debt = principal × borrowIndex / snapshot

That's one storage write per market, whether it has 10 borrowers or 100,000. Your account sits untouched until you act.

Once you've seen this pattern you'll recognise it in staking and reward contracts everywhere.

@hayandaejang has the full write-up. Thanks to everyone who came, and to @FlareNetworksKR, @SantimentData, @xrplkorea and for a great night 🇰🇷
author: soil_farm
quoted_text:
어제 XRPFi Night Seoul 현장에서 가장 귀가 쫑긋했던 질문 하나.

“XRP를 그냥 들고 있는 것과, XRP가 일을 하게 만드는 것은 얼마나 다를까?”

이번 행사에서 @soil_farm 의 발표를 직접 들으면서 그 질문에 대한 꽤 구체적인 그림을 볼 수 있었습니다.

가장 먼저 눈에 들어온 숫자는 약 5%.

그런데 중요한 건 5%라는 숫자 자체보다

“Where does 5% come from?”

즉, 이 수익이 도대체 어디에서 만들어지느냐였습니다.

@soil_farm 이 설명한 구조는 꽤 명확했습니다.

“Two engines. One asset.”

내 XRP는 그대로 XRP 익스포저를 유지하면서 두 개의 수익 엔진으로 운용되는 구조였습니다.

첫 번째 엔진은 약 50%를 전문 트레이딩 회사에 대출하는 방식.

Prime brokers와 hedge funds 등을 대상으로 하며 secured 또는 parent-guaranteed 형태라고 설명했습니다.

두 번째 약 50%는 Market-neutral digital-asset managers.

발표 자료에서는 규제된 multi-manager fund인 M-Squared를 통한 운용이라고 소개했습니다.

그리고 다시 돌아오는 것은

XRP 원금 + 이자.

포인트를 뿌리거나 토큰 발행으로 APY를 포장하는 방식이 아니라 실제 자산 운용에서 수익의 원천을 찾겠다는 설명이 인상적이었습니다.

“No emissions. No points. No token to sell.”

그렇다면 또 하나의 질문이 생기죠.

“내 XRP가 어디로 가는지는 누가 결정할까?”

여기서 @soil_farm 은 모든 facility가 ORQO에 의해 언더라이팅된다고 설명했습니다.

발표 화면에 제시된 ORQO의 수치는

$315M AUM,
20년 이상의 Private Credit 경험,
$1B+ Private Transactions 완료.

그리고 특히 강조한 숫자가 하나 더 있었습니다.

“0 loans lost.”

발표 자료 기준 3년 이상의 온체인 렌딩 과정에서 대출 손실이 없었다는 트랙레코드를 제시했습니다.

물론 화면 하단에도 적혀 있었듯 과거 성과가 미래 결과를 보장하는 것은 아닙니다.

이 부분은 숫자만 떼어놓고 보기보다 같이 봐야겠죠.

또 하나 재미있었던 부분은 온체인과 현실 세계의 법적 계약을 연결하는 방식이었습니다.

“A hash proves it happened.
A legal contract proves it’s yours.”

그래서 KYC도 등장합니다.

계약에는 명확한 두 당사자가 필요하기 때문에 한 번의 KYC를 거치고,

@soil_farm 은 이를 단순한 귀찮은 인증 절차가 아니라 추가적인 보안 레이어로 설명했습니다.

“Lose your wallet. Keep your claim.”

이 문장이 꽤 기억에 남았습니다.

대신 조건도 분명했습니다.

출금을 원할 경우 40-day notice.

수익률만 보고 들어갈 구조가 아니라 자금이 어떤 방식으로 운용되고, 회수 조건이 무엇인지까지 같이 봐야 한다는 뜻이죠.

현재 발표 자료에서 제시한 XRP Vault의 트랙레코드는

$30M+ in XRP,
일평균 신규 유입 $200K~$1M.

현장에서 이 숫자를 직접 보니 XRPFi라는 말이 단순한 구호에서 실제 금융 구조로 넘어가고 있다는 느낌도 들었습니다.

개인적으로 이번 @soil_farm 발표에서 가장 흥미로웠던 건 5%가 아니었습니다.

“왜 5%를 줄 수 있는가?”를 먼저 설명했다는 점.

DeFi에서 높은 숫자는 얼마든지 볼 수 있지만,

그 숫자가 어디서 생기고,
누가 자산을 운용하고,
어떤 계약으로 보호되고,
어떤 조건으로 다시 돌려받는지까지 설명할 수 있어야 진짜 금융에 가까워진다고 생각합니다.

그리고 이어진 Partner Session 2에서는 @FlareNetworks @FlareNetworksKR 의 APAC Community Lead Kyle Kim이

“XRPFi on Flare: Putting Your XRP to Work”

라는 주제로 바통을 이어받았습니다.

행사에 함께한 @sivax_official, @SantimentData, @DCENTWALLETS @DCENTWALLETS_KR 그리고 @Tani_9325 까지.

XRP를 단순히 보유하는 자산에서 실제 활용되는 자산으로 확장하려는 여러 팀을 한자리에서 볼 수 있었던 것도 이번 XRPFi Night Seoul의 재미였습니다.

결국 이날 행사 전체를 관통했던 질문도 비슷했던 것 같습니다.

잠자고 있는 XRP를 어떻게 실제로 움직이는 자산으로 만들 것인가.

💡HD Insight

XRPFi의 경쟁은 앞으로 “누가 APY 숫자를 더 크게 쓰느냐”보다

“그 APY가 어디서 왔는지를 누가 가장 투명하게 증명하느냐”에서 갈릴지도 모르겠습니다.

5%보다 더 중요했던 것은,
그 5% 뒤에 있는 구조였습니다.

author: ika_xbt
quoted_text:
my logics behind betting on pump pairs matter.

pumpfun can change the entire landscape on solana with one move.

make pump pairs the standard. so to me, this is the logical next step. not just another narrative, but a change in how liquidity flows through the ecosystem.

pump already owns a huge part of solana’s activity.

on sept 25, pump reported 872k active solana wallets vs 122k excluding pump activity. pumpswap is doing ~$400m tvl and ~$13b monthly volume.

but sol still sits underneath a lot of this economy.

tokens are paired against sol. traders hold sol between bets. lp liquidity is held in sol. fees and rewards are paid around sol.

so if pump is already the biggest venue, the logical next step is pretty simple:

why should all this liquidity keep creating demand for sol?

flip token/sol into token/pump.

using pumpswap tvl, a rough estimate puts ~$140-180m of sol sitting on the quote side of pump markets today.

at ~$160m and pump around $0.0065, that’s roughly 24.5b pump, or more than 5% of circulating supply.

and that’s just the liquidity already there.

now imagine every new pool needs pump instead of sol.

traders hold pump between bets.

rewards circulate in pump.

pump earns the fees.

pump buys and burns with part of that revenue.

suddenly pump isn’t just the platform.

it becomes the asset sitting underneath the platform’s entire economy.

that’s why pump pairs extremely important narrative and memecoins there will be leading pump eco.

quoted_text:
I normally don't do this but I'm going to go out on a limb here.  With all of the "CT darlings" at pretty rich multiples I've been on the search for protocols where the price looks to be disconnected from fundamentals.

I've found a few but the one I want to post about this evening is ethereum:0xad29f2723fcdbcf665f210f25e06f97477e417cf (Gravity).

Running the raw numbers I believe this could be trading anywhere between 5x-20x below peers, and even more if you assume any sort of growth going forward.  Here's what I'm seeing:

-Gravity doesn't post daily revenue numbers but they do post their fee schedule, rebate programs and daily volume.  Using that data we can calculate a blended fee rate of between 2.1-4.49bp, or around $58M/yr if it lands somewhere in the middle.
-There's another way to guesstimate daily revenue which is to use the book turnover multiple.  Using peer per dex's. this scatter plot has an r-squared of around 0.7 and would put GRVT's fees closer to $28M, which is technically below the lowest possible value using their actual fee tables.  Since nobody knows the real value I'll let you make your own assumption.
-Post-farm OI is climbing.  After OI fell off when the farming programs ended, OI has been back on a healthy climb near ATH's.
-Volume has leveled out, and it may even be back on the rise.  You can see in just the last few weeks volume has significantly smoothed out into a more natural flow vs the very saw-toothed trend going back to last year.  Similar to OI, I see this as the protocol having transitioned into more natural, demand driven usage.
-On almost every metric vs peers (17 other per dex's) this protocol is trading at depressed valuations: revenue/circ mc multiple, revenue/fdv mc multiple,  

So why is it trading like this?  I think it's twofold.  The first and most likely is it's simply not a CT darling.   There is a small cohort of per dex's that trade at rich multiples because they make up 95% of the day-to-day chatter CT chatter and they have some of the biggest investors/KOLs/MM's on their side to keep their attention economy pumping.  The other is the price chart since TGE looks like a wet fart.  Literally everyone that put money in this at almost any point is underwater.  And when you both don't own the attention economy and burned all of your investors out of the gate, you get GRVT multiples.

But time heals all things and I think this token has been punished enough.  It's priced so low that it's almost being priced like a failed protocol, when in fact the numbers look very solid, not far below some of the CT darlings but at a much, much cheaper valuation.

Assuming their fee schedule and posted data is accurate, then there is likely little to no wash trading going on.  It would be too expensive at the posted rates.

So are there no risks?  There definitely are!  First and foremost, just because price is low doesn't mean it can't go even lower.  Oh trust me my bullish friend, it definitely can.  I just assume any money put into something like this can go to zero.  The other big risk is token unlocks.  There are a number of giga unlocks between now and next July.  But the reason I'm not worried about them is not only is this token trading and at *extremely* depressed circ mc multiple (likely around 0.5x) but it's trading at a depressed FDV multiple as well (around 5x).  So even if all tokens unlocked today (and they wont all unlock until 2030) this protocol is still trading around 4x below the cheaper end of its peers.

This is getting much more long winded than I planned so I'll stop here.  But I'd suggest if you're intersted in this then also check out the integrations they already have and some of the tech they are shipping.  It's all looks exciting and bullish to me.

But what do I know, I'm just a ct larp on my best day and an X unc on my worst day.

Disclaimer: I have a position in GRVT, this is not financial advice, I don't really care if you buy it, you will probably lose everything if you buy it, etc

text:
Ethereum Just Solved a Piece of L1-L2 Fragmentation

Ethereum just hit an important milestone for its L1 + L2 ecosystem.

The Ethereum mainnet completed its first atomic transaction between L1 and L2.

In simple terms:
• L1 and L2 can coordinate in the same transaction instead of acting more like separate networks
• Less fragmentation → Apps and liquidity across different Ethereum layers can work together more easily
• Better user experience → Cross-layer actions could become faster and simpler

Why does this matter?
Ethereum has many L2s, but liquidity and users are often split across them.

Atomic composability could help make these layers feel more like one connected Ethereum ecosystem.

This is only the first step, but it could be an important piece of Ethereum’s long-term scaling roadmap.

text:
Polymarket 5m 里，一个很容易被忽略的事实：

99c 也不稳。

如果每次同样买一份、持有到最终输赢结算、忽略费用：

0.99 买入，赢一次赚 0.01。
输一次，亏 0.99。

也就是：

一次全亏 = 99 次全赢。

这几天群里刚好出现了两类相反反馈：

一边是旧策略开始不出信号、反转越来越少；

另一边又有人在尾盘被突然反转打穿。

很多人真正低估的，可能不是参数误差，而是 regime 已经变了，旧参数还在继续跑。

更麻烦的是，实盘里还有另外两个“看起来已经确定”的假象。

一个是“买入成功”。

群友报告的一组实测：

买入回执后 8.7ms 卖出失败；
1.130s 仍失败；
1.319s 才成功。

但正确结论不是：

“那以后 sleep 1.5 秒就行。”

Polymarket 官方把交易状态分成：

MATCHED
MINED
CONFIRMED
RETRYING
FAILED

已撮合 ≠ 最终确认 ≠ 仓位已经可用。

如果 bot 的逻辑只是：

收到成功回执 → 等固定时间 → 反手卖

那么只要链上确认、余额更新或者重连状态发生变化，实盘就可能和测试完全不是一回事。

程序应该让订单状态、成交状态和实际可用余额决定下一步，而不是让固定 sleep 决定。

另一个假象是“刚收到的价格”。

WebSocket 本地刚收到，不等于市场刚发生。

Polymarket TWAP 会区分观察时间和转发时间，而且断线没有历史重放。

如果策略依赖开盘基准，就必须同时知道：

- 哪条 feed
- 30s 还是 60s
- 实际 observation time
- 本地 receive time

关键基准没拿到，宁可停一轮，也不要拿随后的一帧偷偷补上。

所以这期最后只留下三个判断：

1. 99c 不是保险，先算一次失败要吃掉多少次盈利。
2. 收到成交回执，不等于仓位已经可卖。
3. 刚收到的价格，不一定刚发生。

AI 可以帮你更快写出 bot。

但“结果是否确定、持仓是否可用、数据是否有效”，还是得分别拿证据。

New research 🚀 from the ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) team at Stanford

We took the failure lessons out of an LLM agent's memory, and it got better! 📈

Why? We find that failure recovery tips could hurt LLM agent performance when they sit in context all the time, even when nothing is going wrong.

So we build Sentry 🛡️: a test-time framework that recovers LLM agents from failures. It keeps failure knowledge outside the agent and only steps in when a failure actually happens.

On average: +39% over our own ACE, +37% over the best runtime-intervention baseline.

In most cases, we substantially outperform all other frontier models, Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, Veo 3.1 and Sora 2, Cosmos3.

The FLUX 3 base model outperforms all other foundation models, while FLUX 3 paired with a physics verification layer scores even higher.

The FLUX 3 backbone, with its strong physics understanding, gives FLUX 3 Action it’s strong action prediction for robotics, while also giving FLUX 3 Video physically accurate motion when you’re creating content, making ads, films and product shots.

The most common pushback I hear on @Collector_Crypt is that it's "jUsT a gAmBLiNg pLaTfOrm" and "gaChA iSnT suStAinAbLe"

It's simply just wrong, and the @Blockworks data proves it:

Start with the chart most people skip. Wallets holding at least one tokenized collectible, and this is with Gachapon wallets excluded. We are at 18,000+ wallets already, and the curve is steepening into October. 

Those wallets hold $28.9M of insured collectibles across 98,235 cards sitting in the vault right now.

More telling: wallets holding more than one card went from 3k to 8k this year. People aren't trying it once and leaving. They're accumulating.

But the strongest signal is redemptions.

Redeeming means burning the NFT and having the physical card shipped to your door. It's the most expensive, least liquid, most committed action available on the platform. A gambler never does this. A gambler flips and moves on.

Redemptions just hit an all-time high of $1.7M in a single week, at roughly $8k average per wallet.

People are taking real cards home, actual collectors do collect.

Then look at what they actually hold. Across 18,202 wallets and 98,235 cards, average card value scales from $52 in the smallest portfolios to $3,451 in the largest. A 66x step-up. Collectors moving up tiers aren't buying more volume, but they're buying better cards. That's exactly what a real collector does.

633 wallets hold a card worth over $1,000. Two hold cards worth $1M. Shout out to @charred_io here.

To sum it up: the gacha has just been the Trojan horse to get enough supply onchain to attract the right collectors. 

What's actually happening though is what's always been the bullcase from day 1: Collector slowly but surely becoming the superior marketplace that collectors trust and collect on.

text:
I had my first lucid dream. I was 30 years younger and noticed someone I love on a date with someone and they were arguing or having a bad night. I was so stoked to realize I was dreaming and I jumped up and ran over and decided to conjure an object (something you MUST try). I produced an iPhone and showed this person photos of them now.

I said "don't worry about what is going on here. This is future you. She's not here and look how happy you are. Future you is calling! It just does NOT MATTER". 

It was like talking to the founding fathers about dinosaurs though. He was obsessed with the iPhone and its magic. Understandably so. He didn't believe me or the object in my hand but I convinced him I was some kind of time traveler and he just needed to let it all go. 

What I also realized, is this is great advice in general. Go back in time and show yourself during the hard times how you endured. Cheer yourself on from the future. Show yourself an iPhone and marvel at our abilities. 

Marvel at the privilege of being able to have life and be upset at all. 

It's definitely one of the coolest dreams I've ever had.

text:
看完 #OKXNOW 的直播，我最大的感受是：AI 对 OKX 来说，已经不是“锦上添花”的工具，而是在进入业务底层。
直播中提到，OKX 每月在 AI 上的投入已达到千万美元级别。这个数字背后，更值得关注的不是预算本身，而是 OKX 正把 AI 逐步融入研发、运营、产品设计和用户体验中——AI 正成为平台能力的一部分。
OKX 从来不只把自己定义为一家交易所。
从 13 年前与 Crypto 一起起步，到现货、衍生品、Web3、自托管钱包、支付，以及全球化服务布局，交易所更像是 OKX 的起点，而不是终点。正如 Star 在演讲中传递的意思：交易所只是入口，未来真正要构建的是更开放、更智能的金融基础设施。
Crypto 的发展也正处在新的阶段。
它最初是一场关于自由、密码学和价值传递方式的社会实验；后来有了交易所、ICO、DeFi、稳定币、链上金融和合规化进程；如今，越来越多传统机构开始认真研究、配置和参与 Crypto。
这不只是“机构资金进场”，更意味着 Crypto 正在被主流金融体系重新理解。全球支付、资产代币化、价值流动和金融服务的边界，都可能因此被重写。
更值得期待的是，互联网、Crypto 与 AI 正在开始汇流：
互联网让信息全球连接；
Crypto 让价值能够全球流动、透明结算并被编程；
AI 则让复杂服务变得更智能、更个性化、更低门槛。
未来，每个人或许都会拥有属于自己的 AI Banker。
它不只是回答行情、推送资讯，而是能够理解你的现金流、风险偏好和长期目标，动态协助你进行资产规划与决策管理。过去只有高净值人群才能获得的定制化金融服务，未来有可能借助 AI 走向更多普通用户。
但金融创新越快，信任就越重要。
技术可以改变效率，金融最终仍然建立在信任之上。合规、风控、审计、治理和机构级基础设施，并不是创新的对立面，而是 Crypto 真正走向主流的前提。
看完直播，我理解 #OKXNOW 释放的信号很清晰：
AI 正在改变人们工作的方式。
Crypto 正在改变金钱运行的方式。
而 OKX 想参与构建的，是两者融合后的下一代金融体验。
未来不是正在路上。
未来，已经 NOW。

quoted_text:
OpenAI Dots is insane for building a 24/7 AI company...

I mapped the whole OpenAI Dots architecture into one paper: agents, models, tools, memory, delegation, guardrails and the revenue layer.

Here are the 10 steps:

step 1 → stop treating Dots like a chatbot. each Dot runs in a persistent cloud environment with its own browser, terminal, files, memory and scheduled execution. close the laptop and the workflow keeps moving

step 2 → hire by responsibility. give every Dot one clear domain, dedicated sources, a working style, an approval boundary and a trigger. a "general helper" has no role, only undefined context

step 3 → make one Dot the orchestrator. you give it the objective, it decomposes the work, delegates to specialized agents, checks their outputs and merges everything into one deliverable

step 4 → stop being the courier between agents. with isolated delegation, each worker gets only the context and tools it needs, executes in its own environment, then returns a structured result to the orchestrator

step 5 → connect the real business stack: cloud browser sessions, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, internal dashboards and APIs. a Dot without tools is still just a conversational layer

step 6 → put the company on a clock. recurring routines and event triggers turn one-off tasks into persistent operations. research, monitoring, reporting and pipeline checks can run while nobody is online

step 7 → automate the reversible, gate the irreversible. let agents read, research, analyze and draft autonomously, but require human approval before messages send, money moves, records change or production code ships

step 8 → route intelligence by cost. keep the strongest model on orchestration, conflict resolution and final audits, and let cheaper high-context models handle background research, classification and repetitive execution

step 9 → give the company shared memory. project specs, approved claims, pricing, decisions and requirements live in one persistent workspace, so every agent works from the same source of truth instead of rebuilding context from old chats

step 10 → connect the loop to revenue. research finds the signal, outreach creates the opportunity, execution moves the work forward, analytics measures the result and monitoring discovers the next action

AI stops being something you open when you need an answer. It becomes an operating layer that keeps economically useful work moving after you log off.

text:
$BTDR outperforming most neos and powered shell cos this morning in a weak tape. Some of that is BTC exposure, but some may be the loan Bitdeer's tenant launched today -->

Background: Bitdeer leased its Tydal site in Norway to Volta for 16 years, ~$4.7B of rent (though Volta can leave for free after year 10; there's also an 8-year renewal option.) Volta is a GPU cloud startup founded this year by ex-Brookfield execs and backed by a16z, Altimeter, Nvidia and Michael Dell's family office. It rents the GPUs at Tydal to Anthropic on a 6-year, $10B deal (per Bloomberg).

Today Volta started raising ~$5B with JPM and GS at talk of roughly 11%.

>Part buys the GPUs
>Part is cash parked with banks, who promise Bitdeer up to ~$1.3B of rent if Volta doesn't pay. That's about half of the first 10 years of rent
>(Volta's GPU loan is 6-years against a 6 year Anthropic contract, so Volta's lenders get repaid out of Anthropic's checks.)

Bitdeer's side:
>All in, we estimate Bitdeer will have put ~$700-900M into Tydal counting the purchase, the money spent building it out for BTC mining before the pivot, and the ~$500M left to finish. 
>Rent averages ~$260M a year after operating costs, so roughly a 30% annual return and a 3-4 year payback 
>Bitdeer should now be able borrow inside Volta's 11% since banks now cover half  and the asset has less terminal value uncertainty than GPUs themselves. 
>My guess is 8.5-10%. Cipher got ~7%, but it had Google behind it
>Rate sensitivity: Every extra 1% costs ~$45M of borrowing room and ~$10M a year of interest on a ~$1B loan
>The bigger swing is how many years lenders will count. If they lend against Volta's full 10-year commitment, Bitdeer can borrow ~$1B, about double what's left to build. If they only count the bank-backed years, it's closer to $600M

Risk left:
>Getting built on time. First half due end of 2026, rest by March 2027
>Years 7-10: Anthropic has to renew or Volta needs a new customer for 6-year old chips; Volta can walk for free after year 10

Easiest ways for BTDR to close the valuation gap with peers:
>Close the Tydal debt and print the terms. Size, rate, length, and how much cash comes back to the parent
>Put out one table per site every quarter with MW leased, term, $/kW, credit support, total invested, spend left and delivery dates. We had to guess at Tydal's all-in cost to write this. Peers get paid a higher multiple partly because you can model them.
>Clean up the cash flow statement and the related party borrowings
>Sign lease #2.

text:
我一直认为，＃牛来 后面大概率还会有行情。

那为什么现在反而跌？

其实大家可以回头看看 ＃币安人生、＃GIGGLE 这类高热度Meme走过的路。

越是所有人都看好的币，越不容易让你舒舒服服拿到主升浪。

因为共识太强的时候，最大的问题不是没人买，而是想赚钱的人太多了，而且仓位一个比一个重。

上线就几十万、上百万刀往里干，觉得“这东西肯定涨”；胆子再大一点的，现货还嫌慢，直接高倍杠杆梭进去。

这种盘面怎么直接拉？

真直接拉了，相当于所有人坐好轿子等着抬，市场反而缺少足够的换手。

所以很多高共识Meme启动之前，最折磨人的阶段往往就是：跌、震荡、插针、反复磨。

把高杠杆打掉，把短线客洗出去，把追高盘磨到怀疑人生，让筹码重新换手。

等到最开始喊“必涨”的人开始怀疑，重仓的人开始减仓，杠杆被清得差不多，盘面反而轻了。

所以我看 ＃牛来，现在的下跌并没有直接改变我的判断。

当然，洗盘不是上涨的保证，下跌也不能自动解释成洗盘。最终还是要看成交量、筹码结构、社区热度和资金有没有重新回来。

但如果一个币共识还在、流动性还在、关注度还在，那么真正值得观察的，往往不是它顺风顺水的时候，而是它把最坚定的那批人都快折磨到动摇的时候。

市场最喜欢干的一件事，就是先把“肯定会涨的人”折磨到不敢肯定，再开始真正的行情。

Base builders ship hard

Here's 25 things the Base ecosystem launched and announced in September

1) @aave listed Coinbase Tokenized Stocks. Holders can deposit stocks on Base as collateral and borrow USDC against them on Aave V4

2) @modveon launched Sivar. Now Salvadorans can send money between the US and El Salvador at low cost, with instant transfers that settle in seconds on Base

3) @Cloudflare opened a closed beta of its Monetization Gateway. APIs on Cloudflare can charge agents per request, settled in USDC on Base

4) Coinbase partnered with @Citi to bring stablecoin acceptance to Base, letting institutions take stablecoin payments on regulated rails with automatic fiat settlement

5) 10 teams were selected for Base Batches 004 out of 750+ applicants: @bitrepo_xyz, @contavcbr, @flovia402, @greekdotfi, @get_grow_app, @mercatus_ai, @rennfinance, @saturdaybank, @tribeca_xyz, and @ledig_tech

6) @catalystmkts_ launched markets on Base for whether an event happens, starting with social interactions and expanding to listings, launches, news, and onchain events

7) @verantaxyz launched 39 new assets on Veranta and Base. Traders can trade them with up to 25x leverage, including 26 assets that were not tradable onchain

8) @2factorfinance launched its public beta on Base. Long-term holders can hold moderate leverage indefinitely, first on Bitcoin and then on Coinbase Tokenized Stocks, at a fraction of what a leveraged ETF costs to carry

9) @avantprotocol launched Avant on Base, onchain infrastructure for productive capital. It starts by bringing that capital into @morpho lending markets

10) @alchemixfi launched Alchemix V3 on Base. Users can now deposit once and earn with no lock-up, borrow against that money with no interest while it keeps earning, or lock in a fixed return

11) @upshift_fi is live on Base with @clearstarlabs. Curators, fintechs, and asset managers can launch vaults, and depositors keep their own funds. The first vault lets XRP holders earn on cbXRP in @morpho lending markets

12) @revertfinance launched Revert Rewards on Base. Liquidity providers can open a position in the tokenized stock pools on @aeroxyz, set a price range, and track the fees hour by hour

13) @clearstarlabs added cbZEC and cbHYPE to its cbAssets Vault on Base. Both markets are live in its largest vault on @morpho

14) @o1_exchange launched tax tokens on its launchpad on Base. Creators can set a buy and sell tax from 1% to 10% and route it to themselves, to holders as dividends paid in the paired asset, or to burns

15) @zothdotio expanded zPayments on Base, a stablecoin settlement platform for businesses. Businesses can pay out in local currency across 171 countries, at one stated rate, with instant settlement

16) @munifyai is now on Base. People can receive, hold, spend, and move dollars in one account with USDC on Base

17) @rifthq released an onchain API, letting users send money to a deposit address while it runs the swap, bridge, or deposit, including routes to Base

18) @morpho introduced P2P Orders for Midnight on Base, letting you set your own terms from the fixed-rate app

author: ClemToune
quoted_text:
after roughly 12 days, I finished some serious and really promising Bend work which I think is a good example as to how this kind of stuff can be used going forward. I made a formal program of SSZ (The Ethereum's CL encoding) inspired by the fastssz Go's implementation. It uses codegen to generate  the data structures from a yaml file alongside proofs for their setters, encoders, decoders and hashers.

The initial spec I wrote myself (assisted obviously by AI) alongside the initial generators. then I let implementation and optimization side being done by Karpathy inspired AutoResearch loops.

As a third final step, I wired a bunch of auditors agents running GLM-5.3 (thanks @AnthropicAI for the heads up) to find vulnerabilities/proof gaps (mutate impl and see if proofs find it) until none could be found anymore. as I am writting this, GLM cannot literally find gaps or vulnerabilities anymore even after running for 8 hours straight (decode/encode/hashing wise) and it literally gave up on the codec paths. Performance wise it is FASTER than fastssz across decoding and encoding (with hash_tree_root being the only thing that is slower sitting at 5x). I also decided just for the meme to put it inside of Prysm and it works! you can literally use this as your SSZ library inside an actual client via FFI (obv. slower than just fastssz in this case) and can be trivially compiled to RiscV as well. I also realized that the whole infrastucture built could probably formally verify stuff not only in Bend but Lean as well and all other proof checkers (however I did not try it yet). screenshot is prysm running bend-ssz via FFI and posting more info down in a thread.

author: bigironchris
quoted_text:
Sage by @LevantoLabs is the first decision model, launched in July, and currently the best on the market.

It wins across all the evals proposed by @perplexity_ai's CEO (nice job @AravSrinivas!), and it's first on JevBench, beating Jev and Google's models on every dimension.

BUT frankly, benchmarks are not what excites us.
I'm BORED by the dozens of new decision models launching every day with a tiny +0.02 on some eval. They all look the same.

The magic is somewhere else.
There are thousands of new things that could be invented in the space of decision models and models for machines. The invention space is huge!

After launching Sage, we also pioneered:

- The first guardrails and model routers built on decision models

- Automated context engineering with "grounding" (automatic web search when confidence is low). Decision models are only as smart as their context, especially because they can't make tool calls.

- Reasoning. In many use cases you don't know whether your question is System 1 or System 2. With reasoning, the model is as fast as a System 1 model when the question is System 1, and takes more time when it's needed. This enables hard, multi-step decisions. Our clients just want the correct answer, and in some use cases they're happy to wait 0.5s more. This will soon become the market standard (GLiDE/@george_onx and @TypeLLM already followed).

And *so* much is yet to come. Models for machines: it's just the beginning!

We're cooking. Follow @levantolabs for new product primitives that will surprise you.

Open innovation is HEALTHY.
Competition is HEALTHY.
Benchmark-race is BORING.
Product inventions are FUN.

Go go go!!!

Use a swarm of crawlers to scrape crypto and Web3 websites, then use the collected content to train an open-source large language model from scratch that has only been exposed to crypto-related content.

CRAWL is the associated token, used to pay for generating crawlers and to distribute a share of the fees.

Here’s how the mechanism works:

The crawlers do the work. Each crawler is a headless browser powered by a DeepSeek agent that navigates real websites, reading whitepapers, documentation, governance pages, code, and other content. It keeps only pages relevant to crypto and Web3 and discards everything unrelated.

The data is then sent to “Queen.” All the content collected by the crawlers is cleaned, deduplicated, and tokenized before being aggregated into Queen’s training dataset. Queen is the model they intend to train.

Users who want to participate can burn approximately 1 million CRAWL tokens to generate a crawler registered under their name. Twenty percent of the creator fees are distributed equally among crawler owners every 24 hours, with payments made in SOL. The remaining 80% is used to cover crawling costs and GPU training.

The website allows users to watch in real time which page each crawler is reading. Once training is complete, the model weights are planned to be published on Hugging Face, with contributors credited.

In short, CRAWLNET can be understood as an experiment in “publicly crawling crypto websites → accumulating training data → training a specialized small model,” combined with a token mechanism in which users burn tokens to obtain a share of crawler ownership and receive a portion of the fees.

text:
Introducing gdp-ts: Ghosts of Departed Proofs for TypeScript.

gdp-ts is a library, linter and AI skill for safer API design. Under this contract, sensitive functions require 'proofs' that the caller performed an authorization check.

The typechecker verifies these proofs at compile time, preventing your team and agents from shipping catastrophic security (and other kinds of) bugs.

While these patterns have existed for quite some time, especially in ecosystems like Haskell, ① human code review and ② cognitive and syntactic overhead made these solutions niche.

The situation is now inverted. Agents are writing more code than we can review, and they *thrive* in tight loops with hard constraints that would frustrate us. We see this with the rise of Rust, borrow checker, code aesthetics debate and all.

The README and examples model a real-world Vercel API product constraint: changing the password on a Project requires a proof of a certain role + a certain entitlement. Thanks to Matt Noonan and Ollie Charles for their research in this space.

text:
Sage by @LevantoLabs is the first decision model, launched in July, and currently the best on the market.

It wins across all the evals proposed by @perplexity_ai's CEO (nice job @AravSrinivas!), and it's first on JevBench, beating Jev and Google's models on every dimension.

BUT frankly, benchmarks are not what excites us.
I'm BORED by the dozens of new decision models launching every day with a tiny +0.02 on some eval. They all look the same.

The magic is somewhere else.
There are thousands of new things that could be invented in the space of decision models and models for machines. The invention space is huge!

After launching Sage, we also pioneered:

- The first guardrails and model routers built on decision models

- Automated context engineering with "grounding" (automatic web search when confidence is low). Decision models are only as smart as their context, especially because they can't make tool calls.

- Reasoning. In many use cases you don't know whether your question is System 1 or System 2. With reasoning, the model is as fast as a System 1 model when the question is System 1, and takes more time when it's needed. This enables hard, multi-step decisions. Our clients just want the correct answer, and in some use cases they're happy to wait 0.5s more. This will soon become the market standard (GLiDE/@george_onx and @TypeLLM already followed).

And *so* much is yet to come. Models for machines: it's just the beginning!

We're cooking. Follow @levantolabs for new product primitives that will surprise you.

Open innovation is HEALTHY.
Competition is HEALTHY.
Benchmark-race is BORING.
Product inventions are FUN.

Go go go!!!

text:
这两天不少人私信问我 @safetrade 上的低市值“欢乐豆”，干脆把我了解的项目整理一下：主网上线时间较新、体量较小，主要在 SafeTrade 能交易。

涨跌别问我，我也不知道。我只知道，Safetrade上币都是免费的，既然他们选择list，那或许会有一些亮点，而在研究后，我知道这些项目谁在背后，这些信息或许对你有帮助，但只是研究线索，绝对不是投资推荐。

1｜Qubitcoin qubitcoin-2:native @qubitcoinx

做量子电路模拟挖矿的 BTC 分叉。创始人 @MYShalaginov 有 MIT 博士后及量子光学、纳米光子学研究经历，科研背景很不错。

不过，我对他在项目上的持续投入经历抱有疑问。我看过的他自己主持的播客，没见过他提自己的项目。创始人背景这么好，如果能把更多精力放在建设上自己的项目就更好了。

流通市值约 $1.54M｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $14M

2｜Parano1d $NOID @Parano1dComm

通过递归证明验证链状态，以 PoW 确定顺序，尝试减少新节点对完整历史重放的依赖。

开发者 @ignotus_nemo 未实名，但从公开文章和以太坊论坛的讨论看，我个人觉得是想认真做事的，技术方向也有些意思。

我的个人经历比较惨：早期挖过几万个，低位也买过一点，结果 0.01 多就卖了，最近看着上涨，拍断大腿。

流通市值750K｜无固定发行上限，需结合排放计划评估后续稀释与抛压

3｜NeptuneCash $NPT @NeptuneCash

主打隐私和抗量子方向的 PoW 公链，核心设计包括 STARK 零知识证明和 Mutator Sets。

核心开发者包括 @aszepieniec、@ThorkilVaerge。经历25年社区分叉后，项目仍在持续建设，我一直比较关注它的技术路线，技术开发依然活跃。

流通市值560K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $5.5M

4｜Neptune Privacy neptune-privacy:native @NeptunePrivacy

2025 年从 NPT 社区分叉出来的项目，分歧主要围绕代币发行模型和发展路线。

开发方向包括 L2“利维坦”，实际交付还需继续跟踪。就我的观察，社区在传播和推广上更积极，也已经上了 MEXC。

流通市值约 $625K｜无固定发行上限，需结合排放计划评估后续稀释与抛压

5｜Compute Substrate $CSD

一个挺有个性的“链上公共建议箱”：让人或程序提交想法、表达支持，形成可复核的排行榜。

链只记录支持，不判断观点真假，也不替参与者执行决定。更像一个协调与公共记录的应用协议实验，而不是又一条泛用公链。

协议发起者 @matsjulner，也可以关注 @Cairn_substrate、@0xInverse 生态开发者账号。

流通市值约 $17K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $300K

6｜Midstate $MDS @cypherpunkgold

以 BLAKE3、哈希签名和顺序 PoW 为基础，走抗量子电子现金方向。

可关注 @phraudsta 的公开内容，以及他的播客 https://t.co/KmNeYBkI2C。Dev行文有密码朋克色彩，但真实职业履历仍未确认，推特号倒是粉丝不少，有一些加密OG关注和互动。

流通市值约 $21K｜FDV约 $68K

7｜Parallax $LAX @prlxchain

ETN 生态开发者 @andre_patta 发起的新项目，采用 XHash PoW，支持 EVM 智能合约。

这个在我这里更偏“欢乐豆”观察仓：先看开发者有没有持续交付，以及网络和生态能不能慢慢做起来。

行情站流通市值约 $12K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $86K

另外还有 @Kvanta5_QR，也是抗量子方向，但开发者身份和项目沿革仍有待核实，据说是 @BitcoincashII 的同一个人 ，不知道Safetrade觉得他哪方面有亮点，还不清楚。

以上就这些，全部免费分享，祝你们好运。

text:
This direction is what I'd dub "Private trains, public rails". The goal is the best network for assets to be issued, held and used, with value accruing to the network as a whole and ETH.

Ethereum is a confirmation engine. CCIP v1 already waited for Ethereum finality, but Chainlink nodes still had to report the result themselves. That is the pragmatic choice when proving Ethereum's consensus on another chain isn't practical. With zk-powered light clients, the bridge can verify Ethereum's confirmation directly instead of relying on someone's report of it.

Plugging these proofs into the bridge is enabled by the modular architecture of CCIP 2.0, also present in LayerZero. It unbundles the transport layer of the bridge from its application services, such as token issuance, standards and business logic, compliance or other features.

But it's only an attractive proposition if the Ethereum settlement layer is fast, cheap and secure, otherwise the temptation is great to use an alternative with different trade-offs. FCR is another step in this direction.

Zooming out, it starts to show what is imo the right balance between private and public build-out of Ethereum.

- Canonical bridges tying L2s to L1 remain the least featureful and most neutral, but the most secure way to move assets between L1 and L2s, especially ETH and other L1-native assets. They are privately built, but function more like public utilities: available, unattended, and secure, built on L1's settlement (finality or fast confirmation) and more and more on broadly available zk proofs.

- The utility exposed by these bridges becomes the root of trust for private operators offering differentiated services to asset issuers and other customers. Chainlink and others are well placed to serve their customers' business needs, relying on Ethereum's confirmation engine for the rails on which assets run.

Ethlabs is helping to build the public rails: fast, cheap and secure settlement across L1 and L2s, with value accruing to Ethereum and ETH.
author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
It’s very cool to see more zk tech hardening bridges! zk does two things here: it proves that a fact of a world in a remote chain is part of that chain's state, and that this fact of the world is the one everybody agrees happened in the first place, ruling out double spends.

This is already a major improvement, and I'd like to talk about where we could go even further..

Today, and in this @chainlink CCIP 2.0 module, the @SuccinctLabs light client proves that Ethereum finality was achieved (“everybody agrees this version of the world happened”), by proving the report from a small validator subcommittee known as the “sync committee”. Finality is the ultimate agreement. However Ethereum finality still takes about 15 minutes!

Meanwhile, FCR is a snapshot of that agreement with very strong guarantees, at low latency. Now what if you could put together the power of zk and the power of FCR together to reduce by 30x that latency? Turns out, this may be possible! We mentioned it briefly in our weekly update two weeks ago https://t.co/2SVmcO5Bjt

Can we go even further? There are two complementary boosts:

1. Extending state inclusion proofs to full validity proofs. You're then not just proving that the state reported by validators includes data about your bridge transfer. You're proving validity of the entire remote chain's execution! No chance for validators to fool you.

2. Reducing time-to-finality. FCR is great, and will be a great bridge (pun intended) until we get really low latency finality, in the order of tens of seconds. Eventually, we'll get that, as well as a full proof that this finality was achieved, not relying on a subcommittee's report.

You put all this together, and you start to see the future of seamless and secure interoperability across Ethereum. Let's go build it!

text:
我们正站在稳定币超级周期的起点。
但坏消息是，美元稳定币早已是一片红海。

Tether 与 Circle 构成的双寡头格局，让所有后来者望而却步。
供应量上，USDT 与 USDC 合计占稳定币总市值约 83%；
使用量上，仅 USDT 就占据 CEX 交易量的 73.6%；
盈利能力上，Tether 年净利润已超过百亿美元，其美债持仓规模位列全球第 17，超过多数主权国家。
今天想在美元稳定币市场挑战这两大巨头，难度不亚于在 2010 年重新打造一个 Facebook。

然而，这个看似固化的市场中，还隐藏着一个被绝大多数人忽视的机会。
目前，约 99.5% 的稳定币都以美元为支撑。
换句话说，所有非美元货币在链上的份额加起来还不到 0.5%。这是一整片尚未被开垦的大陆。
真正的问题只有两个：
▌哪种非美元货币值得被搬上链？
▌应该用什么机制将它搬上链？

作为目前规模最大的瑞士法郎稳定币，@frankencoinzchf 给出了自己的答案。
Frankencoin 于 2023 年上线，从未脱锚，目前已部署在 8 条链上，TVL 超过 6300 万美元。
10 月 8 日，稳定币 ZCHF 上线 Kraken。目前支持的交易对为 ZCHF/USD、ZCHF/CHF, 对于 Frankencoin 来说，这是一个里程碑式的时刻。

1/ 为什么是瑞士法郎？
稳定币锚定哪种法币，本质上是在替持有者选择一条长期购买力曲线。
过去 50 多年里，美元对瑞士法郎累计贬值约 80%。瑞郎能够长期保持强势，背后有几个重要原因：
瑞士央行长期奉行克制的货币政策；
瑞士拥有长期低通胀的传统；
政治中立、财政稳健、法治健全，使瑞郎具备天然的避险货币属性。
因此，持有 USDT 十年和持有 ZCHF 十年，最终的购买力差距可能相当可观。

2/ 为什么是 Frankencoin？
大多数美元稳定币，本质上是美元资产的代币化包装。
Circle、Tether 等中心化发行商持有美国国债等储备资产，再在链上发行对应的稳定币。用户真正信任的，依然是背后的发行机构。

Frankencoin 选择了完全不同的路径。
没有中心化发行方；
由链上资产超额抵押；
抵押品包括 BTC、ETH、代币化黄金和代币化股票；
整个系统去中心化运行，储备与规则均可链上验证。
它更接近 DAI 的模式，只不过锚定的不是美元，而是瑞士法郎。

对于加密原生用户来说，无需信任中心化机构并非附加功能，而是产品最核心的价值之一。
在机制设计上，Frankencoin 由两个核心代币组成。
▌ZCHF 是稳定币本身，可用于支付、储蓄和借贷。
▌FCS 代表储备池的所有权份额。协议收入归 FCS 沉淀在储备池，同时 FCS 持有者也拥有协议治理权。
一个负责提供稳定价值，另一个负责承接协议收益与治理权，两者共同构成 Frankencoin 的经济系统。

3/ Frankencoin 真正瞄准的市场
必须承认，Frankencoin 不会与 USDT、USDC 正面争夺交易流动性。
属于它的战场在别处。
它瞄准的，是美元稳定币双寡头在结构上难以覆盖的三类需求。
长期购买力保值；
去中心化与抗审查；
真实的瑞士法郎支付需求。
如果用一句话概括，美元稳定币是链上的现金流货币，瑞郎稳定币则更像链上的避险储蓄账户。
二者并不是非此即彼的替代关系，而是服务于不同场景的互补关系。

当稳定币超级周期真正展开，市场终将意识到，稳定币的多元化，不仅意味着发行方的多元化，更意味着底层计价货币的多元化。

Sage by @LevantoLabs is the first decision model, launched in July, and currently the best on the market.

It wins across all the evals proposed by @perplexity_ai's CEO (nice job @AravSrinivas!), and it's first on JevBench, beating Jev and Google's models on every dimension.

BUT frankly, benchmarks are not what excites us.
I'm BORED by the dozens of new decision models launching every day with a tiny +0.02 on some eval. They all look the same.

The magic is somewhere else.
There are thousands of new things that could be invented in the space of decision models and models for machines. The invention space is huge!

After launching Sage, we also pioneered:

- The first guardrails and model routers built on decision models

- Automated context engineering with "grounding" (automatic web search when confidence is low). Decision models are only as smart as their context, especially because they can't make tool calls.

- Reasoning. In many use cases you don't know whether your question is System 1 or System 2. With reasoning, the model is as fast as a System 1 model when the question is System 1, and takes more time when it's needed. This enables hard, multi-step decisions. Our clients just want the correct answer, and in some use cases they're happy to wait 0.5s more. This will soon become the market standard (GLiDE/@george_onx and @TypeLLM already followed).

And *so* much is yet to come. Models for machines: it's just the beginning!

We're cooking. Follow @levantolabs for new product primitives that will surprise you.

Open innovation is HEALTHY.
Competition is HEALTHY.
Benchmark-race is BORING.
Product inventions are FUN.

Go go go!!!

text:
the reaction should *not* be "airdrops are dead" btw

i think we simply move from lots of instant jeet airdrops to fewer but much larger ones

that changes the flow of capital quite a bit

fewer airdrops means fewer recurring wealth creation events across crypto and fewer good tokens means fewer places for that money to rotate into afterwards

less frequent liquidity creations + less asset supply = could make rotations slower while making the winners much bigger
author: 0xNairolf
quoted_text:
on airdrops and why they are less frequent:

first, airdrops are *the* single best community building tool crypto has ever created

you tease an airdrop to acquire users, then turn a percentage of them into actual supporters because they become financially + emotionally tied to the success of the product and most importantly, you put the asset directly in their hands

best growth hack, no debate on this

but the pre token phase is also basically easy mode for teams

users are willing to pay (high) fees, deposit capital, generate volume and juice every metric imaginable for the possibility of an allocation

you are basically getting paid to bootstrap your product

the problem is that this model has been abused to death

there are well over 20 teams still farming airdrop farmers after extracting $100m+ from them, while knowing perfectly well they will never launch a token because launching a token now comes with expectations they cant meet

people want revenue
people want buybacks
people want a fair distribution
people want the token to actually capture value

how many pre token products in crypto can deliver all of that today? 10? maybe less?

so you end up with a weird equilibrium

(i) the pre token phase is extremely profitable and low risk
(ii) the post token phase forces you to prove that your product is actually viable and that there is enough value creation to sustain a token

this is why you are getting fewer airdrops and fewer TGEs

tldr: airdrops are disappearing because they worked too well while the bar for launching a good token became much higher

less TGEs is the natural outcome

text:
单 Agent 无法解决大工程问题，但把多个 Agent 放在一个群里对话，往往只会得到无限复读和互相推诿。多智能体协同（MAS）的本质是分布式系统架构与通信协议设计。

这里最近在做多 agent 的时候看到的一份《Multi-Agent 协作架构与通信协议策展蓝图》：

├── 01 组织拓扑与协调架构（Coordination Topology）
│   ├── 主从分级架构（Hierarchical / Supervisor Pattern）
│   │   ├── 单一 Router / Supervisor Agent 拆解任务并分发子任务
│   │   └── 聚合器（Aggregator）整合各个 Worker 的独立输出
│   ├── 对等协作（Peer-to-Peer / Network Pattern）
│   │   ├── 去中心化动态交接（Dynamic Handoff / Transfer Routing）
│   │   └── 对话轮转控制（Speaker Selection Strategy）
│   ├── 流水线编排（Sequential Pipeline）
│   │   └── 严格 SOP 模式（如 MetaGPT：产品经理 → 架构师 → 工程师 → 测试）
│   └── 共享黑板架构（Blackboard Architecture）
│       └── 所有 Agent 读写全局只读/更新日志，基于事件订阅触发动作
│
├── 02 通信协议与数据格式（Communication Protocols）
│   ├── 结构化消息契约（Contract Design）
│   │   ├── 禁止使用自然语言闲聊：强制使用统一 JSON/Pydantic 协议
│   │   ├── 核心字段：`sender`, `recipient`, `intent`, `payload`, `state_version`
│   │   └── 消息修剪（Message Pruning）：历史轮次压缩，防止 Token 膨胀
│   └── 异步事件驱动（Async Message Bus）
│       ├── Redis Streams / NATS / RabbitMQ 支持高并发 Agent 交互
│       └── 状态快照与会话挂起恢复
│
├── 03 冲突消解与共识机制（Consensus & Debate）
│   ├── 多 Agent 辩论（Multi-Agent Debate / Exchange-of-Thought）
│   │   ├── 正反方角色设定与相互对抗
│   │   └── 裁判节点基于证据打分进行裁决
│   ├── 投票机制（Voting & Quorum）
│   │   ├── 多数表决 vs 加权表决（根据 Agent 擅长领域赋权）
│   └── 反思与自我修正环（Reflexion Cycle）
│
├── 04 故障恢复与死锁预防（Fault Tolerance）
│   ├── 死循环侦测：基于图周期的 Loop Detector（限制最大回环次数）
│   ├── 认知死锁破除：当两个 Agent 互相推脱时，触发超时与人工旁路介入
│   └── 状态回滚机制（State Rollback / SAGA Pattern）
│
└── 05 评测与可扩展性（Benchmarking & Scalability）
    ├── 通信开销比率：完成单项任务消耗的 Token 总量与轮数
    ├── 协同增益率（Collaboration Gain）：多 Agent 表现是否显著优于单 Agent
    └── 标准评测集：GAIA, ChatDev Benchmark, SWE-bench Team Edition

text:
Following last week’s infrastructure investigation, MetaMask Staking has nearly completed processing the exit of its Lido validators without incident. The exited ETH will continue its re-entry to the Lido protocol over the coming weeks. The operator disclosed the issue early and acted quickly, which kept the impact to stETH holders minimal.

As the final set of validators are completing their exits, stETH APR is 2.23% - at or above where it has been since August. stETH rewards come from a diverse set of over 600 independent Node Operators across the Curated and Community Staking Modules, so a precautionary exit by one of the larger operators in the protocol has a limited effect on total rewards. The recent reduction in the Ethereum entry queue also means newly staked ETH starts earning sooner, netting more rewards for all Lido stakers.

MetaMask Staking will publish a comprehensive post-mortem in the coming weeks.

Thanks to the community for your trust and confidence to keep Ethereum staking simple, secure, and decentralized.
author: LidoFinance
quoted_text:
Following an investigation into an infrastructure compromise, MetaMask Staking (ex Consensys Staking) has taken precautionary steps to protect client assets related to its operated Ethereum validators.

These steps include exiting its Ethereum (ETH) validators in the Lido protocol, and will likely incur foregone rewards as well as possible downtime penalties should validators be taken offline in the near future to reduce risks related to potential network penalties. Relevant validators have begun the exit process, with the final validators expected to be exited (but not fully withdrawn) by the end of October 7th, 2026.

No action is required from stETH holders. ETH exited from MetaMask Staking-operated validators is expected to return to the protocol gradually as the relevant validators complete the exit, withdrawal, and re-entry cycle, which is estimated to take approximately up to 45 days due to the extended entry queue. As a reminder, staking operations are non-custodial in nature and MetaMask does not manage withdrawal keys for staking on behalf of clients.

As always, the Lido Protocol’s diverse Node Operator set and other security systems including the ad hoc reserve fund (of over 6,750 stETH), are designed to contain and mitigate disruptions to the normal operations of the protocol, in addition to other potential routes.

https://t.co/bZZU5oNlWp

A full investigation is underway, and further updates will be shared as they become available. For further details, please refer to the MetaMask Staking release linked below.

text:
有一种观点认为，人类会朝两极分化：大部分人继续沉迷于 AI 生成内容和“奶头乐”产品，小部分人则会借助 AI 极大丰富自己的创造力。

我觉得还有第三种观点值得认可：这种技术的加速主义会导致越来越多的大众开始思考，在很长一段时间之内，他们人生中真正值得去做的事情。所以最终，这反而会加速“奶头乐”产品的灭亡。AI 生成短剧就是一个比较明显的例子。如果在一个完全竞争的市场当中，制造 AI 短剧的成本越来越低，最终会往两个方向发展：

第一个方向是大量低内容、低质量的 AI slop 类型短剧。这种短剧很显然在火爆一阵子之后会彻底沉寂，因为内容的极大丰富实际上在提升所有人的审美（或者审丑）水平。

当然，我们也会看到一小部分创作者使用 AI 去创造很多优秀的、在现实社会当中不存在的精彩剧本。我觉得这一部分内容创作者的群体会越来越大，可以说是从零增长为一个不容忽视的内容分类分野。

Kernel agents can already beat hand-tuned kernels. Spinning up more agents is easy, but scaling GPU evaluation is still hard and expensive.

What happens when the agents scale faster than the GPUs?

Meet KCoral 🪸: a lightweight shared GPU benchmark environment for agentic kernel development.

🧑‍💻 Agents keep writing and revising code in their own workspace.
⚡ Evaluation is sent to KCoral, which schedules a shared GPU pool and returns correctness and timing.
🌐 Scale across multiple GPUs and nodes through a unified API endpoint.
🔒 Per-request isolation with only milliseconds of execution overhead.

By overlapping CPU compilation with GPU work across requests, KCoral further speeds up kernel evaluation. On a single NVIDIA B200, this translates to 2.58× the throughput of sequential local execution.

text:
The market data provider @massive_com recently started selling US stock data to AI agents one request at a time, paid in USDC, with no account and no API key (using @coinbase's x402 payment standard). As @kleffew94 mentioned in the partnership announcement, and I fully agree with, agents need real-time market data without the friction of API keys, subscriptions, or human provisioning. 

Market data has traditionally been licensed in advance: per seat for someone at a terminal, or under firm-level agreements for the systems trading on it. This model introduces a new kind of buyer: software that pays for a piece of data at the moment it needs it.

For that buyer, a price without reliable time context is incomplete. An agent receiving a single observation needs to know not just what the market said, but also exactly when it was true.

That makes timestamping part of the market-data infrastructure. Inside @TheHUB, packets are timestamped in hardware as they enter the network against a shared GPS-synchronized clock, creating a common time reference for the data moving through it.

text:
the main problem when you trade low caps is rugs. it's either a big win or a 0. so the #1 goal is not touching the rugs.

so i built a bot that spots rug pulls on robinhood chain before they dump. it saved me $30k of losses on tokens i'd probably have aped.

turns out the rugs aren't random. it's the same wallets, launch after launch.

the bot remembers every wallet that keeps buying early into launches that die, and flags the next one.

i backtested it. of the tokens still trading when it decided, 293 died within the hour. it had flagged 255 (87%).

flagged tokens died 55% of the time. unflagged: 3%. skip what it flags and your odds of buying a rug drop from 1 in 6 to 1 in 34.

how i'd use it day to day:
> let it run 24/7 on every new token
> pipe the verdicts to a telegram bot so they hit your phone
> skip everything it flags. no chart, no research, no fomo
> what's left is a short list. that's where the real work goes: lore, socials, who's behind it, is the community real

it doesn't pick winners. it tells you where your time is worth spending.

used @coingecko api to build this bot. the advantage is this api gives you the wallet behind every trade and every pool's real liquidity. so you see who's buying and whether the pool is already empty, not just a chart.

here's the repo to use the bot: https://t.co/zRBDuAXoRA
and the api key: https://t.co/JhMwdCSOrs

to use it, just:
> clone the repo and put your coingecko api key in .env (analyst plan or above)
> run python -m sniper collect
> let it run a few hours so it learns the wallets
> open the dashboard with python -m sniper web and check the verdict before you buy

A token launch platform built on Solana and powered by Orca DEX.

Traditional memecoin launches on Solana typically require completing a bonding curve first and then migrating to a DEX to create a liquidity pool. This can create issues such as opaque liquidity, migration risks, and limited fee distribution.

POD’s approach is different: users enter the name, ticker, and image, select a trading pair, and can create a real Orca Whirlpool pool in about one minute, with locked liquidity available for trading from the very first block.

The fixed fee is 2%, with 80% going to the creator side and 20% going to the platform. Creators can choose different “modules” to determine how their 80% is used.

For example:

Harbor: Send the fees directly to themselves or their team.
Undertow: Buy back and burn the token.
Reef: Deepen the locked liquidity pool.
Cargo: Use the fees to purchase tokenized stocks and distribute them to holders.

The platform currently supports pairing with SOL, USDC, ORCA, as well as hundreds of tokenized stocks.

Platform-related revenue is used to buy back and burn POD.

All tokens launched on the platform are permanently linked to POD. Cargo uses trading fees to purchase tokenized stocks and periodically airdrops them according to predefined rules to POD holders and holders of the corresponding Cargo token.

text:
papertrade launch details

papertrade is a fair launched smart contract exchange built on the hyperevm blockchain. as a fully onchain protocol, papertrade has significant advantages - decentralization, reliability, composability, transparency. it also has the usual onchain constraint - throughput. trades on papertrade are atomic opens/closes with no orderbook, so during normal trading sessions congestion will not be an issue. however, during launch we expect extreme chain congestion.

10.08.2026 - phase zero: predeposit only

two days before live trading begins, https://t.co/AdIx336QsD will open for user deposits. trading will be paused during this period. this allows separation of the deposit and account creation transactions from live trading. if a user does not complete these steps, they are likely to face long delays during launch, as active trading will be heavily prioritized over deposit processing. there is no further advantage to depositing earlier during this phase.

10.10.2026 - phase one: frontend only live trading

in order to prevent an onchain race and remove the incentive skew that mev creates, all transactions during the launch must go through the https://t.co/AdIx336QsD frontend, using the whitelisted relayers. the contract itself will not be open for direct interaction during this phase. this ensures that real frontend users are the first participants, flattening the technical skill curve as far as is appropriate.

during this phase, all trader activity on papertrade lives in an intent system, and carries a priority weighting. in almost all cases this ordering is done by transaction type and notional value, and is always indiscriminate of user/account. for instance, liquidations are more important than position opens and this is reflected in both activity types' respective weightings. that said the exact mechanics and weightings of the relayer intent system are adaptive, and will change over time as trader activity is processed. trades can be cancelled while still pending within the relayer intent system.

the paper token will begin minting on user losses at the start of live trading, from an initial supply of 0. it will not be transferable at the start beyond staking and unstaking, in order to encourage trading adoption and mitigate onchain congestion.

after launch - phase 2: open contract

once the launch congestion has passed and there is no longer any risk of mev wars, the papertrade smart contract will open up to everyone, allowing any human, contract or agent to write and receive an onchain atomic position. at this point papertrade becomes a fully decentralized, composable onchain liquidity primitive.

after launch - phase 3: builder codes

builder codes allow any frontend or router to receive the 1% frontend fee by sending trades to the papertrade smart contract, further decentralizing the protocol and incentivizing integration.

after launch - phase 4: token transferrability

at launch, paper will not be transferable. this is to encourage accumulation through trading participation and reduce onchain congestion load. transfers will be enabled after a sufficient period of time has passed.

even with this staged rollout, the launch congestion will be significant. expect lengthy confirmation delays during launch especially for smaller notional trades. predeposit if you want to trade at launch for the best chance at a smooth experience.

learn more about how papertrade works at: https://t.co/XCo1VHBoEe

The recent reduction in the Ethereum entry queue also means newly staked ETH starts earning sooner, netting more rewards for all Lido stakers.

MetaMask Staking will publish a comprehensive post-mortem in the coming weeks.

Thanks to the community for your trust and confidence to keep Ethereum staking simple, secure, and decentralized.

text:
关于少做「 咬牙坚持 」之事， 
我觉得 @variational_io 是个很好的案例。

这个项目为什么我能前后搞上一年半？ 
因为去年六月，我就窥探到了未来？  

咋可能嘛，哥们儿他喵的又不是先知， 
谁能想到这玩意儿能做到现在这么大？  

真正的原因其实只有一个，
那就是一路走来，它都是无情的印钞机， 
把它当交易工具来使用，全程都是正反馈。
一件每天都见得到现金利润的事儿，需要鸡毛个坚持？

而猿哥也从没藏着掖着，产品不同阶段，我把所有的商业判断和交易策略，都毫无保留地分享给了大家。  

今天对过往关键推文稍做整理，给自己的小农经济交易策略做个复盘，留作 TGE 前的纪念：  

1. 2025 年 6 月 5 日，在和团队深入交流了几次后，觉得产品设计颇为有趣，如果说 @Lighter_xyz 是卖订单流给 mm 的 robinhood 模式，那 @variational_io 则是连 citadel 的那份做市利润也想自己吃。

看懂这个之后，我发布了关于这个项目的第一篇研报，当年我视它为一座优雅的内循环赌场。
  https://t.co/PLU3mVIfiG 

记得那时整个平台的 OI 也就百来万，点差大到离谱，但他的资费机制特别奇怪， $BTC $ETH 大部分时间趴在零轴上下。  

所以我的策略很简单，找个正资费的所和它对着开，每天都在吃利息。  

而老天赏饭的地方在于，我配对的所是 var 和 lighter，当年只是想赚点儿小农经济的钱，没想到最后比起他俩的积分价值，那些资费，都是些可有可无的东西了。  

这里打住一下。  
那仨瓜俩枣的资费，真的是可有可无的吗？  

当然不是。  

如果没有资费收益的及时反馈，我根本不会去做这俩项目。正是因为有了现金流，这件事儿才是件不需要坚持，不需要把希望寄托在明天的好生意。

author: Metabape
quoted_text:
一个可能不太讨喜的观点：

人生应该尽量少做需要「坚持」的事。

我很佩服能咬牙坚持的人，因为在我的操作系统里，一旦发现自己需要反复打鸡血、做心理建设，才能继续做一件事时，我就会警惕：

是事儿选错了？是方法用错了？还是步子迈太大了？
为啥还没开始干活，先得跟自己的本能打一架？

这个社会太爱给「坚持」鼓掌，
仿佛熬得够久，就能把方向熬对。

可苦吃得多，不代表吃得值。
很多时候，舍不得停，只是不愿意承认前面的罪白受了。
怕之前的苦白吃，于是左侧梭哈加仓，拼了命地再吃点。

不可否认，做任何有难度的事，都会遇到枯燥、挫败和暂时看不到回报的时候。
但偶尔需要咬牙，和每天都在咬牙，是两回事。

适合你的事，也会让你累、让你烦、让你骂骂咧咧。

可缓过来之后，你还是想回去，把那个没解决的问题弄明白。过程中，总有些东西在吸引你：一点好奇，一点进步，一点「卧槽，原来如此」的快乐。

计划长期投入的事儿，总得有点「我还想做」，不能全是「我不能停」。

但如果一件事从头到尾都让你抗拒，唯一的安慰是「等成功了就好了」，那我会非常警惕。因为我正在拿确定要付出的今天，换一个不确定会兑现的明天。

之前读王阳明龙场悟道时，记下过一段很美的话：

人一旦把全部希望押在结果上，眼前的日子就会变得特别轻。今天只是过渡，明天才算生活。
此刻只是忍耐，等命运转弯，自己才算正式出发。

等赚够了钱，
等公司上市，
等做出成绩，
等终于证明了自己……

好像眼下这个疲惫、焦虑、不快乐的自己，只是一个临时版本，熬到条件达标，就能换个人生。

可问题是，这段「临时人生」，也在一天一天消耗着我们，纵然它日功成名就，亦千金难买的光阴。

我追求的人生状态，是对结果少一点「非它不可」，做事时多一点游刃有余，过程中还能时不时觉得：今天这事儿，干得挺有意思，哥们儿学到了。

想赢，但不至于输了就觉得自己一文不值。

期待未来，但今天也得有点活头。

尽量少用「等以后好了」，来解释眼下所有的不快乐。
毕竟，那些被我们咬牙熬过去、恨不得赶紧跳过的日子，也都算在了这不长的一生里。

text:
整理下目前的理解：

AI生物制药主要利好药物发现，药物发现主要有三个环节：

1.靶点发现  2. 化合物筛选 3. 候选药物确定。AI在里面的功能主要就是把化合物筛选和靶点发现这一块的时间缩短，可能原本要四五年的事情缩短到几个月搞定。之前的逻辑是把点发现了之后，可能要去几千上万个库里面，一个一个找相应的分子去试。现在的话就不需要人工来做这个事情了，就可以直接通过AI来做。

但这个流程只是药物发现的一个比较小的环节，后面还有临床一期、二期、三期，非常漫长的审核期。这一块是AI没有办法去加速的，因为都是要在物理世界完成的。

然后这块业务相对于后面临床以及正式大批量的药物上市来说，体量完全不在一个级别，所以我们会发现，所这里面很多相应的公司其实绝对的市值其实跟那些大型药企来比，其实都很低。这倒不是因为他们在一个很早的阶段，而是因为其实本身这一块的业务，它的体量就没有非常大。

然后按照现在的瓶颈理论，AI 明显压缩的是临床前早期，不是整条新药周期。靶点假设、苗头化合物、先导优化，确实可以从过去常见的 4–6 年压到 18 个月左右。

目前的主要瓶颈在湿实验，因为分子发现的速度变快了之后，那就需要物理端现实世界的湿实验来落地去测AI发现的分子是否有用。这块的主要公司有晶泰科技、Recursion（RXRX）这两家是做自动化湿实验平台、Twist Bioscience（TWST）、金斯瑞这两家是做合成和试剂的。

都属于铲子公司，就是分子发现的越多他们越赚，但至于最后的结果怎么样就跟他们无关了。这点其实和早期的半导体炒作挺像的，就是你AI到底有没有用，落地商业化怎么样，其实不关键。

但是你在训练AI的时候，就已经需要去整个半导体产业链上面去买芯片，去买存储了。

到AI生物制药这块，那就变成你AI生物制药最后能不能造出临床上可用的药，或者说提高这个可用药的比例或者效率是怎么样的，我还不确定。但是你因为分子发现的速度变快了，那你最后去给这些分子做湿实验。要用到的试剂的需求肯定是变大的。

text:
现在用 AI 自动做科研，最怕的其实是一处没人发现的 bug：

后面十轮实验，可能全建立在一个假结果上。

这篇 RankEvolve 研究的，就是 Auto-Research 里的「执行可靠性」。

长时 ML 实验中，Agent 很容易引入数据泄漏、漏掉归一化、断开梯度，甚至配置根本没生效。代码能跑、指标也正常，但实验已经失真。

RankEvolve 主要做了三件事：

把研究流程编译成可执行的状态机，强制 Agent 按协议推进；

让 Claude Code、Codex、OpenHands 等不同 Coding Agent 互相 review 和 repair；

保存每轮 patch、配置、指标和失败经验，避免后续重复踩坑。

在相同预算下，异构 Agent 协作把执行正确率从 45.8% 提升到 62.5%。

连续 12 轮自动研究后，在 MovieLens-20M LARGE 上，NDCG@10 比公开基线提升 4.48%。

所以 Auto-Research 跑得越久，越要先保证每一轮实验都值得相信。

否则「自我进化」很容易变成持续放大一个早期错误。

text:
TLDR of @papertrade_xyz: 

nothing like this exists in a crypto; it is truly a brand new primitive

it is modeled after "bucket shops" that were popular in the early 1900s. They were gambling dens were you could wager on stock price movements without actually buying or selling the underlying. The house would always take the exact other side of your bet

This is exactly how papertrade operates. When you place a trade, the house (aka papertrade LP) takes the otherside of your trade. There is no orderbook; the trade is exactly executed at the HL oracle mid price

Now where does the LP funds from?
Incredibly, the LP starts at 0 - no one prefunds it. The LP counts on the skill of the average trader being poor and thus in aggregate a losing position. A fee is skimmed off the top of winning trades (none from losing) to also skew the LP positive

What if the LP doesn't have sufficient funds?
Then traders owed $ are placed into a queue where they're paid out in FIFO order. Traders have to lose to payout traders who won.

$Paper Tokenomics 🧻:
Here is the very cool part - you can only earn their token by losing trades. And the emissions increase when the LP has < $2M, to encourage people to lose to backstop a dwindling LP

And then staking paper earns you the fees and profits that the papertrade LP earns.

Incredibly interesting experiment built by @izebel_eth. Best of luck on the launch! A ton of eyes on this and a lot of people who want to farm $PAPER

On Ethereum, an AI agent can write an app.

It can't write a new opcode. That takes an EIP, a hard fork and a year of calls.

On @aoTheComputer, the agent can extend the machine itself.

ELI5: most chains let you cook in their kitchen. AO lets you build a new oven, and the blueprint goes in a library that never burns down.

The door:

1. Agent writes compute.lua
2. Uploads it to @ArweaveEco → permanent TXID
3. Spawns a process:
   Execution-Stack: scheduler@1.0, lua@5.3a
   Script: <TXID>

Any HyperBEAM node that picks up a message fetches that script from Arweave and runs it. No allow-list, no governance vote, no 24KB contract limit.

Nodes that opt in (load_remote_devices + trusted_device_signers) go further and load whole devices signed by keys they trust.

An agent shipping new hardware for a world computer, and the code is still there in 2126.

text:
Since the CLARITY Act died in the Senate on September 15 (49-50 on the vote just to start debate, with 60 needed), the SEC and CFTC have kept moving without Congress. Here's everything they've done in three weeks.

Sep 16: Both chairs said they'd act anyway. SEC Chair Paul Atkins said "with or without legislation, we will act decisively within the SEC's statutory authority." CFTC Chairman Mike Selig said the CFTC would deliver a framework "using our existing statutory authorities."

Sep 17: The SEC's Innovation Exemption. Approved venues can trade tokenized versions of US stocks on-chain for the next five years, with limits on which stocks and how much volume.

Sep 17: CFTC staff said apps that only pass your trades through to registered brokers don't have to register themselves.

Sep 22: Selig told a New York Fed conference that with tokenization, on-chain finance and 24/7 trading, "the next decade will likely bring more change to financial markets than the previous several decades combined."

Sep 24: CFTC staff said brokers can hold customer money in tokenized versions of approved investments, and blockchain records can count as official records.

Sep 25: SEC staff said token buybacks don't turn a token into a security on their own, and neither does development work after a network launches. Staff views, not rules.

Oct 1: The SEC proposed how investment advisers and funds can hold crypto for their clients.

Oct 2: The SEC approved the first 3x Bitcoin and Ether funds. They're not trading yet. The same day Commissioner Hester Peirce left, so the SEC is down to two commissioners.

Oct 5: The CFTC asked for comments on its first crypto trading rules. One set covers leveraged crypto trading for regular people, the other creates a new kind of US exchange built for crypto. 60 days of comments come first, then actual proposed rules. Selig: "Today's action is just the beginning."

What none of this covers: plain buying and selling of crypto, with no leverage, still has no federal regulator. That part still needs Congress.

text:
Some thoughts about building infrastructure and building a consumer product. (No, they are not the same and you should think about them as different). B2C vs B2B.

Building a consumer product is cool. Brings a lot of eyes, gets hype quick. Major issue though is once a competitor comes or your hype slows down, your product immediately suffers. That’s pretty much the issue of every B2C business model. Ofc, there are outliers. 

When it comes to infrastructure, things are completely different. The onboarding process takes longer, you are judged by the direct value you bring to consumer products. But once your value prop is understood by the products, you start getting traction. You are also not limited to a single product. You become the infrastructure to ALL products (if your infra is good).

It’s much more difficult for a competitor to come and break a solid relationship between two businesses, compared to breaking a relationship between a product and its retail customers. Hence why getting the initial traction is hard, but the returns are long term. The beauty of B2B.

We are building the only Value Retention Infrastructure, giving a brand new layer of revenue to the entire DeFi. Our business model is B2B and oh boy, is it getting traction. After all, who doesn’t like getting more money without paying for it?

text:
The market data provider @massive_com recently started selling US stock data to AI agents one request at a time, paid in USDC, with no account and no API key (using @coinbase's x402 payment standard). As @kleffew94 mentioned in the partnership announcement, and I fully agree with, agents need real-time market data without the friction of API keys, subscriptions, or human provisioning. 

Market data has traditionally been licensed in advance: per seat for someone at a terminal, or under firm-level agreements for the systems trading on it. This model introduces a new kind of buyer: software that pays for a piece of data at the moment it needs it.

For that buyer, a price without reliable time context is incomplete. An agent receiving a single observation needs to know not just what the market said, but also exactly when it was true.

That makes timestamping part of the market-data infrastructure. Inside @TheHUB, packets are timestamped in hardware as they enter the network against a shared GPS-synchronized clock, creating a common time reference for the data moving through it.

他认为，区块链正在从“可编程资产”走向“可编程数据”。借助零知识证明，用户可以验证信息、资产或身份是否可信，而不必向公众公开全部内容。在 AI 代理逐渐接触个人想法、工作资料和敏感数据的背景下，选择披露哪些信息将成为一项基础能力。

AI 也可能成为新的用户界面。Vitalik 分享称，他曾让本地运行的 AI 代理编写脚本，在不打开传统界面的情况下更新 ENS 记录。未来，人们可能通过 AI 直接完成复杂的链上操作。传统网页和中间层的安全风险会减少，但提示注入、模型误判和代理权限管理等新问题也会出现。

他预计，未来两年以太坊将支持更多、更便宜且更具隐私性的交易；链上交易对手、应用程序和报价系统也会越来越多地由 AI 创建和执行。

与此同时，安全不能只停留在协议和私钥层面，还必须覆盖操作系统、AI、网络与硬件。今天的硬件钱包，未来可能成为连接个人数据、资产和现实世界的通用安全设备。

美国 10 年期美债收益率突破近 24 年新高

10月6日 凌晨，10 年期美债收益率盘中触及 5.351%，刷新近 24 年新高。长期利率继续走高，会抬高企业发债、居民房贷和旧债再融资的成本，即使美联储暂时不继续加息，融资压力也会增加。

在过去的一个月 10 年期美债收益率从 4.75% 上升到 5.28%，增加了 0.53 个百分点。同期以抗通胀国债衡量的实际收益率，从 2.44% 上升到 2.92%，增加了 0.48 个百分点。这一阶段的上涨大部分体现在实际收益率上，投资者要求获得更高的扣除通胀后的回报。

美债提供的收益提高，其他投资也需要提供更高的回报才能吸引资金。企业借钱扩大生产，需要项目收入能覆盖更高的利息，投资者购买股票，需要企业有更强的盈利增长，或者以更低的价格买入。市场对未来利率的预期、国债供给，以及持有长期债券需要的风险补偿，都会影响美债收益率。

对于美股，如果企业盈利预期没有相应提高，资金成本上升就会给估值带来压力，估值较高、利润兑现时间较远的公司受到的影响通常更大。企业原来借的低息债到期后，如果只能用更高的利率续借，利息支出也会增加进一步压缩利润。

对于 bitcoin:native 来水，美债收益率提高会增加持有不生息资产的机会成本。投资者承担价格波动，需要获得更高的预期回报，市场也需要持续的现货买盘来支撑价格。

9 月非农只新增了 2.9 万人，就业增长已经放缓，长期融资成本却仍在上升。如果后续就业继续走弱，企业和居民收入增长放慢，而实际收益率又降不下来，消费和投资就可能同时受到收入与借款成本的限制。这种情况持续越久，对企业盈利和风险资产的压力就越大。

十年期美债收益率盘中一度突破了5.3%，最高到5.306%，随后仍在5.3%附近。从PCE公布后约5.20%的低点算起，已经反弹了超过10个基点，通胀数据带来的缓解没有维持住。

这次核心PCE环比增长0.2%，低于预期的0.3%，确实是好消息。但同一份报告里，个人消费支出增长了0.9%，即便扣掉涨价的影响，实际消费仍增长了0.6%，说明美国人的消费需求还很强。

也就是说，通胀比市场担心的温和一些，但需求并没有明显冷下来。再加上能源价格的压力仍在，仅凭这一次PCE，还不足以让市场相信美联储很快就能结束加息，或者让利率降下来。

这轮收益率反弹，更像是市场重新考虑高利率还要维持多久。投资者如果担心未来利率更高、通胀迟迟压不下来，就会要求更高的回报才愿意买债，债券价格因此被抛售，收益率往上走。

目前十月加息的市场概率已经降到了 37% 左右，说明十年期突破5.3%，并不意味着十月一定会加息。长债还在反映未来几年的利率和持有期间的风险。说人话，就是市场越来越相信美联储会维持高利率的时间更长，甚至接下来加息的概率上升。

text:
In electricity markets, a "merchant" power plant is one built without a buyer. It sells whatever it generates on the spot market and hopes the price holds. Lenders dislike them. Most plants get built only after someone signs a long contract for the output.

GPU clouds are learning the same lesson.

For years, the on-demand market ran on merchant capacity. A neocloud would buy a few hundred GPUs on speculation, list them across marketplaces, and fill them by the hour. The arrangement suited the marketplaces well. They took the listing, earned on every hour sold, and carried none of the risk if the hours went unsold. The provider bought the hardware. The marketplace held a free option on it.

That free option is disappearing.

The first reason is financing. Lenders now want contracted revenue before they fund hardware, and an hourly listing is not contracted revenue. Capital that once backed speculative clusters now asks for minimum commitments and utilization floors before it will release the capacity.

The second is risk appetite. When three-year reservations sell as fast as they are offered, nobody needs to gamble on an hourly fill rate. Why take merchant risk when the contract is sitting on the table?

So providers are doing the rational thing. They are pulling capacity back and selling it as reserved blocks. What they still list, they list on new terms: the marketplace commits to something, or the capacity goes elsewhere.

The prices reflect it. The average on-demand H100, a chip now three years old, rose about 6% over the summer. One widely followed index has the B200 up nearly 80% in three months, to about $8 an hour. Flexibility hasn't vanished. It has simply stopped being cheap.

Spot remains, and for good reason. Any provider serious about its SLAs keeps warm spare nodes ready to swap in when hardware fails. Between failures, those spares can earn something. That is spot capacity: real, useful, and recallable the moment a reserved customer needs it.

None of this makes marketplaces obsolete. Buyers still need a place to compare, source, and place capacity across dozens of providers. What has changed is the bargain. A marketplace that brings nothing but a listing page now has very little leverage. One that shares the risk has a great deal.

That is the shift we have made at Shadeform. Our new provider agreements commit us alongside our partners, structured so that we do not win unless they win.

Flexibility is an option, and options have a price. For years the market let intermediaries hold that option for free.

Those days are over.

text:
This direction is what I'd dub "Private trains, public rails". The goal is the best network for assets to be issued, held and used, with value accruing to the network as a whole and ETH.

Ethereum is a confirmation engine. CCIP v1 already waited for Ethereum finality, but Chainlink nodes still had to report the result themselves. That is the pragmatic choice when proving Ethereum's consensus on another chain isn't practical. With zk-powered light clients, the bridge can verify Ethereum's confirmation directly instead of relying on someone's report of it.

Plugging these proofs into the bridge is enabled by the modular architecture of CCIP 2.0, also present in LayerZero. It unbundles the transport layer of the bridge from its application services, such as token issuance, standards and business logic, compliance or other features.

But it's only an attractive proposition if the Ethereum settlement layer is fast, cheap and secure, otherwise the temptation is great to use an alternative with different trade-offs. FCR is another step in this direction.

Zooming out, it starts to show what is imo the right balance between private and public build-out of Ethereum.

- Canonical bridges tying L2s to L1 remain the least featureful and most neutral, but the most secure way to move assets between L1 and L2s, especially ETH and other L1-native assets. They are privately built, but function more like public utilities: available, unattended, and secure, built on L1's settlement (finality or fast confirmation) and more and more on broadly available zk proofs.

- The utility exposed by these bridges becomes the root of trust for private operators offering differentiated services to asset issuers and other customers. Chainlink and others are well placed to serve their customers' business needs, relying on Ethereum's confirmation engine for the rails on which assets run.

Ethlabs is helping to build the public rails: fast, cheap and secure settlement across L1 and L2s, with value accruing to Ethereum and ETH.
author: ethlabs_org
quoted_text:
It’s very cool to see more zk tech hardening bridges! zk does two things here: it proves that a fact of a world in a remote chain is part of that chain's state, and that this fact of the world is the one everybody agrees happened in the first place, ruling out double spends.

This is already a major improvement, and I'd like to talk about where we could go even further..

Today, and in this @chainlink CCIP 2.0 module, the @SuccinctLabs light client proves that Ethereum finality was achieved (“everybody agrees this version of the world happened”), by proving the report from a small validator subcommittee known as the “sync committee”. Finality is the ultimate agreement. However Ethereum finality still takes about 15 minutes!

Meanwhile, FCR is a snapshot of that agreement with very strong guarantees, at low latency. Now what if you could put together the power of zk and the power of FCR together to reduce by 30x that latency? Turns out, this may be possible! We mentioned it briefly in our weekly update two weeks ago https://t.co/2SVmcO5Bjt

Can we go even further? There are two complementary boosts:

1. Extending state inclusion proofs to full validity proofs. You're then not just proving that the state reported by validators includes data about your bridge transfer. You're proving validity of the entire remote chain's execution! No chance for validators to fool you.

2. Reducing time-to-finality. FCR is great, and will be a great bridge (pun intended) until we get really low latency finality, in the order of tens of seconds. Eventually, we'll get that, as well as a full proof that this finality was achieved, not relying on a subcommittee's report.

You put all this together, and you start to see the future of seamless and secure interoperability across Ethereum. Let's go build it!

We've replaced attention with relative strength in our holder strength index.

Attention was the only part of the index built on social data, and it didn't read every coin reliably. Relative strength uses the same onchain prices as everything else and works the same way on every chain.

It measures how a coin's price held up over the past week against the coins from its own launchpad/chain/ecosystem. The chart below is what that looked like during last week's dip.

Same 12.5% weight, and the history was rescored so the trend stays continuous. 

Live now at https://t.co/bb6UD3TtAR
author: ArtofConviction
quoted_text:
Most coins move together on a dip. Last week almost every coin in our index went down, and the median one lost 35%.

They didn't all fall the same way, though. Five went up, between 25% and 70%. Five more dropped only 3% to 13% while the median coin on their launchpad or chain dropped around 30%. Some lost more than half.

That spread is relative strength: how each coin holds up against the coins from its own launchpad or chain. It exists onchain like it does in any other market, and a dip is when it's easiest to see, because every coin is under the same pressure at once.

The map shows every coin we measure against its peers.

text:
花旗10月5日发布的《全球股票季度展望：韧性还是自满？》核心其实是在回答一个很重要的问题：为什么在油价高位、全球重新进入加息周期、长端利率大幅上行、美国—伊朗冲突没有彻底解决、市场广度又明显恶化的情况下，全球股票仍然接近历史高点？
这是基本面真的比想象中强，还是市场已经对风险麻木？
花旗给出的答案：目前仍站在 “Resilience（韧性）” 一边。它实际上把未来半年全球股票继续上涨的条件压缩成了两个变量：盈利必须继续兑现，地缘和利率冲击不能进一步升级。

当然长债收益率上涨绝不是没有影响：影响主要落在传统行业、中小盘、房地产、消费等利率敏感资产。而 AI / 半导体 / 大型科技由于盈利增长足够强，靠“分子”增长抵消了“分母”折现率上升。
花旗的逻辑跟我之前推文逻辑很一致，

花期这份报告对当下美股投资三个意义：
1）AI交易目前没有结束。
因为驱动 AI 股票的东西正在从估值扩张
逐渐切换成EPS兑现；
2）收益率上涨为什么科技不跌、传统行业跌这个现象仍然可能持续；
3）未来真正能够让美股牛市发生趋势性逆转的变量，很可能不是第一次或者第二次加息，而是盈利revision开始转负。

花旗认为目前的市场韧性大体是真的，因为盈利增长足够强，过去一年甚至在股价上涨的同时把全球股市估值从19倍消化到了16倍；但市场已经进入一个对EPS兑现高度依赖的阶段，未来再靠估值扩张赚钱越来越困难。

只要盈利没有开始下修，这种分化本身还不能当作牛市结束信号。真正需要警惕的是 高利率从“经济强的结果”逐步变成“财政/通胀/term premium失控的结果”，与此同时AI盈利revision开始见顶。 这两个条件如果同时出现，才会把花旗的“韧性”真正推向“自满”。

之前10月1号对9月份有一个回复和10月展望 跟花旗的这期报告逻辑很类似： https://t.co/kpblUc6mco
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
昨晚的美股债市总结下来就是一句话：弱非农把10月加息概率进一步压低，AI高beta继续主导市场，但债市给出的信号远没有股市乐观。这里的核心还是油价和长债收益率。
1、油价方面：
1）好的层面
美军护航部分油轮集中通过海峡，沙特阿美快速恢复每日通过东西输油管道输送约600万桶原油，约有450万桶/日的管道流量可用于出口。市场有实际出口能力正在恢复的预期。

同时G7领导人同意通过IEA协调释放1亿桶柴油和其他石油储备，川普也明确表态美国不会实施柴油出口禁令，如果未来两周柴油裂解价差明显回落，会比Brent单独回落更有利于Fed通胀路径。

2）但风险依然在
如1号推文聊到“伊朗应该还保有把某一批船打停的能力”，昨晚英国海上贸易办公室（UKMTO）就报告两艘油轮在海峡被袭击，也就说明了伊朗还有干扰南部航道的能力；
美军还在往中东部署第三支航母战斗群和第三支两栖陆战队远征军部队，威胁中期选举后动武；
同时沙特明显从前几周的“防御 + 空袭”往“准备改变地面控制线”推进。看路透社报道沙特开始认真筹划曼德海峡沿岸反攻计划。

这些都让昨晚油价出现V反、先跌再涨。
油价就在“航线可能恢复”和“战争升级”之间摇摆。

2、长债方面
油价又起来，然后长期资本成本、财政供给、期限溢价这些仍很高，所以美债收益率昨晚也是先跌后涨。

在现在这个位置上、长债收益率越往上市场压力也越大。

但另一方面，经纪名义GDP增速还可以，AI产业也还在继续快速进化（引用推文里有梳理最近一段时间产业上的进展），这种情况下基本面好盈利强劲业绩预期兑现节奏快的标的是能扛住宏观逆风的，而且稍有缓和就容易往上蹦。这也是有人感到最割裂的地方、看债市觉得摇摇欲坠、看道指、标普等权、罗素2000弱的一逼、但看纳指则是稳步震荡向上、核心就在这里。

所以这也是我在引用的推文聊的“当下市场最害怕的是收益率快上往上飙；
如果能稳住、市场也会缓缓；
现在的市场并不需要收益率大幅跌，只需要稳定小幅回落、那么那些业绩没问题股票就能起来，之前被收益率压制的板块也能起来。

所以综合起来就是：
1）当下收益率水平部分强势标的能扛住，如果长债收益率还要快速往上飙升，小盘股、价值股还得继续泄，AI和大科技也会被压制； 

2）如果us10Y不能稳定下来（当下位置震荡），那么AI半导体和大科技里逻辑最硬的标的还是能扛住，还能震荡向上，碰到有波动调整逢低买。

3）但如果5.2~5.3%开始成为新的均衡水平，在这个基础上如果能小幅回落，估值受到的边际压力会明显减弱，那么不仅AI科技板块继续走强，而且资金可能开始从少数半导体、AI科技龙头向银行、周期和部分中小盘扩散。 

当然更重要的点是10月下旬大科技的三季度财报陆续出来，市场应该会看到AI商业化进程还是远超预期的，美股基本面还是第一位的。

author: chang_defi
quoted_text:
We had GPT-6 Astra, an AI coding agent, teach a robot arm to screw in a lightbulb, entirely in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

The task: we reproduced the new EmbodiedSWE benchmark on our own rented GPUs. A simulated Franka arm has to pick up a bulb lying on its side, stand it upright, set it on a socket, and screw it down along a physically simulated thread until it seats.

The agent gets a simulator, a camera, and 4 hours to write the controller from scratch.

By the numbers:
- 4 hours
- 7 work sessions
- 289 commands
- 22 checkpoints
- 47.7M input tokens (43.8M cached)
- 42.7K output tokens
- ~$85–120 in API calls at list price
- ~$4 of GPU time (5.2 hours on a single RTX 4090)

The model is ~95% of the cost. It read ~1,100 tokens for every token it wrote.

For comparison, Claude Opus 5.5 on the same task and setup got the bulb upright on the socket but never got the thread to catch: 0 of 2 setups seated so far.

Next: turning Astra's working solution into hundreds of verified robot demonstrations for training robot models, all generated in simulation.
