text:
$CLAUS has played out pretty much as I expected

In my previous update, I said the $12–14M range wasn’t where I wanted to chase. If the thesis remained intact, the $7–8M area would offer a much better risk/reward

CLAUS eventually reset to around $7.5M, right into the area I was watching, before pushing to a new ATH near $20M. It has since cooled off and is now trading around $16–17M

The chart playing out is one thing, but what interests me more is what has happened behind the scenes since my last post

At the time, I said CLAUS had already shown that the team could ship quickly. The next stage was no longer about counting how many hooks they could add. I wanted to see whether those mechanisms could actually start generating real activity and cash flow

NFT Vaults are the first place where we’re starting to get an answer

All 300 NFTs are still outstanding, representing roughly 15M CLAUS locked in the vaults. According to the on-chain snapshot I checked at around 23:52 UTC on October 6, the first epoch had accrued roughly 4.406 ETH, with around 4.082 ETH already distributed to NFT holders, worth approximately $11K at the time

The epoch started at 22:41 UTC on October 5, with roughly 0.325 ETH still remaining in the epoch pot and not yet distributed

This is a much more meaningful update to me than the NFT floor

In my previous post, I deliberately avoided putting too much weight on the projected yield because everything was still theoretical. Now we at least have real payouts showing that the mechanism actually works

That said, my view on the 15M CLAUS hasn’t changed. This is a temporary lock, not a burn. Each NFT is backed by 50,000 CLAUS, and holders can burn the NFT to receive those tokens back

So the next thing to watch isn’t just how large the payouts are. It’s whether volume can remain high enough to keep the yield attractive, and how many NFTs start getting redeemed if activity slows down

The team has also continued expanding the programmable layer with Higher or Lower

It’s essentially a prediction market built directly into the pool. Users choose a target market cap and deadline, then bet ETH on Higher or Lower. The result is determined using the average market cap over the final 30 minutes

For now, the scale is still very small. The pot I saw was only around 0.025 ETH

So at this stage, I see it more as another demonstration of what can be added to the same live token than a meaningful source of economic activity

Prediction markets themselves aren’t new. What interests me is that another completely different mechanism has been added directly to CLAUS without launching another token

There was also another update that I think is equally important, even though it isn’t bullish

The Arbitrage hook was deployed and then removed on the same day after the mechanism failed to execute real arbitrage as intended

The token didn’t change. The pool and NFT Vaults continued operating. The part that failed was simply rolled back

This shows the other side of programmability

The team can add new mechanisms quickly, but they can also ship an experiment that doesn’t work and have to remove it

For me, that strengthens the technical thesis while also making the execution risk clearer

Shipping fast doesn’t mean everything they ship creates value

On the burn side, roughly 4.58M CLAUS has now been burned, equivalent to around 0.46% of the original supply

That still doesn’t change how I view the token

The burn is too small to become the main thesis

What matters more is how fees are being distributed across the different mechanisms

At the snapshot I checked, while the weather state was dry, the active split was roughly 1% to the project, 0.35% to NFT rewards, 0.35% to auto liquidity, 0.15% to buyback and burn, 0.15% to FOMO buybacks and 0.30% to the programmable layer

This isn’t a permanent configuration

Weather can change the allocation between burn and liquidity. When it rains, burn can increase to 0.35% while liquidity drops to 0.15%

What matters to me isn’t which percentage is higher at any specific moment. It’s that most of this economic loop still depends on volume

NFT rewards need volume

Burn needs volume

Auto liquidity needs volume

FOMO buybacks also need activity

So from here, I care much more about volume than the number of hooks

Another area where I’m still cautious is liquidity

The main pool only has a few hundred thousand dollars of liquidity while the valuation is already in the eight-figure range

That helps explain how CLAUS could move from around $7.5M to nearly $20M so quickly, but it also means the downside can happen just as fast

More importantly, GoPlus currently shows 0% of the LP locked, with the LP tokens of the main pool sitting in the project wallet

That’s a separate risk I think is worth monitoring because downside doesn’t only have to come from traders selling the token. Any meaningful change involving the LP or project wallet could directly affect the liquidity structure

After the move from around $7.5M to nearly $20M, my approach is naturally different from the previous post

At $7–8M, the question was whether the thesis remained intact enough to justify the risk

At the current valuation, the question is whether economic activity can start catching up with the valuation

The first payout of roughly 4 ETH is a good signal, but one epoch isn’t enough to answer that question

I want to see the main pool continue doing a few million dollars in daily volume, future epochs continue paying ETH, NFT redemptions remain under control and the existing mechanisms start seeing real usage

The prediction market is live, but the pot is only around 0.025 ETH

Arbitrage failed and was rolled back

Burn remains below 0.5%

So I think CLAUS is now entering a pretty clear new stage

The team no longer needs to prove that they can modify a live token or continuously add new mechanisms. They’ve already done that

What they need to prove next is whether these mechanisms can retain users, volume and cash flow once the initial attention starts fading

That’s what I’ll be focusing on from here

The chart has already gone through the reset I was waiting for and then expanded from around $7.5M to nearly $20M. NFT Vaults have moved from projected yield to real payouts. Programmability continues to be demonstrated, while the Arbitrage failure also shows the other side of moving this fast

So the thesis hasn’t changed much, but the bar for me to stay bullish is higher now

At this stage, I don’t need more hooks

I want to see the things they’ve already built actually being used

quoted_text:
Only a few hours after my previous research post on $CLAUS, there’s already quite a lot to update

First, the chart. $CLAUS broke through the previous $10–11M ATH zone and pushed to around $13.5–14M MC, before resetting back toward $10–11M

But price isn’t the most interesting part to me. During those same few hours, @contractclaus and @founderclaus kept shipping, and this time we got a few updates that actually add to the thesis I talked about before

The biggest one is that NFT Vaults are now live and all 300 slots have already been minted

The mechanism is pretty simple. Each NFT requires 50,000 CLAUS to be locked. NFT holders then receive a share of the ETH fees from the main pool based on how long they hold

300/300 have been minted, which means roughly 15M CLAUS, or 1.5% of the supply, is currently sitting inside these vaults

According to the Founder, 0.35% of the ETH volume from the main pool is distributed to NFT holders from the existing 2% fee. There’s no additional tax

Exiting is also pretty simple: burn the NFT and get the 50,000 CLAUS back

So I don’t consider those 15M CLAUS burned. They’re only temporarily locked. If a lot of people redeem at the same time, those tokens can return to the market and potentially create sell pressure

And don’t confuse NFT Vaults with passive yield for simply holding CLAUS. You need to lock 50,000 CLAUS into an NFT to receive these fees

Their current estimate is around $70/day if volume stays around $6M and all 300 NFTs are held for the full day. Sounds pretty good, but I’m not going to hype that number yet

What I want to see next is real payouts

If the first batches actually distribute ETH, volume remains in the millions per day and holders keep their vaults instead of redeeming, then NFT Vaults start to have some real economic proof behind them

Another interesting detail is that the market is currently valuing these NFTs much higher than the CLAUS backing each one

50,000 CLAUS at the current price is only around $550, while the OpenSea floor previously reached around 0.95 ETH

That premium is basically the market pricing in future fee flow

If payouts come in as expected, there’s a reason for that premium to exist. But if payouts are much lower or volume starts dying, the NFT premium can collapse pretty quickly. That’s when I’ll start watching whether redemptions increase

There’s another update that I think fits the CLAUS thesis even better than the NFTs

They literally changed the live token itself from :

Claus / CLAUS

to

SAME FUCKING COIN / SAME

and then changed it back to :

Claus / CLAUS

Same contract

Same balances

No new token launch

In my previous post I was careful with the name/ticker part because at the time, most of the proof came from an earlier test token

This time they actually did it directly on the live CLAUS contract

It sounds degen as hell, but it demonstrates exactly what I’ve been interested in from the beginning :

Same token, new rules. And now even the same token, new identity

That’s why I still think people are looking at CLAUS the wrong way if they only call it an AI coin, weather coin or NFT coin

Weather is one hook

Arena is an experiment

NFT Vaults are another hook

The name change is another demonstration

What I’m actually betting on is the ability to keep changing the token after it has already launched

The existing mechanisms haven’t stopped either

Burn has increased from around 3.36M CLAUS in my previous post to roughly 4.4M, or around 0.44% of the original supply

It’s moving, but my view hasn’t changed: burning less than 0.5% of supply isn’t enough for me to call this a deflationary play

Auto-liquidity is still running in batches of around $500, weather still adjusts the allocation between burn and liquidity, Fomo still uses 0.15% to buy CLAUS into the Founder wallet rather than burning it, Arena is still running, and now NFT Vaults have been added on top

So basically, in just a few hours we got :

A new ATH, the 8th hook, 300/300 NFTs minted, around 15M CLAUS locked, more tokens burned, and a live demonstration of changing the token’s name/ticker on the same contract

That’s the part I’m slightly bullish on: the speed of execution

But I also think CLAUS is entering a different stage now

Before, the question was :

“Can they actually ship these ideas?”

They’ve shipped quite a few of them now

The next question should be :

“Can the things they ship create real economic activity?”

NFT Vaults will be a pretty good test of that

I’ll be watching the actual ETH payouts, how many NFTs get redeemed, the NFT premium relative to the underlying 50,000 CLAUS, main pool volume and, of course, whatever hooks they deploy next

If volume stays in the millions per day and payouts actually work, I think NFT Vaults could become an interesting layer

On the other hand, if volume drops hard below roughly $1–2M while the valuation stays high, the yield drops with it. At that point, the NFT premium could collapse and those 15M locked CLAUS won’t look nearly as attractive as the headline “1.5% of supply locked”

My chart plan also needs to change after the new ATH

$12–14M is now the new high zone. I’m not chasing here, especially with only a few hundred thousand dollars of liquidity in the main pool

$9–11M is where we are now, and it’s still only a shallow dip from the new ATH. I’ll be watching the reaction here, especially volume and NFT payouts

$7–8M would be a deeper reset, roughly 40% from the top. Risk/reward starts looking much better to me there if the thesis remains intact

$5–6M is still the area I’d prefer if the market actually gives it back, but I’m not going to sit around waiting for exactly $5M either

And below $3.5M, I’m no longer asking, “Is it cheap?”

I’m checking whether they’re still shipping hooks, whether volume is still alive, and whether the thesis itself is starting to break

So overall, my thesis on $CLAUS hasn’t changed over the last few hours, but it’s becoming easier to prove

I’m not betting on whether it rains in London

I’m not betting on 4.4M tokens being burned

And I’m not betting on the NFT floor being high

I’m betting on the idea that the same token can keep changing, testing new mechanisms and creating new economic experiments without having to relaunch from scratch

@contractclaus and @founderclaus are shipping fast, but from here I want to see more than just new features

I want to see real payouts, real volume and real demand for the mechanisms they’ve just built

Price can do whatever it wants

They keep shipping, I keep watching

Check is: one living person, counted once, AI agents can’t fake it. FHE encryption runs on the phone; no ID needed, no raw image stored.

text:
Project Eleven Launches Strongpoint for Post-Quantum Custody with Zcash Foundation as Initial Development Partner

Zcash Foundation joins Project Eleven to shape institutional custody infrastructure for the post-quantum and AI era as more than $1 trillion in digital assets remain at risk of attack by sufficiently powerful quantum computers.

Project Eleven, the post-quantum security company for digital assets, today introduced Strongpoint, its flagship custody platform built for navigating the transition to post-quantum cryptography. @ZcashFoundation joins Project Eleven as an initial development partner, helping shape Strongpoint’s institutional custody architecture.

Strongpoint is designed to give institutions a consistent control layer for securing and managing digital assets as networks change the cryptographic standards underneath them. Rather than rebuilding key-management, transaction approval, and audit infrastructure for each new signature scheme or network migration, institutions can maintain a common set of security controls while the underlying cryptography evolves.

“Institutional digital asset custody was built for a world where the cryptography underneath it rarely changed,” said Alex Pruden, CEO of Project Eleven. “Quantum computing is upending that model. If every network adopts a different solution, institutions could be forced to rebuild their security infrastructure again and again. Strongpoint is built around crypto-agility, so the cryptography can change without the infrastructure changing with it.”

“Institutions holding shielded ZEC need custody infrastructure that respects Zcash’s privacy model today and can adapt as cryptographic standards change,” said Alex Bornstein, Executive Director of Zcash Foundation. “Project Eleven is building Strongpoint with the crypto-agility and technical foundation needed to support those requirements over time, helping strengthen custody infrastructure for the broader ecosystem.”

Zcash Foundation Joins as an Initial Development Partner

Zcash Foundation joins as an initial development partner for Strongpoint, bringing its expertise in privacy-preserving cryptography and protocol engineering to Strongpoint’s institutional custody architecture. Zcash’s privacy-preserving design introduces sophisticated key-management and transaction requirements, making it a valuable environment for developing custody infrastructure capable of supporting evolving cryptographic standards.
The collaboration will help inform how Strongpoint handles network-specific requirements while maintaining a consistent institutional control framework across assets and cryptographic schemes.

Post-Quantum Migrations Are Taking Different Paths

The digital asset industry’s post-quantum transition is becoming a coordination challenge. Among the networks represented by the 20 largest assets in CoinGecko’s Layer 1 (L1) category by market capitalization, Project Eleven found that only 10 have published a network-specific technical proposal, roadmap or implementation path for migrating transaction or account authentication to post-quantum cryptography.

Those approaches span at least six proposed post-quantum signature schemes and vary significantly in how they address account migration, key rotation and legacy-asset recovery. Even where technical roadmaps exist, operational readiness remains uneven, leaving institutions to navigate different standards and requirements across networks.

For institutions operating across multiple networks, that fragmentation means accommodating different cryptographic standards and migration requirements without losing a consistent security model. Strongpoint is designed to provide that common operating layer while allowing the cryptography beneath it to change independently.

Early Access and Deployment

Project Eleven targets production deployment in Q4 2026 and is working with a limited group of development partners ahead of general availability. Additional development partners and supported networks will be announced. Institutions interested in early access can request more information at https://t.co/Sl7ErXIJCx.

Founded in 2024 by Alex Pruden and Conor Deegan, Project Eleven raised a $20 million Series A led by Castle Island Ventures in January 2026, bringing its total funding to $26 million. The company recently acquired Riva Labs, a specialized engineering firm with deep expertise in post-quantum signatures, wallet infrastructure and blockchain cryptography, expanding Project Eleven’s in-house research and protocol-engineering capabilities.

Methodology: Project Eleven reviewed the 20 largest assets in CoinGecko’s Layer 1 (L1) category by market capitalization on September 25, 2026. A network was counted only where an official network organization, foundation, core development team or recognized protocol-improvement process had published a network-specific technical proposal, roadmap or implementation path for migrating transaction or account authentication to post-quantum cryptography. General research programs, statements of intent and post-quantum work that did not specify such a migration path were not counted. Draft technical proposals were included and do not imply network approval or adoption.

a16z GP David Haber (@dhaber) on landing at Goldman Sachs after it acquired his startup, Bond Street:

"I would often ask myself, what does it mean to take risk inside of a big company? Because that was my natural disposition. I'd just spent four years running through walls."

"Let me just completely disregard my job description and speak very plainly to the most senior people and the most junior people."

"I just started firing off emails to Marty Chavez, who was the CFO at the time, and the heads of banking and asset management, being like, hey, I'm here. How can I help?"

"I was a very weirdly shaped Goldman employee… I was kind of running around the building."

quoted_text:
Last year, as part of a comprehensive review of NIH’s intramural policies, I announced that NIH was adopting an updated agency-wide framework to embed principles of academic freedom within our Intramural Research Program. This framework recognizes that intramural researchers must be free to share their scientific viewpoints and to communicate their scientific findings through manuscripts, presentations, media interviews, and so on. This includes hosting outside lecturers for events focused on their scientific work. 

Today, NIH reaffirms this commitment to academic freedom as members of the intramural research community host Kristian G. Andersen, MPhil, PhD, as a guest lecturer. 

Dr. Andersen is a co-author of a March 2020 paper published in Nature Medicine titled “The proximal origin of SARS-CoV-2.” The paper’s authors assert: “Our analyses clearly show that SARS-CoV-2 is not a laboratory construct or a purposefully manipulated virus.” They further write that “we do not believe that any type of laboratory-based scenario is plausible.” 

The paper was cited extensively by members of the media, social media companies, and government officials to refute or suppress lab-origin hypotheses and to discredit anyone who publicly dissented from the dominant natural-origins narrative. As then-NIH Director Dr. Francis Collins wrote, “this study leaves little room to refute a natural origin for COVID-19.”

Yet before and after the paper’s publication, Dr. Andersen himself expressed substantially more uncertainty. In January, he wrote in an email that some features of the virus “(potentially) look engineered.” One month after the paper’s publication, he wrote privately that he was not fully convinced that every lab-based scenario could be ruled out. 

In January 2025, the Central Intelligence Agency released the results of an assessment conducted during the Biden administration that found a “research-related origin” of SARS-CoV-2 was “more likely than a natural origin,” while assessing both theories as plausible. Given the evidence I’ve seen, I think the preponderance of evidence supports the theory that the virus leaked from a lab. 

I am keenly aware that no hypothesis about the origins of SARS-CoV-2 has been conclusively proven. When it comes to open scientific questions like this, our ability to pursue truth depends on our freedom to explore various hypotheses, weigh all available evidence, and deliberate openly. This freedom was denied to many scientists during the pandemic. 𝗜 𝗮𝗺 𝗽𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗡𝗜𝗛 𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗴𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝘀—𝗻𝗼 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗻𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗦-𝗖𝗼𝗩-𝟮—𝗲𝗻𝗷𝗼𝘆 𝗶𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘄.

text:
Just got How to Live an Extraordinary Life: Volume II today.

I rarely read an entire book in one sitting, but I couldn’t put this one down. I just finished it, and it’s incredible.

The wisdom Anthony has accumulated by this point in his life is truly something to aspire to. As someone in my 30s as well, I hope to develop that same level of wisdom, perspective, and ability to turn ideas into action.

What makes this book especially meaningful to me is that I’ve experienced firsthand how one of Anthony’s books can change the trajectory of your life.

After reading Volume I, I sent Anthony an idea I had: Bitcoin Mining in Space.
Anthony’s obsession with hunting for good ideas led our paths to cross.

He wrote about the idea in The Pomp Letter in 2024, and that moment helped spark what has become my extraordinary life, taking an idea I couldn’t stop thinking about and turning it into action as the Co-Founder & CEO of my current startup.

That’s why I don’t say this lightly:
Reading Anthony’s books can genuinely change the way you think and potentially change what you do with your life.

I also love that this book is written as letters to his children. You can feel the wisdom being passed down from a father to his kids, and I feel incredibly grateful to now be a recipient of some of that wisdom too.

Anthony’s children are very fortunate to have a father who is intentional about passing these lessons down to them. And we’re lucky that he’s willing to share them with the rest of us.

Highly recommend this book to everyone.

Go read it. Then go do something extraordinary with what you learned.

text:
On Sanctum App.

One of the most fascinating things about studying businesses is seeing how much money gets made on small inefficiencies and frictions.

One classic example is how little traditional retail brokerages pay on bank deposits. At Schwab, uninvested cash gets moved into Schwab's own bank, which is invested and pays users a pathetic 0.19%.

That switching cost alone makes Schwab $5-9 billion more a year.

There's a similar dynamic on crypto CEXs.

Most users simply stake their tokens on CEXs out of convenience. E.g. Binance gives you 2.7% on your staked SOL. If users bothered to learn DeFi, they'd realise they're leaving more than half of their money on the table - your average SOL LST gives you 5% yield, or Sanctum's INF has given users 6.5% APY over the last 12 months.

Having the best product and better yield isn't enough. The hard part is educating users and getting them to move. Much of our work on the Sanctum App is about making switching easier than staying.

French rioters are blasting the rap song “MRH” which glorifies a terrorist who executed a 3 year old French Jewish child.

Lyrics: “Like Mohamed Merah, dodging the cameras  at the Bataclan, I shot him with my eyes, manhunt, Salah Abdeslam.”

14 years ago Mohammed Merah broke into a Jewish school in the French town of Toulouse and executed a pair of 3 year old and 5 year old French Jewish boys.

He then chased an 8 year old Jewish girl named Myriam Monsonego.

Merah caught her by her hair and raised a gun to execute her. His gun jammed, so he changed weapons. He then shot the little girl in the head while filming the execution with his GoPro.

He later said that he carried out this crime to “uphold the honour of Islam.” He called it an act of revenge because “the Jews kill our brothers and sisters in Palestine.”

According to one of his brothers, Merah was raised in an "atmosphere of racism and hatred" in their Muslim family.

Merah's sister Souad later said, "I am proud of my brother. He fought until the end against the Jews, and all those who massacre Muslims, I detest them."

According to his brother, when Merah's body was brought home, members of the local terrorist community visited the family to praise his actions and they cried tears of joy. Their only regret was that Merah had not killed more Jews.

Merah was buried on 29 March 2012 in the Muslim section of the Cornebarrieu cemetery, near Toulouse. About 50 people attended, including the local imam.

The mayor of Toulouse at the time tried to block Mohammed Merah’s burial, so French President Nicolas Sarkozy stepped in to support the burial.

"He was French. Let him be buried and let's not have any arguments about it," Sarkozy said.

Now he is held up as a hero by French rioters.

text:
继 Blast 后，Abstract 也关了：L2 的今天，很可能就是 Perp DEX 的明天😲😲😲

4 天内，两条 Ethereum L2 宣布关停。Blast 因为运营成本已经高于收入。

Abstract 更扎心，Igloo 贴了 18 个月的钱，亏了数千万美元，最后连发币回血都放弃了。

Abstract 有40 万+用户、3.25 亿笔交易、144+应用，还有 Disney、Red Bull Racing 这种品牌进场，关停前链上甚至还有接近 4800 万美元资产，因为流动性不够深、DeFi 起不来、机构不来，用户和交易也没有变成足够支撑一条链长期运营的利润。

L2 照进现实：

市场需要扩容，但根本不需要这么多 L2。技术栈越来越成熟以后，自己发一条链本身几乎不再构成护城河，真正稀缺的是用户、资产、流动性、分发和持续赚钱的能力。

没有这些东西，再漂亮的 TPS、钱包数、交易笔数，最后都是服务器账单。

成也 L2，败也 L2。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
I’m extremely sad to announce that Abstract is shutting down.

When we were just a three-person team building Frame I never could have imagined the two and half year journey I was about to embark on.

From the tireless nights preparing for launch, to mainnet going live in January 2025, and everything in between, this journey is one I will treasure for the rest of my life. Even though the outcome is not what we wanted, I am incredibly proud of everything we built at Abstract.

The Portal and Abstract Global Wallet made interacting with a blockchain feel seamless. That foundation led to a wave of unique apps, novel onchain experiences, and, most importantly, an incredibly passionate community that gave Abstract an identity and culture of its own.

But the truth is that the industry has changed significantly since the idea was first conceived in the summer of 2024, and Abstract was facing difficulties with our DeFi Ecosystem and liquidity on the chain.

We reached a crossroads of experiencing significant growth, but not having cemented product-market-fit,and that was becoming an issue from a business sustainability perspective.

A very difficult decision needed to be made. Abstract’s growth had stalled and the chain was simply not economically sustainable anymore despite our best efforts.

I am extremely grateful to the Igloo, Inc team who truly gave it their all to explore every angle and make Abstract work.

I want to take this time to thank the incredibly talented team I had the pleasure of working with over the last three years. Every single one of them poured their heart and soul into Abstract and together we created something truly special that pushed forward what onchain discovery and experiences could look like. It is the best team that I have ever worked with. I will always be proud of that.

I want to thank all of our partners and builders that worked with us to make Abstract such a unique, special place. Truly some of the most talented developers launched on Abstract and I know you will all kill it in your next chapter.

Most of all I want to thank the Abstract community for the support over these three years. I know there have been moments of frustration, but your passion and admiration for Abstract are what made it so special and helped create a culture that is incredibly rare in crypto. I truly wish this could have worked out for all of us.

Thank you for supporting the green chain ✳️

text:
I listened to Aster CEO @Leonard_Aster latest interview.

The most interesting part wasn’t the usual “we’re growing” talk.

It was how Aster sees its next phase.

A few things stood out 👇

1/ Aster doesn’t want to remain just another perp DEX.

The long-term goal is to become the liquidity infrastructure underneath other products.

Regional frontends, wallets, AI agents and other apps could all plug into Aster liquidity without users necessarily interacting with Aster directly.

That’s a much bigger ambition than simply competing for perp volume.

2/ AOS could be an important part of this.

With the Aster Open Standard, third parties can permissionlessly deploy markets, provide liquidity and keep the fees generated by those markets.

Instead of Aster deciding what every market should look like, the idea is to let an ecosystem of deployers compete on top of the same infrastructure.

3/ Leonard also made an interesting point about metrics:

He cares more about active, fee-paying traders than headline volume.

Volume can be gamed.

Users who repeatedly come back and actually pay fees are much harder to fake.

Aster’s near-term target: 100K+ daily active traders.

4/ Another shift worth watching is incentives.

Leonard basically said the era of perp DEXs endlessly giving away their own token to generate volume is ending.

The model Aster wants instead:

Projects bring their own incentives → distribute them to Aster traders → use Aster as the liquidity/distribution layer.

USD1/WLFI is the first visible example.

5/ And this is probably the key quote from the whole interview:

Aster spent year one catching up.

Now Leonard says they’ve largely reached feature parity with the major DEXs/CEXs.

The next phase has to be differentiation.

So the Aster thesis from here isn't really:

“Can it build another good perp DEX?”

It’s:

“Can Aster become infrastructure that other trading products build on?”

That’s the part I’d be watching.

text:
I’ve been experimenting with Devin and autoresearch every night for the past week or so. The prompt I’ve been using for is pretty simple:

`I want you to do autoresearch to improve {verifiable metric(s)}. Hill climb. You have a budget of ${budget} and {time limit}. Use sub-devins to parallelize work. Track your plans and progress as you go in the filesystem. Work methodically. Create abstractions if you need to to help you verify faster. Manage your own PRs/babysit code review and merge as you see fit until you get a candidate that passes gates you set. Boil the ocean. Believe in yourself. You got this. {+more confidence/hype statements}` 

After you have the setup you like, just make this into a skill and turn on automatic code review. With this prompt, Devin can run for hours autonomously. 

Funny enough, the “boil the ocean” and hype statements seem to yield better exploration behavior and make most models less likely to give up early or reward hack changes/ship incremental fallback stuff. Inspiration for this was @jarredsumner’s prompts during his Riemann work.

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
花旗10月5日发布的《全球股票季度展望：韧性还是自满？》核心其实是在回答一个很重要的问题：为什么在油价高位、全球重新进入加息周期、长端利率大幅上行、美国—伊朗冲突没有彻底解决、市场广度又明显恶化的情况下，全球股票仍然接近历史高点？
这是基本面真的比想象中强，还是市场已经对风险麻木？
花旗给出的答案：目前仍站在 “Resilience（韧性）” 一边。它实际上把未来半年全球股票继续上涨的条件压缩成了两个变量：盈利必须继续兑现，地缘和利率冲击不能进一步升级。

当然长债收益率上涨绝不是没有影响：影响主要落在传统行业、中小盘、房地产、消费等利率敏感资产。而 AI / 半导体 / 大型科技由于盈利增长足够强，靠“分子”增长抵消了“分母”折现率上升。
花旗的逻辑跟我之前推文逻辑很一致，

花期这份报告对当下美股投资三个意义：
1）AI交易目前没有结束。
因为驱动 AI 股票的东西正在从估值扩张
逐渐切换成EPS兑现；
2）收益率上涨为什么科技不跌、传统行业跌这个现象仍然可能持续；
3）未来真正能够让美股牛市发生趋势性逆转的变量，很可能不是第一次或者第二次加息，而是盈利revision开始转负。

花旗认为目前的市场韧性大体是真的，因为盈利增长足够强，过去一年甚至在股价上涨的同时把全球股市估值从19倍消化到了16倍；但市场已经进入一个对EPS兑现高度依赖的阶段，未来再靠估值扩张赚钱越来越困难。

只要盈利没有开始下修，这种分化本身还不能当作牛市结束信号。真正需要警惕的是 高利率从“经济强的结果”逐步变成“财政/通胀/term premium失控的结果”，与此同时AI盈利revision开始见顶。 这两个条件如果同时出现，才会把花旗的“韧性”真正推向“自满”。

之前10月1号对9月份有一个回复和10月展望 跟花旗的这期报告逻辑很类似： https://t.co/kpblUc6mco

text:
$CRCL 感觉是本轮最难拿住的标的之一 😭

因为它总是利空利好不对称：
利空新闻的大跌往往走趋势延续（11/12），而利多新闻的大涨特别容易回吐（延续只有 3/7）
导致你以为放量突破了，结果每次追高都被挂在山顶⛰️

而且 CRCL 的大波动几乎都挂在事件驱动上，财报、监管文本和竞争颠覆三类事件影响最大，利率、评级、小合作这类消息影响反而不咋影响 K 线

所以我们炒的时候，CRCL 利好别急着追，利空别急着抄

原因我觉得主要有几点：

1. 早期投资人太喜欢出货
CRCL 上市这一年，基本都在往下修估值，13G 文件里能看到早期股东一路在减持
股价在均线下面时，套牢的人多，空头也挤，利好一来先逼出空头回补，涨得又快又猛
站上均线以后，上方全是解套盘和获利盘，利好放出来的量，很大一块是有人借机出货

2. 利好往往只影响短期利润，利空更多打的是长期估值
利好多是兑现预期，比如财报超预期、牌照获批，改变的是一两个季度的数字；
利空如 OUSD、CLARITY 收益限制，改变的是长期分销成本假设

3. 合规叙事天花板被卡住
Circle 很长一段时间故事建立在「USDC 是合规美元稳定币的默认选项」之上。监管通过、牌照获批，属于故事里本来就有的部分，只能确认叙事天花板；但OUSD、银行联盟币、支付巨头自建平台，则直接挑战 Circle 在价值链中的位置

目前统计下来：

利空的影响大概能走 10 到 12 个交易日。利好大涨后，第 2 天基本就是顶，第 4 天开始往回吐

利好我觉得可以观察 50 日均线
涨之前在均线下方的，3 次都延续、已经站上均线的，3 次都回落

现在有点懂 wufan 老师了，这种反复折腾的票还是 buy & hold 最舒服。做技术驱动或者事件驱动都有种被反复玩弄的感觉 🤡 不知道大家怎么炒的？

text:
又一个 L2 公链 Abstract 今天宣布关闭了

跟 Blast 不一样的是，Abstract 没有选择发币割最后一波，再跟社区说「Sorry,  我们失败了」，而是直接关闭

跟 Blast 一样的是，Abstract 在主网上线的这一年多时间里，其实通过 L2 排序器等方式，有几百上千万美元收入 (不是利润) —— 这些钱不是由 VC 出资，而是由对 TGE 充满期待、害怕错过的撸毛用户们一起赞助的

Abstract 早期能得到这么多关注，因为它是由知名 NFT 系列 Pudgy Penguins 创始人推出 (通过收购 Frame)，要打造一个为品牌 IP、内容创作者的公链。这跟铁顺在应用 Blur 成功后做公链 Blast 类似，都带着一种路径依赖

因为有多年做 to C / 社区 / 内容产品的经验，我一直对 Abstract 要做的服务于社交 / 内容 / 品牌 IP 的「消费者链」，以及所有 SocialFi 方向的产品，都不看好。就像它的名字一样，很抽象。Abstract 创始人的公告里也直言，Abstract 并没有找到可持续的 PMF，在情理之中

接下来 1 年，更多没有可持续 PMF 和生态应用的公链，会加速出清；有限的流动性、用户会集中回归到 DeFi 和 RWA 的正轨上

在区块链行业的发展过程中，Web3 是一段弯路，Money 2.0 才是正途

text:
Andrew Huberman on why Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic are all going to become biotech companies.

"Dario came up through neuroscience. Sam, I've spoken to, is extremely smart about the neuroscience, as is Zuck.

The technologists who used to just engineer stuff, they're becoming neuroscientists...and I think most people don't realize that.

They will all tell you, 'Okay, here's the goal. The goal is to be able to read and write from your brain non-invasively.'

Even just for things like drive and motivation, a non-invasive device where you could literally crank up your level of motivation by stimulating the nucleus accumbens and related pathways while engaging in a particular learning task or in hard work, and then turning it off so that you can capture more energy.

That's coming, and those companies are all about that. That's what the real arms race of AI is about."

In a 30 minute talk, here is what Shayne Coplan said about POLY at Token2049

quoted_text:
Abstract is winding down.

Starting today, all of @IglooInc's focus will go towards taking Pudgy Penguins, Pudgy NFTs, and $PENGU to the next level.

When we acquired Frame in the summer of 2024, the vision was to build the blockchain for consumer crypto. Pudgy Penguins had shown us what it meant to reach the masses, and we believed we could bring that same approach to building a chain.

Abstract achieved a lot in a short period of time; we built the Portal and AGW, onboarded major global brands, amassed over 300 million transactions, and grew a vibrant onchain ecosystem. 

The journey became stifled by the lack of a DeFi ecosystem, insufficient liquidity, minimal institutional cross-over, and prohibitively high costs that impeded growth in winning areas.

Unknown to most, Igloo, Inc. had been funding Abstract over the last 18 months.

After losing tens of millions of dollars over two years, building consumer products, assembling an all-star team, onboarding some of the biggest brands in the world, and building a community of millions, we still had not found product-market fit.

In combination with the market's reduced appetite for what we had built and not being able to find a scalable path forward, we could no longer justify taking from the Pudgy Penguins business.

Igloo, Inc. has always been a community-first company. Even after losing 8 figures, we could have launched a token or pursued an ICO.

Ultimately we decided against this. A token only works if there is something driving demand to it, and launching a token that we don’t have conviction in would have been a disservice to our community.

The entire team at Abstract has worked tirelessly with a tremendous amount of passion to make the consumer crypto vision come true. I cannot fault a single one of them for this outcome.

To the Abstract community, I want to thank all of you for sticking by our side on this long journey and for continuing to champion us. You supported us through all of the ups and downs, and I wish the result could have been different.

There will be many that will find satisfaction in seeing this shut down, and that is fine. I take a great amount of pride in having the ambition to venture into the chain business, notoriously one of the most difficult to make work, and the only regret I have is not being able to celebrate a win alongside the Abstract community.

As we wind down Abstract, our full focus shifts to making Pudgy Penguins into the global & cultural phenomenon I know it can become. 

Return to Pudgy Penguins.

他向Abstract社区及团队表示感谢，并称接下来将全力推动Pudgy Penguins成为全球性文化现象。

text:
The real fun starts when BlackRock realizes that BTC is, in fact, tokenized compute.

BTC proof of work tokens = transferable proof of compute expended in the past.

AI inference tokens = digital representation of compute to be consumed in the future.

So an AI can accumulate BTC representing past compute, then spend it to purchase future compute.

Past compute becomes future AI agency.

Which means AI agency is constrained by compute costs at both ends of this stack.

On one end, there must be enough inference compute available in GPUs and AI chips to execute the action.

On the other, there must be enough BTC available to pay for that compute and everything else the AI needs to act.

BTC can serve as that stockpile. It is the geopolitically neutral asset and network for that exact task.

The business world already understands the first constraint. AI chips are massively oversubscribed because everyone understands that access to inference compute determines AI capability.

What almost nobody understands yet is the second constraint.

BTC is not understood as critical AI infrastructure yet because the market still categorizes it as "crypto" or "blockchain" tech thanks to years of tangential gambling shitcoinery 

It has not yet priced Bitcoin as infrastructure for metering, budgeting, and imposing costs on machine agency.

Available inference compute determines what an AI can do.

Available BTC will determine how much AI can afford to do.

And the latter is a lot more scarce and valuable than the former.

If AI security ultimately comes down to:
1. controlling access to compute, and
2. imposing costs on autonomous action,

then Bitcoiners are already sitting on the world's largest infrastructure for the second half of that equation.

The world understands why AI needs chips.

It has not yet figured out why AI may need Bitcoin.

When the market finally understands that distinction, the correction is going to be insane.

When we acquired Frame in the summer of 2024, the vision was to build the blockchain for consumer crypto. Pudgy Penguins had shown us what it meant to reach the masses, and we believed we could bring that same approach to building a chain.

Abstract achieved a lot in a short period of time; we built the Portal and AGW, onboarded major global brands, amassed over 300 million transactions, and grew a vibrant onchain ecosystem. 

The journey became stifled by the lack of a DeFi ecosystem, insufficient liquidity, minimal institutional cross-over, and prohibitively high costs that impeded growth in winning areas.

Unknown to most, Igloo, Inc. had been funding Abstract over the last 18 months.

After losing tens of millions of dollars over two years, building consumer products, assembling an all-star team, onboarding some of the biggest brands in the world, and building a community of millions, we still had not found product-market fit.

In combination with the market's reduced appetite for what we had built and not being able to find a scalable path forward, we could no longer justify taking from the Pudgy Penguins business.

Igloo, Inc. has always been a community-first company. Even after losing 8 figures, we could have launched a token or pursued an ICO.

Ultimately we decided against this. A token only works if there is something driving demand to it, and launching a token that we don’t have conviction in would have been a disservice to our community.

The entire team at Abstract has worked tirelessly with a tremendous amount of passion to make the consumer crypto vision come true. I cannot fault a single one of them for this outcome.

To the Abstract community, I want to thank all of you for sticking by our side on this long journey and for continuing to champion us. You supported us through all of the ups and downs, and I wish the result could have been different.

There will be many that will find satisfaction in seeing this shut down, and that is fine. I take a great amount of pride in having the ambition to venture into the chain business, notoriously one of the most difficult to make work, and the only regret I have is not being able to celebrate a win alongside the Abstract community.

As we wind down Abstract, our full focus shifts to making Pudgy Penguins into the global & cultural phenomenon I know it can become. 

Return to Pudgy Penguins.

It’s time for QUANTUM BITCOIN

You may have seen QTC go live on Near yesterday. Here is my thesis for why this is one of the most asymmetric tokens of the upcoming cycle.

I don’t trade. I buy coins that have massive asymmetric growth over a long period. 0x or 100x over 10 years.

Crypto has clearly bifurcated into two categories: crypto money (e.g. BTC, ETH, ZEC) and crypto equity (e.g. HYPE, LIT, MORPHO)

Both are good, but the former category is one I’d describe as “irresponsible to not be exposed to”

We need moneys with stable monetary supply outside of the fiat and physical commodity systems. These moneys should compete with each other to approximate the platonic ideal:
- univerally accepted
- auditable
- scarce
- private
- secure
- sustainability

None are yet perfect. Quantus has unique advantages that give it massive upside at this point in time.

1. It is already quantum proof, not just quantum recoverable 
2. Every single transaction could plausibly be to a private address, while appearing public. This is a stronger version of the best of both worlds ZEC has
3. It takes a small % fee on the order of bps in the privacy pool to re-up the security budget. With enough volume it can achieve “Monetary Escape Velocity” and never encounter a security budget issue.

There are only two downsides here:
1. it is a new chain, not yet lindy and widely integrated 
2. similarly its price and liquidity are not at the scale to support the highest levels of store of value

If you believe these obstacles can be overcome, it is very worth keeping a close eye on QTC.

text:
今天突然发现自己被内测到了的桌面端的小微，简单用了下给大家一些反馈：

第一个，桌面端的小微和手机端居然是没打通的。
我之前在手机里的小微已经聊了很多东西，也有很多历史聊天记录，但是桌面端基本获取不到。
这个我觉得还挺奇怪的，你本身做的就是 Personal Agent，最值钱的不就是我跟你日积月累聊出来的这些 Context 吗？
结果我从手机换到电脑，你直接失忆了，那这个体验其实挺割裂的。

第二个倒是比较意外。
我不知道是不是错觉，但我感觉桌面端的小微，Agent 执行能力会比手机端好一些。
就是它真的去执行一些任务的时候，完成度、过程、整体 Agent 感都更强一点。
具体为什么我也不知道，可能桌面端单独做了一些优化，或者底层 Agent infra有更新。
这个我后面准备再多测几个任务看看。

然后第三个，也是我觉得小微一直以来最大的老问题。
哥们，你明明手里拿着可能是整个中国互联网最丰富的个人 Context，结果你看看你给我推的都是什么东西：
菠菜和豆腐一起吃会结石吗？
经常早起眼皮浮肿一般和哪些原因有关？
洗完澡皮肤总是发痒明显一般什么原因？

我嘞个豆啊，哥们。
我打开小微不是他妈来当十万个为什么用的，也不是来打开一本AI百科全书的。
这些问题我随便打开任何一个大模型都能问，我为什么要找你？

你真正应该做的是告诉我，今天有什么重要消息还没回，谁找了我好几次我没回复，哪个群里有和我相关的重要信息，我之前答应了谁什么事情还没做，最近有没有什么我可能遗漏掉的重要东西。

甚至再进一步，你应该直接帮我把这些东西整理出来。

比如告诉我，Max，这三个人你最好今天回一下；
这个事情你昨天答应了，但是还没做；
这个群里刚刚聊到一个和你有关的机会；这个人最近连续找了你几次，可能比较重要。
这个才是我打开 Personal Agent 真正想看到的东西。
你拿着我最丰富的 Context，然后让我问你菠菜和豆腐一起吃会不会结石.....哥们，你没事吧你？我真的有点绷不住.....

当然还有一些之前就有的老问题，比如现在很多设置不能调整，比如调model、prompt什么的，而且Agent 到底能干什么、不能干什么，用户自己也没什么配置空间。

但说真的，我到现在还是觉得小微特别可惜。

因为 Personal Agent 这个方向，最难的其实根本不是模型，最难的是 Context。
而小微偏偏拥有别人最难拿到的东西。微信聊天、联系人、群聊、公众号、文件、各种社交关系，这些东西如果真的能够被一个 Agent 理解和长期利用，它的上限其实非常高。
理论上，小微完全有机会和infra比 Meta、Manus、GPT-Dot 这些 Personal Agent 做得好很多。
别人还在想办法让用户主动把 Context 喂给 Agent，你这里 Context 都快从地上冒出来了。

你不要跟我说你处理不了。

你要是最后真处理不了，那我觉得可能也不是技术问题了。

要不咱认真找个靠谱的 Product Lead，把这件事重新想一遍。

再不行，咱也可以考虑考虑，从外面买个团队回来干这个事儿.....

text:
Glamsterdam 10 月 6 日 已在 Sepolia 测试网上激活。

按照惯例，以太坊升级路径是：Sepolia（开发者、应用、合约先测），之后是Hoodi（验证者和质押基础设施），最后是主网。

Hoodi还没正式排期，如果Sepolia 观察期内终局性、ePBS、区块级访问列表（BALs）和新 gas 计价都没有大问题，那么，顺利的前提下，Hoodi最快有可能10月下旬就安排上。

至于主网激活，得看Sepolia和Hoodi的测试情况，目前的目标大概是今年年底前后。

这次升级本身除了大幅提gaslimit扩容之外，还要把执行层 Amsterdam 和共识层 Gloas 绑在一起。核心是协议内的提议者-构建者分离（ePBS，EIP-7732）、区块级访问列表（EIP-7928，便于并行读状态和验证），以及把状态创建、状态访问的成本重新计价。
author: lanhubiji
quoted_text:
最近两天，英文社区不少人提到Glamsterdam 升级后，以太坊 L1 gas limit 将从当前的 60M 直接拉到 200M 下限的事情。

这意味着什么？

相当于 L1 执行容量 3 倍+，且后续还有进一步翻倍的预期。配合 ePBS、BAL优化、gas repricing 等技术，L1 吞吐量会大幅提升，在需求不突然大暴涨的情况下，L1 费用有可能长期保持在很低的水平，甚至让用户无感。

那么， 这对以太坊L2或其他高性能公链意味着什么？

首先是，以太坊 L1 费用逼近L2，甚至相差无几。
 当前 L1 普通转账费用已经很低（约 0.1-0.4 美元），升级后如果 gas 价格进一步压到 0.01-0.05 gwei 级别，很多简单交易直接在 L1 做就够了，不需要再去L2。一是，多了一层桥/ 提现成本，二是，还不如L1安全。
 L2 过去最核心的卖点之一——“比 L1 便宜太多”，会被大幅削弱。

其次， L2 的经济模型面临调整。

L2 本身也要把数据打包到 L1（data availability），L1 变便宜对 L2 是利好（rollup 成本下降），但同时 L1 本身变得“够用又便宜”，很多应用可能会直接选择 L1 部署（尤其 DeFi、NFT、游戏里不需要超高 TPS 的场景）。

这也是迫使L2进行升级，L2 要想维持竞争力，就必须在速度、自定义执行环境、特定应用优化（比如 zk 证明速度、账户抽象、perp专用链等）上拉开差距，而不是单纯靠“便宜”。

演化的趋势是，除了少数通用L2，如base和arbitrum之外，未来更多可能是应用链L2，如Lighter、ronin之类，这也会促使Polymarket选择走以太坊L2的路子。

短期看，以太坊L1看似少了很多费用收入；但长期看，这对以太坊的生态掌控力很有帮助，最终会转化为更多的费用收入。

最后， 对高性能 公链的压力增大很多。
 高性能链过去拿“ETH L1 又慢又贵”当靶子。现在 ETH L1 突然“又快又便宜 + 安全性最高 + 流动性最深 + 开发者生态最全”，高性能公链的差异化优势就被严重压缩。
 除非它们能在实际 TPS、最终性、开发者体验、资本效率上继续大幅领先，否则很多项目和用户可能会重新评估“是否值得离开以太坊生态”。

这会带来一种趋势，除了少数1-2个高性能公链，其他的高性能公链会逐渐成为以太坊生态的一部分，且越来越多的项目和用户会转向以太坊L1及L2。

这轮升级是以太坊“单链叙事”的一次回归：L1 本身先把容量搞起来，L2 在上面继续叠加。

对 L2 项目方来说：短期是利好（成本降低），中期是压力（必须证明自己比 L1 更有价值）。

对其他公链来说：竞争门槛又被拉高了。

quoted_text:
Ling 3.1 Flash makes large gains in intelligence over its predecessor, scoring 41 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with particular improvement in agentic capabilities

@AntLingAGI has released Ling 3.1 Flash, a reasoning model with 560B total parameters, 25B active parameters, and a 1M token context window. It scores 41 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3, up from 20 from Ling 3.0 Flash, which launched in August. Ling 3.1 Flash is expected to be open weights, with Ant Group releasing the weights soon.

Key results:

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash improves agentic capabilities over its predecessor. With a GDPval-AA v2 Elo of 1,622 and an AA-Briefcase Elo of 1,400, the model rivals peer models such as GLM-5.3-Flash, Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Max). Ling 3.1 Flash also shows notable gains on AutomationBench-AA (62%) and Terminal-Bench v4.0 (33%).

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash scores +2 on AA-Omniscience, a 22 point improvements from Ling 3.0 Flash (-18). Compared to its predecessor, its accuracy rate rose from 18% to 29% while the hallucination rate fell from 44% to 38% at a similar attempt rate (56% to 58%), demonstrating the gain comes primarily from knowing more, not abstaining more. For comparison, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Max) has a hallucination rate of 97%.

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash is a larger model than its predecessor, priced accordingly, but more token efficient. It has 560B total and 25B active parameters, up from 124B and 5.1B for Ling 3.0 Flash, and is priced at $0.30 / $0.90 per 1M input / output tokens, up from $0.075 / $0.22. It used 218M output tokens to run the Intelligence Index, 16% fewer than Ling 3.0 Flash (261M).

➤ Ling 3.1 Flash has a higher cost per task than some peers, but remains in the most attractive quadrant. Ling 3.1 Flash costs $0.99 per task, well above GLM-5.3-Flash ($0.42) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Max, $0.32) but below Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) at $1.24.

Additional model details:

text:
The tokenized stock story may look US-centric at first glance.

But Asia is already playing a much bigger role than it seems.

1. The demand is already here in Asia

Asia already has a massive base of crypto-native investors.

Binance bStocks is currently the second-largest tokenized stock platform by market cap, and both Binance and BNB Chain have particularly strong user bases across Asia.

The trading data makes this even clearer. 72% of bStocks trading volume happens onchain, and 92% of that onchain volume takes place outside US market hours.

Activity also picks up around the start of the Asian trading day.

Asia is not just a potential market for tokenized stocks. The demand is already there.

2. Asia itself is home to some of the most attractive assets for tokenization

The opportunity is not just about Asian investors buying US equities. Asia itself has some of the most globally relevant stocks.

Korea, China, Taiwan, and Japan sit at the center of semiconductors, memory, batteries, robotics, EVs, and advanced manufacturing.

As AI becomes more dependent on physical infrastructure, these industries are becoming even more important.

We are already seeing this demand move onchain.

SK Hynix has consistently been one of the most actively traded equities in perp markets, alongside names like Samsung Electronics and other Asian tech companies.

Tokenization can eventually bring much broader global access to these assets.

3. Asia has the regulatory infrastructure to make this real

One of the biggest challenges in tokenized equities is legal structure.

Many existing products rely on multiple jurisdictions for SPVs, issuance, custody, prospectus approval, and distribution.

ADGM offers a very different setup.

Within a single jurisdiction, companies can establish an SPV, structure a tokenized security, receive prospectus approval, offer it publicly, and potentially trade it on a regulated exchange.

That makes ADGM particularly attractive for equity tokenization. And this is not theoretical.

Binance bStocks and Coinbase Tokenized Stocks are already using ADGM's regulatory framework.

4. Regulation is moving across Asia, but each market will take a different path

There will probably never be one unified "Asian tokenized stock market."

Each jurisdiction is developing around its own capital market structure.

Korea is building a legal framework for security tokenization, with the new regime taking effect in 2027.

Hong Kong is opening regulated secondary markets for tokenized investment products.

Japan already has an established security token framework, although tokenized equity activity remains limited.

The UAE, through ADGM, is taking a more infrastructure-driven approach and is already attracting global platforms.

Different paths, but the direction is becoming increasingly clear.

5. Asia has almost all the ingredients needed for the next phase of tokenized stocks

- A large investor base.
- Crypto-native users.
- Globally important equities.
- Deep capital markets.
- Regulatory frameworks that are gradually becoming workable.

Asia is still easy to overlook when people talk about tokenized stocks.

But from trading activity and investor demand to underlying assets and regulatory infrastructure, the region is already having a much bigger impact than most people realize.

text:
Hot take: The vast majority of DeFi users are better off simply LPing into the most liquid venues and vaults.

Yield assets are concave assets: the downside needs to be priced before the upside. Yield accrues slowly, while losses can materialize quickly when liquidity disappears.

That forces you to ask not just what an asset yields or whether it can be looped, but how volatile and liquid it will be under stress. That is very hard to answer even for the most sophisticated participants.

author: 0x_Arcana
quoted_text:
This is probably a controversial take but I think we won't see a pure meme above 1 billion market cap this cycle.

The reason for that is that the market has matured and evolved. Trading memes has become a hyper optimized game that is just a wealth transfer from new participants to those who have the right tools.

Last cycle a normie could buy a viral tiktok meme, log off and hope for the best. This cycle we have a dozen launchpads on a dozen chains with a dozen launch settings. 

It is near impossible for a normie to navigate through all of this. Even if they managed to do so, there is a 90% chance another token with a slight difference tries to vamp. 

This isn't only bad for normies but also for the whole ecosystem. The liquidity is spread among 5 different tokens on the same narratives. A coin that would've went to 5 million now now splits that capital between 10 different coins that all top at 1 million.

People would rather take a shot at a 10x on a vamp than ride the original to a billion. This mindset forces all other participants to adapt or die.

Above a certain market cap there is no marginal buyer left for a coin with no fundamental value anymore. Degens already bought. Funds can't underwrite it. And whoever is still on the sidelines has 50 other coins competing for the capital.

Going forward I think the only tokens that can reach a billion are tech coins. Real innovation in AI or tech, plus a value accrual mechanism that creates an outside bid. Something buying the token that isn't just the next degen.

That outside bid is the key part. Revenue funded buybacks, burns tied to usage, a reserve that grows with volume. A buyer that shows up whether sentiment is good or bad. Pure memes don't have that.

AI is 100x more efficient than last cycle. I'm sure we will see a lot of innovation happening through crypto rails this cycle. 

RWA paired memes sit somewhere in between. They have meme distribution and community with a real asset or a real narrative beneath them.

The question here is whether that middle ground is enough to break through the ceiling pure memes keep hitting. I think it can be. The attention engine of a meme plus a reason to hold beyond attention is a combination we haven't seen run at scale yet.

In practice this means the ceilings on pure memes are lower than people price in. Take profits earlier on runners. Spend more time looking for coins with an outside bid.

Pure memes won't be the runners of this cycle.

text:
Ever wonder where a crypto lies in the evolutionary tree of money?

USD stablecoins are evolution’s favored child - the product of thousands of years of natural selection. And Bitcoin and ETH are the first new major currency families in 500 years.

I mapped all currencies in use today back to their ancestors (and traced some extinct lineages).

Nearly all descend from the first coin struck in Lydia ~630 BC.

~15 descend from India, through the rupee.

The Siamese tical and (rebooted) Cambodian riel each have a single descendant.

The US dollar - originally 371.25 grains of silver - hangs off a long, proud lineage 

Aside from Cambodia, BTC and ETH are the only currencies that start from nothing - no conversion, no peg, no metal, no commodities behind them.

To avoid survivorship bias, this tree also shows major families that died out: the Mesopotamian shekel, the Egyptian deben, Chinese cash, cowries, Aztec cacao, Ethiopian salt bars, Inca cloth and Yap's stone money.

DM for a better resolution picture or the bibliography

OpenAI just released 722 AI-written math papers. Here are the 4 biggest claims in plain English. None have been confirmed by outside mathematicians yet.

1/ Quasi-Riemann hypothesis. Zeta has no zeros with real part above 7/8. It's not the Riemann hypothesis (that needs 1/2), but nobody had ever cleared a fixed strip before. Has a Lean proof.
https://t.co/DnS7S8lFRY

2/ Unique Games Conjecture. The central open question on which problems computers can't even approximate well. A proof means the best known algorithms for problems like Max-Cut can't be beaten unless P = NP. Has a Lean proof.
https://t.co/T1gDeXGS0O

3/ Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. A special case of a Millennium Prize problem, about which topological features of a shape come from pieces defined by polynomial equations. No Lean proof yet.
https://t.co/a1TDLJQWER

4/ Free group factors. Open since the 1940s: are the operator algebras built from free groups on 2 and 3 generators the same? Claimed answer: yes, all of them are. Has a Lean proof.

text:
The real battleground for major blockchains will be native issuance, not simply tokenizing existing RWAs. 

Native issuance means a company or project, especially one in an emerging market, can be priced, syndicated and issued directly on-chain. Its shares can trade against stablecoins and become accessible to a global investor base, w/ potentially deeper liquidity and a dramatically lower cost of distribution. 

This is much more consequential than issuing token w/ unclear value accrual, or wrapping an already-liquid US equity onchain. Native issuance actually expands the investable universe.  

I believe Binance is unusually well positioned here: 

1) Binance has the largest pools of crypto-native capital in the world + mature exchange infrastructure. For an issuer, that compresses what would normally be separate underwriting, listing, custody, FX and investor-distribution functions into one pipeline.  
2) BNB Chain can become the issuance and ownership layer beneath that liquidity. The chain gives issuers a programmable venue for cap tables, settlement, (some) corporate actions,  collateralization and composability. The CEX is the liquidity engine; the chain is the capital-market infrastructure.  Whoever captures native issuance at scale does not just win the next decade. They get a credible shot at redefining how global capital markets are organized.

@binance @heyibinance @BNBCHAIN

i've been saying prediction markets need a regulator that actually understands event contracts. this is the closest we've gotten

coinbase now lets you trade btc, eth or sol up or down, anywhere from 15 minutes to daily

i think this is how most retail ends up trading. it's leverage for people who don't want to learn leverage, and if they like it more than perps, a lot of volume moves over

sui is going hard on trading agents and robinhood demoed agentic trading at their summit last week

i believe agents become real traders eventually, but i want to see one run a position through a bad month without blowing up first

all four point the same way. the products that win give people a better price, a new thing to trade, or a reason to stay

quoted_text:
Project Eleven Launches Strongpoint for Post-Quantum Custody with Zcash Foundation as Initial Development Partner

Zcash Foundation joins Project Eleven to shape institutional custody infrastructure for the post-quantum and AI era as more than $1 trillion in digital assets remain at risk of attack by sufficiently powerful quantum computers.

Project Eleven, the post-quantum security company for digital assets, today introduced Strongpoint, its flagship custody platform built for navigating the transition to post-quantum cryptography. @ZcashFoundation joins Project Eleven as an initial development partner, helping shape Strongpoint’s institutional custody architecture.

Strongpoint is designed to give institutions a consistent control layer for securing and managing digital assets as networks change the cryptographic standards underneath them. Rather than rebuilding key-management, transaction approval, and audit infrastructure for each new signature scheme or network migration, institutions can maintain a common set of security controls while the underlying cryptography evolves.

“Institutional digital asset custody was built for a world where the cryptography underneath it rarely changed,” said Alex Pruden, CEO of Project Eleven. “Quantum computing is upending that model. If every network adopts a different solution, institutions could be forced to rebuild their security infrastructure again and again. Strongpoint is built around crypto-agility, so the cryptography can change without the infrastructure changing with it.”

“Institutions holding shielded ZEC need custody infrastructure that respects Zcash’s privacy model today and can adapt as cryptographic standards change,” said Alex Bornstein, Executive Director of Zcash Foundation. “Project Eleven is building Strongpoint with the crypto-agility and technical foundation needed to support those requirements over time, helping strengthen custody infrastructure for the broader ecosystem.”

Zcash Foundation Joins as an Initial Development Partner

Zcash Foundation joins as an initial development partner for Strongpoint, bringing its expertise in privacy-preserving cryptography and protocol engineering to Strongpoint’s institutional custody architecture. Zcash’s privacy-preserving design introduces sophisticated key-management and transaction requirements, making it a valuable environment for developing custody infrastructure capable of supporting evolving cryptographic standards.
The collaboration will help inform how Strongpoint handles network-specific requirements while maintaining a consistent institutional control framework across assets and cryptographic schemes.

Post-Quantum Migrations Are Taking Different Paths

The digital asset industry’s post-quantum transition is becoming a coordination challenge. Among the networks represented by the 20 largest assets in CoinGecko’s Layer 1 (L1) category by market capitalization, Project Eleven found that only 10 have published a network-specific technical proposal, roadmap or implementation path for migrating transaction or account authentication to post-quantum cryptography.

Those approaches span at least six proposed post-quantum signature schemes and vary significantly in how they address account migration, key rotation and legacy-asset recovery. Even where technical roadmaps exist, operational readiness remains uneven, leaving institutions to navigate different standards and requirements across networks.

For institutions operating across multiple networks, that fragmentation means accommodating different cryptographic standards and migration requirements without losing a consistent security model. Strongpoint is designed to provide that common operating layer while allowing the cryptography beneath it to change independently.

Early Access and Deployment

Project Eleven targets production deployment in Q4 2026 and is working with a limited group of development partners ahead of general availability. Additional development partners and supported networks will be announced. Institutions interested in early access can request more information at https://t.co/Sl7ErXIJCx.

Founded in 2024 by Alex Pruden and Conor Deegan, Project Eleven raised a $20 million Series A led by Castle Island Ventures in January 2026, bringing its total funding to $26 million. The company recently acquired Riva Labs, a specialized engineering firm with deep expertise in post-quantum signatures, wallet infrastructure and blockchain cryptography, expanding Project Eleven’s in-house research and protocol-engineering capabilities.

Methodology: Project Eleven reviewed the 20 largest assets in CoinGecko’s Layer 1 (L1) category by market capitalization on September 25, 2026. A network was counted only where an official network organization, foundation, core development team or recognized protocol-improvement process had published a network-specific technical proposal, roadmap or implementation path for migrating transaction or account authentication to post-quantum cryptography. General research programs, statements of intent and post-quantum work that did not specify such a migration path were not counted. Draft technical proposals were included and do not imply network approval or adoption.

quoted_text:
Abstract is winding down.

Starting today, all of @IglooInc's focus will go towards taking Pudgy Penguins, Pudgy NFTs, and $PENGU to the next level.

When we acquired Frame in the summer of 2024, the vision was to build the blockchain for consumer crypto. Pudgy Penguins had shown us what it meant to reach the masses, and we believed we could bring that same approach to building a chain.

Abstract achieved a lot in a short period of time; we built the Portal and AGW, onboarded major global brands, amassed over 300 million transactions, and grew a vibrant onchain ecosystem. 

The journey became stifled by the lack of a DeFi ecosystem, insufficient liquidity, minimal institutional cross-over, and prohibitively high costs that impeded growth in winning areas.

Unknown to most, Igloo, Inc. had been funding Abstract over the last 18 months.

After losing tens of millions of dollars over two years, building consumer products, assembling an all-star team, onboarding some of the biggest brands in the world, and building a community of millions, we still had not found product-market fit.

In combination with the market's reduced appetite for what we had built and not being able to find a scalable path forward, we could no longer justify taking from the Pudgy Penguins business.

Igloo, Inc. has always been a community-first company. Even after losing 8 figures, we could have launched a token or pursued an ICO.

Ultimately we decided against this. A token only works if there is something driving demand to it, and launching a token that we don’t have conviction in would have been a disservice to our community.

The entire team at Abstract has worked tirelessly with a tremendous amount of passion to make the consumer crypto vision come true. I cannot fault a single one of them for this outcome.

To the Abstract community, I want to thank all of you for sticking by our side on this long journey and for continuing to champion us. You supported us through all of the ups and downs, and I wish the result could have been different.

There will be many that will find satisfaction in seeing this shut down, and that is fine. I take a great amount of pride in having the ambition to venture into the chain business, notoriously one of the most difficult to make work, and the only regret I have is not being able to celebrate a win alongside the Abstract community.

As we wind down Abstract, our full focus shifts to making Pudgy Penguins into the global & cultural phenomenon I know it can become. 

Return to Pudgy Penguins.

text:
矮胖企鹅母公司宣告关闭 Abstract Chain，L2 消费链梦碎？

以太坊 L2 Abstract Chain 宣布将于 2026 年 12 月 15 日 停止链上服务。母公司 Igloo 及 Pudgy Penguins CEO Luca Netz 表示，团队过去 18 个月为 Abstract 补贴了数千万美元，但由于缺乏 PMF（产品市场契合度），决定不再抽调资金维持运营，未来将集中全部精力回归 Pudgy Penguins、Pudgy NFTs 及 PENGU 的发展。  

📌 核心要点梳理：

1. 资产迁移：用户可通过 Migration Hub 或原生桥进行资产迁移（原生桥约需等待 3 小时），截止日期后未迁移资产将无法访问。  

2. 败因分析：尽管曾吸引迪士尼、红牛等品牌入驻并拥有 40 万用户，但由于 DeFi 生态匮乏、链上流动性不足、机构参与度低 以及高昂运营成本，专注于消费加密的单一公链模式难以为继。  

3. 拒绝发币：团队明确表示即便亏损达八位数，也不会通过发币或 ICO 来融资，因为无法证明市场对代币有持续需求。  

⚠️ 警惕冒充官方的虚假迁移钓鱼网站，请仅通过官方渠道核实链接！

text:
Agent 时代，SaaS 最先被拆掉的，可能就是订阅制。

一个挺有意思的公司 Monid 刚融了 770 万美元，做的事情可以简单理解成「Agent 工具界的 OpenRouter」。

现在你想让一个 Agent 真正干活，背后其实很麻烦。

查人可能要 Apollo，搜网页要 Exa，抓数据要 Apify，发邮件、打电话、生成视频又各是一套服务。开发者得一个个注册账号、申请 API Key、充钱，最后每个月养着十几个甚至几十个订阅。

Monid 想把这一层全部吃掉。

你只需要给 Agent 接一次 Monid，往里面充一个余额。之后 Agent 缺什么能力，可以自己在运行过程中搜索、比较和购买工具。

比如要找一个人的联系方式，它可以现场发现 Apollo、People Data Labs 等不同 API，看价格、速度和能力，然后自己选一个调用。

不用提前订阅。

调用一次，付一次钱。

创始人 Shengkun Ye 最新公布的数据是，目前已经可以通过一个连接访问 2,500 个 API，覆盖 leads、SEO、搜索、电商、股票数据、图片/视频/音乐/3D 生成，甚至 Agent 自己发邮件、打电话。

这个方向我觉得比「又一个 MCP 平台」有意思得多。

因为如果 Agent 真的开始独立完成越来越长的任务链，它迟早需要过去只有人类和公司才有的购买能力。

OpenRouter 解决的是 Agent 临时决定「我要用哪个模型」。

Monid 想解决的是 Agent 临时决定「我要买哪个工具」。

以后大量软件可能都不需要卖给人一个 $99/month 的 Dashboard 了。

把能力拆成 API，标个单价，站在那里等 Agent 自己来买。

text:
市场被7月惊吓之后，有点不太敢炒缺货 ie MLCC一直缺货涨，Murata/Taiyo也没大涨

As you known, Im not a fan of bottleneck trade 我也炒，但明白“可炒，不可投资”

相同部件纯靠涨价—就是周期股的定义。卡脖子三年，不代表股票能涨三年。相反，股价会在短期打满涨价缺货预期

一、在缺货预期出现后继续涨，你必须证明

1. 能进一步无序涨价
2. 或确定缺货周期更长
3. 产能可以“持续”显著提高，且能保持“持续”涨价（这本身就有矛盾—如果真可以就不是周期股了，是NV了）

即使3点中你认为有可能，跟买marginal benefit也太低

因为，会存在“变数”包括
——谣言谁谁又delay了—本质你没有“拿5年删IB”的信心（挑战）

——可能竞争与类似的rumors：投入研发、产能拼一个别人占领技术、产能高点的存量市场无异自杀。但很多零部件公司的绝对垄断过去就是建立在上述存量市场上的，当AI大需求浪潮席卷过来。后起之秀的试错成本就变得很低了—-看看CXMT

二、所以缺货trade最靠谱的是“先信”

买在无人问津处，等他缺货预期起来，连X都知道缺货了就跑。这样marginal benefit才值得

我不会跑在盈利最高，因为盈利周期和股价周期lag很大。更高赔率的是跑在预期落地。我承认上述1/2/3都很可能发生，但是鱼为有肥有瘦

三、切记是“炒”

与需求无关，别“炒”缺货还说需求，你都定义是瓶颈了

与盈利无关，缺货票盈利真爬坡就该跑了

要知道瓶颈是机会也是挑战

机会是让公司忽然莫名其妙赚居多钱；让本来要死的后发者，在提价能吃残羹剩饭也能活好、能站稳脚

挑战是因为你掐脖子，所有产业中优秀的人都会研究怎么“优化”使用你、有没有替代方案

周期大浪平息之后，必然一地鸡毛（所以没人敢拿5年）

四、“投资”什么

投资产品持续迭代

1. 由良率提高、产品迭代持续提高毛利的公司

2. 因为本身产品迭代在带动行业进步，供货商/客户设计是围绕你的R&D进步迭代的。由一圈公司形成生态，门槛不是自己而是产业

现在半导体中就一句话总结：你这个公司是不是在贡献token deflation，并且还能在这个过程中提毛利、提收入

这才是正向飞轮

quoted_text:
OpenAI just released 722 AI-written math papers. Here are the 4 biggest claims in plain English. None have been confirmed by outside mathematicians yet.

1/ Quasi-Riemann hypothesis. Zeta has no zeros with real part above 7/8. It's not the Riemann hypothesis (that needs 1/2), but nobody had ever cleared a fixed strip before. Has a Lean proof.
https://t.co/DnS7S8lFRY

2/ Unique Games Conjecture. The central open question on which problems computers can't even approximate well. A proof means the best known algorithms for problems like Max-Cut can't be beaten unless P = NP. Has a Lean proof.
https://t.co/T1gDeXGS0O

3/ Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties. A special case of a Millennium Prize problem, about which topological features of a shape come from pieces defined by polynomial equations. No Lean proof yet.
https://t.co/a1TDLJQWER

4/ Free group factors. Open since the 1940s: are the operator algebras built from free groups on 2 and 3 generators the same? Claimed answer: yes, all of them are. Has a Lean proof.
https://t.co/tuVAtYvMQg

a16z's Angela Strange sits down with @Valon's Andrew Wang and Linda Du to unpack what it takes to rebuild the infrastructure underneath a $13 trillion mortgage market that still relies heavily on systems designed before the internet.

Linda and Andrew explain why Valon chose the hardest path: becoming a regulated mortgage servicer, translating decades of federal and state regulation into software, and proving the platform on its own loans before selling it to the industry. That foundation made Valon roughly 3x as efficient as traditional servicing and created the system of record it is now using to bring AI into complex mortgage workflows.

They also discuss what AI makes possible on top of that infrastructure, from agents handling long-tail servicing tasks to voice interfaces and more personalized customer experiences. And they explain why deploying the technology into large regulated enterprises is ultimately as much a change-management challenge as a technical one.

text:
Most banks started on permissioned networks, and that did real work for hedging the risk and building capability. @motypes 's EthConnect 2026 keynote was about what comes after, because the architecture chosen at step one sets the cost of step three, and the wall on the way to a public network is almost always confidentiality.

Confidential is not anonymous. It is control over who sees what, when and how: the counterparty sees the trade, everyone else sees only a proof that it is valid, the operator sees nothing, and the regulator holds a disclosure key.

The same question ran through both panels. Good conversations with @Sharplink , @LidoFinance , @ETHGasOfficial , @Offchain , @zama , @axelar and @FourPillarsFP , and our thanks to @0xundefined_ for hosting.
